title: Great appliance! I have had
body: Great appliance! I have had this now for a month and have used almost daily since receiving and having quite a lot of fun with it. Although I am not able to comment about its ability to cook rice since I have other cookers for that. Additionally, I don??t want to worry about spices/flavor from previous meals carrying over to the rice. However a good cleaning and using the auto sterilization function does a good job of taking care of this anyway. The non coated pot is easy to use and a little soaking takes care of any stuck on food. It??s nice not to have to worry about babying non stick coating. I was concerned initially about the lack of a removable inner lid but this has not been an issue. Overall this is a really nicely made unit. There is a bit of a learning curve if you??re like me and not used to using a pressure cooker other than canning. Support documentation is adequate but as opposed to similar products there aren??t a lot of recipes out there. You just have to tinker with time/setting for the most part and it gets easier with more experience. Other than the USA website I have found some interesting recipes on cuckoo??s Brunei website, the ??utube??, and some other miscellaneous places that have been helpful. The upside has been more interesting and various meals with relatively minimal effort. I really look forward to using this in the summer as I live in the far north without air conditioning. There are a few days every year it can get really hot and it will be nice not to have to deal with the stove/oven.

author: Grand S.
title: Fantastic air purifier with great odor absorption
body:
Since the pandemic started, we have been cooking at least 5 times a week and really enjoy it but even though we have a strong range hood, it does not eliminate all the cooking smell. We have been using a small air purifier but it did not help much so we decided to give the Cuckoo 5-stage filtration air purifier a try and are so glad we did. 
 
 First of all, the unit is twice the size of our older airpurifier. It is so much nicer and even though it is a pretty big unit, it blend in with the home d??cor and looks very nice in the house. Setting it up was a breeze as all I needed to do was open the back, remove the gigantic filter from the plastic wrap and the unit was ready to go. 
 
 Now when it comes to performance, the difference with our old unit is really night and day. The airflow of the Cuckoo at the maximum setting is very strong. I do have to say that it is loud but I didn??t mind as it was able to get rid of the cooking smell in no time compared to our smaller air purifier. 
 
 All in all, we have been very pleased with our Cuckoo device and it goes without saying that it is getting a perfect rating from us.

body: I have been wanting to try one of these for so long. I have moderate to severe asthma and this has helped me so much with pollutants and fragrances that usually trigger my asthma. I have this on full power and I cannot even tell that it??s running. It??s amazing! Not only is it quiet, but it definitely works. I kind of burned dinner tonight. Not smoke up the house and set off the fire alarm burned, but you could definitely smell it. By the time we were all sitting at the table, you couldn??t smell a thing. As far as function and maintenance, I love that there are different settings (I usually use the auto setting so it powers up when it senses there is more in the air and powers to a lower setting when not as needed) and different run time settings as well. There are three filters that filter different pollutants. The outside filter can just be wiped or rinsed off. The other two need to be replaced, but last a fair amount of time before needing replacement. The manual tells you the estimated time frame based on being used in a smoked in environment, so I feel like it will last much longer if you don??t smoke or have a lot of pets. If you do, I think this can really handle it too!

body: The Cuckoo Electric Pressure Cooker is simple to use with several settings to choose from. Measuring the ingredients was easy with the level markings found inside the cooking pot. Plug in and select from the menu what setting you want to cook at, and start. The rice/quinoa made about 5 cups and cooked in about 15 minutes and came out perfectly fluffy and tender. The handles on the side of the pot make it easy to lift out without needing hot pads. Washing up was a breeze. Just put it on the top rack of the dishwasher and you are done. I look forward to making many meals using the Cuckoo Electric Pressure Cooker. author: Wendy
title: Cleaner air without the noise
body: The Cuckoo 5-stage filtration air purifier has been a great addition to my home and is just what was needed for cleaner, healthier air in my home. It's perfect for medium to large rooms, so it was ideal for me to place it in my bedroom to help filter out allergens, pet dander, and other airborne particles so that my overall sleep quality is improved. This air purifier is very quiet and won't disturb your sleep if used in a bedroom as it has a sleep mode that slows down the fan speed and dims the lights for a peaceful night's sleep. The 5-stage filtration system with UV-C light and fine dust sensor helps detect and eliminate tiny dust particles such as pet dander, allergens, odors, smoke, and more. The filter will need to be replaced every 3 to 6 months depending on usage. The initial setup and directions for setting up the air purifier were simple and easy to follow, and the unit was up and running within just a few minutes. This air purifier is much bigger than my old one, so it needed to be placed in a room that had plenty of space for it and plenty of space around it so that it can work properly. It has a nice modern look to it and fits in nicely with my bedroom and decor. I like that it's lightweight, easy to use, and simple to switch between modes. I prefer to mostly use auto mode so that it automatically detects the air quality and adjusts the fan as needed. Overall, this is a great air purifier which I feel is making a difference in the quality of the air in my home, but it would be nice if it were able to connect to my smartphone so that I could monitor the air quality while I'm away from home or make adjustments to settings via an app. I highly recommend this air purifier to everyone.

author: Tony K.
title: Great Value Rice Cooker
body:
This does not have any of the fancy bells-and-whistles of the more expensive CUCKOO models (e.g. induction-heating or pressure). It simply gets the job done, and it is a great value. It's easy to clean and the inside part of the top comes off so that you can wash it separately. It comes with a measuring cup, and the ratio of dry rice to water is 1:1. The size is compact and doesn't take too much counter space. 
 It takes about 40 minutes to cook 2 cups of white rice on the regular mode. There are several modes, but I have only used the White Rice cooking mode. 
 
 In summary, this is a no-frills rice-cooker that does a consistent job of making good rice! Excellent value.

author: Jooyoung
title: Excellent Rice Cooker
body:
I love this rice cooker! It cooks perfect rice every time (glutinous, mixed grain, brown, etc.) and works wonderfully as a steamer and pressure cooker for other dishes, such as steamed egg. The turbo setting is very helpful for when I??m in a rush too. Even if it??s not on turbo, it also cooks a lot faster than other rice cookers I??ve used. 
 
 It??s very easy to keep clean thanks to the Auto Clean feature. I was a bit on-the-fence at first because of the price but it is well worth it, given the ease of use and deliciousness of rice lol
 
 It took some time to understand the different modes but after reading the manual, it??s actually very simple!

author: D-Winders
title: Fluffy rice every time!!
body:
I have had cheap rice cookers as well as cooked rice on the stove for many years. I was honestly in the fence in spending so much for a rice cooker but I do not regret at all! It is one of the best purchases I??ve made! The rice is perfectly fluffy every time. It is super easy to use and to clean. It takes about 35 min to cook the rice in the setting I use, but there are other settings you can choose from. You can even customize it further if prefer but I have been sticking to the preset programs and it is working perfect for me. 
 I definitely recommend to everyone I know!!

author: Wayne T.
title: My first multi-cooker/pressure cooker - Loving it!
body:
This is my first multi-cooker (think "Instant Pot") but I've jumped into the craze with both feet since I got it on 11/22/2022, getting a glass lid, extra seals, silicone sling, 7" spring pan, etc. For months I used it more than any other cooking medium. I've made meals from a killer pot roast, Penne Bolognese, to steel-cut oatmeal and practically everything in between. One of the attractions for me was almost instant pinto beans. I've made refried beans from dried beans in less than an hour!
 
 My first unit apparently had a flaw in the temperature sensors because the release valve would constantly hiss once the cooker reached pressure but the replacement that Amazon sent has worked flawlessly.

title: Improved Quality of my life as a dog owner. Recommend it to small-medium size dog owners!
body:
I have Mini Bichon Frise, and after every walk, her legs and paws turn dirty. And her fur catches dirt very easily too and it??s very noticeable because she is a white dog. 
 It??s very hard for me to sit down every day trying to wash and dry her paws for 10 to 30 minutes after every walk. But this pet dry room simplified my work so much that I can confidently recommend it to other dog owners. It was a little expensive but I use it every day, so it??s definitely worth your money. 
 Noise level: This pet dry room is not too noisy when the door is closed, but you definitely can hear the sound if the door opens. 
 
 Air shower: I really like this feature air which gives a cool air blow to get rid of dirt and pollen from my dog??s furs after every walk. 
 
 Durability: I have been using it for 7-8months now, but I haven??t had any issues.
 
 Will your dog like this?: It took my dog couple of days to get used to it. There is a training instruction on Youtube so definitely watch it first and follow the training instructions to get your dog used to it first. You know the first impression is important so don??t rush!
 
 Size: my dog is 9.5lb and a little short on her. It??s spacious, but a little short. I tried using it with two mini bichon frise (12lb and 9.5lb) and they fit. (If it was a little taller, it could??ve been better, to be honest.) If you have a larger dog, I would not recommend this product. 
 
 Temperature: When you use Dry mode, the temperature goes up slowly, so during the winter time, i would recommend turning it on 1min before putting your dog (temp might be little cold in the beginning. I saw my dog shivering a little bit for few seconds)

author: Christina A.
title: Powerful and Versatile Product
body:
We have had our 360 Air Circulator for about a month now, and we are loving it so much! Assembly was a breeze- literally just a few clicks and it's good to go. It's also just as easy to take apart if you prefer to have it at a height where you can place on a counter or tabletop as opposed to on the floor. 
 
 The air circulator is remote-powered, and it is so convenient to be able to change the settings without having to walk up to the circulator itself. It has 4 wind modes & more to choose from, to make it perfectly customized to your comfort. Turbo mode is our favorite for a hot summer day as it's so powerful and gives great ventilation. We also love the 360 rotation for making sure that air is truly being circulated throughout a space. 
 
 Overall, there may be similar products on the market, but none that do everything that the Cuckoo 360 Air Circulator does and do it as well. This product is compact, but powerful. It's aesthetically pleasing, adjustable, and customizable. It has it all and I highly recommend it!

author: Hyewon
title: Game Changer!
body:
I recently had the pleasure of trying out the Cuckoo CRP-RT0609FB rice cooker, and I must say, it has truly revolutionized my cooking experience. This sleek and innovative appliance has proven to be an indispensable addition to my kitchen, consistently delivering perfectly cooked rice that is nothing short of a delight.
 
 From the moment I unboxed the Cuckoo CRP-RT0609FB, I was impressed by its modern design and compact footprint. Its glossy black exterior exudes a sense of sophistication, fitting seamlessly into any kitchen decor. But it's not just about looks ?? this rice cooker packs a punch when it comes to performance.
 
 The standout feature of this rice cooker is its advanced Fuzzy Logic technology. This intelligent system takes the guesswork out of rice cooking, adjusting temperature and cooking time based on the type and quantity of rice you're preparing. Whether it's jasmine, basmati, sushi, or plain white rice, the Cuckoo CRP-RT0609FB consistently produces grains that are fluffy, tender, and perfectly cooked.
 
 One of the aspects that sets the CRP-RT0609FB apart is its versatility. In addition to its exceptional rice cooking capabilities, it offers a variety of cooking modes to cater to different preferences. The multi-cook feature allows you to prepare dishes like quinoa, oatmeal, and even soups with utmost ease. This has truly made it a one-stop solution for a wide range of meals in my household.
 
 Cleaning up after cooking can often be a hassle, but the Cuckoo CRP-RT0609FB has taken care of that concern as well. Its non-stick inner pot not only prevents rice from sticking but also makes cleaning up a breeze. The removable parts are dishwasher-friendly, making maintenance a simple task.
 
 The user-friendly interface and digital display make operating this rice cooker a walk in the park. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a novice cook, you'll appreciate the simplicity and clarity that the control panel offers. Additionally, the keep-warm function ensures that your rice stays at the ideal temperature until you're ready to serve, saving you the trouble of constantly checking on it.
 
 I can confidently say that the Cuckoo CRP-RT0609FB rice cooker has elevated my culinary endeavors to new heights. Its combination of smart technology, versatility, and ease of use make it an indispensable tool for anyone who appreciates perfectly cooked rice and hassle-free meal preparation. If you're in the market for a top-tier rice cooker that goes above and beyond, I wholeheartedly recommend giving the CRP-RT0609FB a place in your kitchen. It's not just a rice cooker ?? it's a culinary game changer.

author: JJ L.
title: Cuckoo Inner Pot replacement is great!
body:
I have a fairly old Cuckoo ricecooker that still works great! Model GHSR1009F, but the inner pot I had was too old and was getting crusty so I was contemplating what to do.
 
 At first, I remembered that there was a Home Shopping World (Korean store) in Buena Park where I drive by all the time. I called them asking if they had a replacement inner pot and they said they had to put in an order for it so I asked them to order it for me. So far so good, but then they instructed me to make sure to unscrew both handle bars of the existing inner pot so I can transfer them to the new innerpot when it arrives. WTF! Why?! They said when you order innerpot they dont come with handles. 
 
 I was in disbelief so I came to Cuckooamerica and called them to ask if in fact they dont come with handles. Then they assured me all replacements come with handles. 
 
 So, I canceled my order at Home Shopping world and ordered on this site CuckooAmerica.com. Plus, it was about $10-20 cheaper too!
 
 The order arrived very quickly and now I'm back to having a nice rice cooker come back to life making great rice all the time! 
 Cuckoo rice cookers are the best and a must have for anyone cooking rice!
style: Replacement Inner Pot for CRP-FHVR1008L, CRP-GHSR1009F (INNERPOT-CRP-FHVR/GH10)

title: Used for 1 year and 2 months - Loving it
body:

 Durability: no complaints at all, the build quality is just as good as the day I bought it. Also the rice cooker pot is very high quality and is still working very well.
 
 Rice quality: tastes amazing every time, no complaints here. There are many times where I have to make the rice and leave it in the keep warm mode for several hours, and when I do finally come home to take out the rice it tastes fresh as if it had just finished cooking.
 
 Cleaning: Very, very, very easy. I only have to do this once every two weeks and everything pops out very easily which makes this step a breeze.
 
 
 Would I recommend: Yes, absolutely I would recommend.

author: Russ
title: A worthwhile upgrade
body:
I always wondered why Asians would spend big bucks on a dedicated rice cooker. I had a mid-range cooker from another make, but wasn't entirely happy with it. Then I picked up a Cuckoo Multi-Cooker and was so impressed with it, I took the plunge on this unit.
 I'm happy I did. This thing is built like a tank but with the lines of a Lamborghini. Functionally, the rice has a better, more consistent texture (ditch the grocery store long-grain). And the keep warm function is actually usable!
 I haven't ventured beyond gluten and brown rice. I do wish the manual was a little more user-friendly. The recipe book that came with the multi-cooker was amazing and got me up to speed much more quickly, The user manual seems to have been written by Asians for Asians who are more familiar with mixed grains, soak times, etc. And the translation frankly could use a little work ( It says right on the cover that it's a pressure jar cooker (?)).
 That said, the unit looks good and works great, which is the main thing. I would recommend it and would purchase it again.

author: Choyeon K.
title: A culinary Masterpiece
body: The CUCKOO 6-Cup Twin Pressure Rice Cooker & Warmer is a culinary masterpiece transforming how you approach rice cooking. As an Asian who has eaten rice all his life, I am susceptible to the taste of rice. So I know that the taste of rice differs depending on the rice cooker. When I first came to the US, I bought an ordinary rice cooker and cooked rice, but the rice was dry and not sticky. So I looked for a Cuckoo, which I had been using since my grandmother, and finally, I was able to settle on this rice cooker. This rice cooker is responsible for my daily meals. It has various functions, but my favorite functions are the multigrain rice function and the steamer function. As you can see in the photo, I ate galbijjim with a rice cooker, and the taste was amazing. That function made the meat more tender. In addition, by washing the leftover using the automatic washing function after braised ribs, it was possible to cook rice without the smell of galbijjim. Moreover, it has stainless steel cover to use clean and preserve the taste and texture of my rice. I have recommended this rice cooker to my friends and left a review to let others know about this rice cooker's features. I hope you trust me and buy this rice cooker. I love it so much!

body: This is life changing! I made rice on the stove for years, then got a cheap rice cooker, you know the one, very basic, and essentially an on switch that flips to warm once done. Can you get good rice on the stove or steamer? Sure, but not without some effort and not every time. I've yet to have less than amazing rice, and besides washing the rice and putting the water in, doing nothing, this machine just takes care of you and your family! Cleaning up wise, super easy to clean, and everything that needs to be washed that comes in contact with the rice or steam comes apart easily. I can't underscore how much you need this in your life, put it in your cart, it is SO worth it!!

title: Great! And a tip
body: We really like this one! I??ve had this model for years, and if you are worried about the touch, not working, don??t worry about it. I have never had issues with the touch buttons, and everything is still very functional and rice comes out beautifully! A tip: do not wash your rice straight in the container. You will eventually scratch the container over time and this is a tip for any rice cooker that you might have. Instead, wash your rice in a separate bowl and then transfer it into the rice cooker container. That way, you can continue to use the machine for years in a pristine condition.

author: Mike L.
title: A superlative rice cooker
body:
The 16 minute turbo mode has all of the performance you really need out of a rice cooker. It's tolerant of differing water measurements. I've ended up using two examples of this model and the manufacturing is excellent. The quality and consistency of output is better than local restaurants (Seattle, WA) and I intend to use this one for life.
 
 Things to look out for:
 The steam release when completing a turbo rice cook is energetic - keep an eye out for wooden cupboards overhead.
 The manual is extraordinarily pedantic, and it may take a while to understand what mode you're looking for.
 Be sure to use the appropriate cup measure, matching the included cup. This amount will match the markings in the cooking vessel. Not all cups are equal.
 If you have the time, the slower mode will produce marginally better results.
 The english voice mode's intonation and vocabulary are konglish, with big unintended meme potential. They pronounce 'glutinous rice' the way Flanders says 'nothing at all'.
reply:
We're delighted to hear that you're happy with our product. 
 Our team works hard to ensure that every customer has a great experience, and it's always rewarding to hear when we've succeeded. Thank you for choosing us!

author: Melissa W.
title: My favorite kitchen appliance
body: Stainless steel is always a winner! It has been around a lot longer than any nonstick cookware. It's durable and takes a beating without compromise. I know it's not nonstick and isn't as convenient to clean, but I'll take that over nonstick anyday. Also, there are a few work-arounds with this pot. You can use parchment paper, stainless steel trivet, foil, separate stainless steel bowls. Since I bought my Cuckoo, it's been a non-stop favorite at home and it helps with preparing foods quickly and saves me a lot of time. I bought a stainless steel trivet and use it to steam sweet potatoes, reheat rice, and steam veggies and more. Sometimes, I add ingredients for porridge, and preset it to cook in several hours for dinner.

author: Melissa W.
title: Well designed and a beauty on your kitchen counter
body: I bought my Cuckoo Multi-cooker over 3 years ago and it is still going strong! The clever design allows me to use the appliance with ease. The parts are easy to remove and clean and it's quite intuitive. It requires some patience in exploring at first, but once you get it, it's really simple. The auto-steam release, attached lid, elegant design, and stainless steel inner pot option is what sold me on this product over other competitor brands that I've seen, which often I find out break within a year or so. Since buying this multi-cooker, I have bought 3 more for family members. It's a great mid-level option if you want to buy something that's going to last but isn't too expensive.

author: Wendy
title: Functional and sleek multi-cooker
body: My family and I love this rice cooker! I purchased this 5 years ago and it's still going strong. Definitely worth the investment and plays a cute song once cooking is completed. It's multi-functional and looks much nicer in the kitchen than most other appliances. We mainly use it for rice and have also tried a few different recipes such as Korean steamed ribs from the recipe book, easy one-pot meals, and the food turns out amazing every time. It's easy to clean, durable, and has a large capacity. However, there does appear to be a design flaw at the back--every time we cook rice, when we open the lid, the water will run down and spill out of the water catcher and onto the counter, getting the electrical cord wet. It doesn't affect the cooking function but does seem to be a hazard. I'm not sure if there's a way to prevent this but we take care to wipe up the pool of water each time behind the cooker each time we make rice. I also wish there were more Cuckoo recipes available on the website.

author: Travelfashiongir
title: Great investment for those who enjoy multiple type
body:
The Cuckoo 3-in-1 K-Cup Coffee Maker is a versatile brewing machine that appeals to coffee and tea lovers who appreciate convenience and variety. This coffee maker stands out for its ability to brew single cups using K-Cups, ground coffee, and tea, making it a great addition to any kitchen.

The user-friendly interface includes clear buttons for different brewing options, making it easy to switch between coffee grounds, k-cup, or tea. author: Duy
title: Conveniently
body:
The Cuckoo K-Cup Coffee Maker is a versatile and efficient coffee brewing machine designed for single-serve convenience. Known for its sleek design and reliable performance, this coffee maker stands out with its user-friendly interface and compact size, making it an ideal choice for small kitchens or offices.
 
 The Cuckoo K-Cup Coffee Maker offers compatibility with a variety of K-Cup pods, providing flexibility for users to enjoy different coffee flavors. Its fast brewing time ensures you can have a fresh cup of coffee in under two minutes, while its easy-to-clean components simplify maintenance. Some models also feature adjustable cup sizes and a strong brew option for those who prefer a bolder taste.
 
 However, like many single-serve machines, it produces disposable waste from K-Cups, which might be a concern for environmentally conscious users. Overall, Cuckoo delivers a reliable, stylish, and convenient coffee-making experience for individuals who value speed and simplicity.

author: Heidi N.
title: Good water heater/boiler, quite large, stainless steel interior
body:
I drink a lot of tea in the morning, and the convenience of having hot water available without waiting for it to boil is so helpful when I'm getting up out of bed. I've previously used a Zojirushi water heater/boiler, but don't love that the inside isn't non-toxic. This Cuckoo water heater/boiler has a stainless steel interior, which is non-toxic and super important for me. The water heater works just as expected and I keep it on the highest temp setting (185). It lets out steam slowly and is fairly quiet when it's heating up water. It's quite large and would be good for a family.
 Slight cons are: 
 -I wish the handle felt a little more secure (I haven't had any issues with it but it doesn't feel strong enough for me to carry it when it's full of water, so I have my other hand carry the base). The handle on my Zojirushi one feels more secure.
 -Once in a while I have to press the Unlock of Dispense buttons a couple times for it to work - the buttons are not as responsive as the ones on my Zojirushi one.
 -It might be too big for one person (it is for me) and takes up more space than I would like, however the stainless steel interior was a big sell for me and worth the space it takes up. If Cuckoo made one that was 3 liters that would be ideal for me.
 
 Overall I'm happy with this water heater/boiler, especially if you want one with a non-toxic interior and one with a larger capacity. This and the Tayama 13. 5cup device are the only ones I've found that are lined inside with stainless steel, however I couldn't find reviews for the Tayama one.

body: The instructions are pretty simple, with the up and down buttons to adjust the temperature and the power button to let it start up, and both of them being used together to customize which specific temperature you desire. Also comes with the FAHRENHEIT and CELSIUS button for those that prefer one or the other. The cleaning can be done by putting vinegar and water inside so it's not required to wash the outside at all. The box comes with the base with plug, the normal lid and tea lid, and the kettle itself. The kettle has light indicators so you can tell which temperature the water/liquid is getting, which might be helpful if you're busy doing other stuff. The only problem I had was the adjust temperature buttons wouldn't function but it is fixed now. I just had to wait for a few minutes since apparently it just needed to turn off.  The built-in tea infuser is a game-changer for anyone who loves loose-leaf tea. It's easy to use, fits perfectly in the kettle, and makes brewing tea super convenient without needing extra tools or cleanup.
 
 Another standout is the keep-warm feature. It keeps the water at just the right temperature for hours, which has been a lifesaver when I'm enjoying a slow morning or hosting friends for tea.
 
 This kettle has been a fantastic upgrade to my kitchen. Between the sleek design, practical features, and fun extras like the LED lights, it's a great choice for tea or coffee lovers, or anyone that needs to boil some water quickly. author: Sometime
title: Convenient and Compact: The Cuckoo Single Serve Co
body:
The Cuckoo Single Serve Coffee Maker is a compact and efficient option for coffee drinkers who value convenience and speed. Its sleek design is perfect for small kitchens or offices, and the user-friendly controls make brewing simple. Compatible with both ground coffee and K-cups, it offers versatility for different brewing preferences.
 Performance is solid, with the machine quickly heating water and brewing a decent cup of coffee in just a few minutes. While the flavor is smooth and consistent, it may not satisfy those who prefer a particularly rich or bold cup. The brew strength can be adjusted, but it's not as customizable as higher-end machines.
 One of the standout features is its ease of cleaning. Most parts, including the drip tray and water reservoir, are dishwasher-safe, which makes maintenance hassle-free. However, the water reservoir is on the smaller side, meaning frequent refills are required if you're brewing multiple cups in a row.
 Overall, the Cuckoo Single Serve Coffee Maker is an excellent choice for those who want a quick, convenient cup of coffee with minimal fuss. It may not have all the bells and whistles of more expensive machines, but its simplicity and reliability make it a solid pick for everyday use.

author: Branflakes
title: Amazing Rice Cooker!
body:
This new rice cooker is everything I could??ve wanted and more! I have never owned a rice cooker before and I??m wondering how I managed without one. Starting with a design of the product itself, this rice cooker has a sleek and modern design to it that would fit well in almost any kitchen. It has a nice broad base so it is sturdy. The first thing you??ll notice when you plug in the product and turn it on is that it talks to you. The default language is Korean, but the instructions in the manual that comes with it layout how to easily change the voice language between English, Korean and Chinese. The display and buttons are very bright and responsive to touch so a light press is all that??s needed. The instruction manual itself does an excellent job of walking you through step-by-step how to use each of the many features this product has.
 
 It is designed to be able to cook a wide variety of types of rice and has a number of settings to change how each of those types of rice is cooked. You can cook up to 3 cups of your chosen rice at once which allows it to accommodate cooking for more than one person. It also has a built-in feature that will keep the rice inside warm after it is finished being cooked without over cooking the rice.
 
 Cleaning this product is much simpler than I thought it would be. All of the parts that need to be cleaned to come out easily and don??t need much more than soap, water, and a soft sponge. The instructions also do an incredible job of taking you step-by-step through this cleaning process so that you clean everything you need to and don??t have to worry about accidentally messing with parts of the machine that you don??t need to. The components themselves are high-quality and made to last. Everything down to the locking mechanism feel smooth and secure so I always feel safe using it and never have to worry if something is on properly or not.
 
 Overall, this is an amazing rice cooker that has every feature you could want, is capable of producing a moderate amount of rice per cooking session, is easy to clean, and looks incredible. I would highly recommend this product to anybody who loves to cook.

author: Mel
title: Efficient and Stylish Kettle for Tea Lovers
body:
I recently received the Cuckoo Electric Kettle, and overall, I'm very impressed with its performance and thoughtful design. One of the standout features is how quickly it heats water to your desired temperature'perfect for tea lovers who need precision for different types of tea. The addition of a basket for loose tea is a game-changer, allowing you to steep tea directly in the kettle without needing separate equipment.
 
 The kettle also features color-changing lights that indicate the water's temperature as it heats up, which is not only functional but also adds a fun and modern touch. Once the water reaches the set temperature, the kettle beeps to let you know, so you're never left guessing when it's ready.
 
 While I'm happy with the kettle, there are a couple of minor downsides. Once your tea has finished steeping, there's no dedicated place to put the lid with the attached tea basket, which can be inconvenient. Additionally, the kettle doesn't have a feature to keep the tea warm after it's finished boiling, so you'll need to drink up or transfer it to another container fairly quickly.
 
 Despite these small drawbacks, the Cuckoo Electric Kettle is a fantastic product for anyone who enjoys tea or needs hot water quickly. Its stylish design and practical features make it a worthwhile addition to any kitchen.
style: Electric Glass Kettle with Tea Infuser (CK-G170BS)

author: Lei L.
title: Good item for the kitchen
body:
"After using this personal blender for several days, I'm excited to share my impressions on several important aspects.
 The initial presentation and packaging are impressive. The package is not heavy and contains 4 essential elements:
 ?? An efficient motor that is activated with a simple touch or button press, generating less noise than a traditional blender.
 ?? A large 500 ml measuring cup with 4 crossed blades, ideal for processing large pieces of food.
 ?? A second 300 ml measuring cup, perfect for personal portions, which require cutting food into smaller pieces.
 ?? A third 500 ml measuring cup without blades, designed to store preparations.
 The cups are easily attached to the motor thanks to the indicators on the base and cups, ensuring a secure connection. All components are removable for easy cleaning and disinfection.
 The material of the lids and cups is sturdy, thick plastic, with a matte finish. Although I'm not sure how it will look over time, it seems to be of good quality. I primarily used this blender to make healthy protein shakes, process food, and chop ingredients, and it performed well in all cases. The included instruction manual offers valuable tips for optimal product performance.
 Overall, I am very satisfied with this personal blender. It is convenient, easy to use and clean, making it ideal for today's fast-paced lifestyle. ??

title: Simple and easy to use!
body:
Thanks to Cuckoo for sending over their Classic Drip Coffee Maker (BD001B) in exchange for my honest thoughts.
 
 Here??s what stood out:
 
 Pros:
 Set it and forget it. The 24-hour timer is clutch??waking up to the smell of fresh coffee already brewing? A luxury I didn??t know I needed until now. You literally set the time you want and you'll have a fresh pot of coffee ready!
 
 Reusable filter. Less waste, less hassle. I love that it skips the paper filters entirely.
 
 Solid capacity. 10 cups is perfect for weekends when we have company or, let??s be honest, on weekdays when one cup won??t cut it.
 
 Clean look. Sleek black and stainless steel design fits right in on the counter without screaming for attention.
 
 The warming plate. Keeps the coffee warm without burning it, which feels like a small miracle.
 
 
 Cons:
 
 The water reservoir opening is a little narrow. Not a huge deal, but if you??re pouring fast, it might splash.
 
 The LED screen is great but the buttons can be a little sensitive??nothing major, just takes a second to get used to
 
 Final thoughts:
 This one hits the sweet spot between function and simplicity. If you're looking for a machine that just does its job well (and looks good doing it), this one delivers without overcomplicating things.

author: Cuam
title: Small size, big convenience (but a little plastick
body:
I wasn??t expecting much because it??s pretty compact, but it actually fits perfectly on my counter without crowding anything. That was already a win. The carafe is glass, which I love??it just feels cleaner and looks nicer than plastic. But the glass is on the thinner side, so I??ve been extra careful when taking it out or washing it.
 
 I set the timer before bed and wake up to hot coffee ready to go, which seriously saves me time in the morning. The filter is reusable, easy to clean, and big enough to make a full 10 cups. No waste, no hassle.
 
 Now for the downside??most of the inside parts like the filter holder and carafe lid are plastic. It still works fine, but it??s a little disappointing when everything else looks so nice from the outside.
 
 Still, it??s easy to use, doesn??t take up much space, and makes good coffee. Just don??t expect super high-end materials.

author: Derek V.
title: Disappointed
body:
- This model doesn't use physical touch buttons and relies on a passive touch. The majority of the time button presses go unregistered causing frustration with the product or incorrect selections.
 - The water collection tray at the back of the unit is too small. When using non pressure white rice mode, when cooking 3 cups of rice following the cooking instructions in the book, the water overflows and creates a mess on the counter and on some occasions will drip into the vents at the bottom and back of the unit.
 - When opening the lid, due to the button design, accidental button pressing occurs, resulting in the user having to open the lid differently.
 
 I miss my old CRP-P1009S but it sadly died and we wanted to downgrade as that was a larger unit.

title: The Korean Brand (CRP-BHSS0609F)
body:
My wife and I recently married and first time home owners didn??t realize how much the right kitchen appliances could become part of our daily rhythm until we started using the Cuckoo CRP-BHSS0609F rice cooker and our K-Cup coffee maker.
 
 The Cuckoo rice cooker has completely changed the way we enjoy meals at home. Rice comes out consistently perfect??fluffy, evenly cooked, and never dried out??whether we??re making short-grain rice for Korean dishes or prepping rice for the week. The build quality feels solid and premium, and the smart features make it effortless to use, even on busy days. It??s become one of those appliances we rely on without thinking twice, and it genuinely elevates our home-cooked meals.
 
 Pairing that with our K-Cup coffee maker makes mornings feel simple and comforting. With just a push of a button, we each get a fresh cup of coffee exactly when we want it??no measuring, no mess, no waiting. It??s perfect for our different schedules, and it??s turned our mornings into a small but meaningful routine we share before the day starts.
 
 Together, these two appliances bring a lot of joy and convenience into our home. From relaxed mornings with coffee to satisfying dinners centered around perfectly cooked rice, they??ve made everyday moments feel easier, cozier, and more enjoyable. While there wasn't much info on this newer model, I took a chance on it based on the overall brand reputation. This model is very affordable and simple to use. It's also a convenient size, both for the amount of counter space it takes up and the capacity being perfect for two people. The warm feature is very nice to have as well. We've only made white rice in it so far, but it came out great. It was fluffy and moist, and much better than Minute Rice. After cooking and sitting on warm for a little while, there was no burning on the bottom. There was only a slightly more cooked layer that easily fluffed into the rest of the rice. The steamer is a nice addition, and I'm looking forward to using it.

I ask her to verify whether they receive my return as cuckoo america website shows my return was never received, even though fedex tracking showed return was completed on Dec15 2025. author: kim
title: BAD Warranty
body:
In October 2025, I purchased two frying pans of different styles from Cuckoo. Unfortunately, the coating on one of the pans began to peel after one month of normal use, during which I did not use any metal utensils. I have been using both pans regularly, and while one remains in good condition, the other has developed a small chip in the coating.
 
 Upon contacting customer service regarding this issue, I received the following response: "Please kindly note that the frypan coating is considered a consumable component. Even within a short period of use, the coating may naturally experience wear depending on cooking conditions, heat exposure, or cleaning methods. For this reason, coating wear is not covered under our standard one-year warranty. We sincerely ask for your kind understanding regarding this policy. If the coating has significantly worn or peeled, we recommend replacing the frypan. However, if the wear is minimal and does not affect functionality, it is still safe to use. "
 
 I believe that the product has a factory defect rather than showing signs of misuse. This is particularly significant because I have previously had a positive opinion of Cuckoo products, including their rice cookers and air fryers. Potential buyers should carefully consider their options, as my experience indicates that the likelihood of being satisfied with this product is around 50%. I still have one frying pan that is working well.

Good: The stainless steel pot is great, we're trying to avoid non-stick coatings. Cooks 4 cups brown rice in 25 minutes!

Fancy has a more solid detachable lid which is more complex. . . but I must admit it eliminates one rubber seal, the lid seal is the only one, so I'll call it a slight advantage for cleaning the fancy model.

author: Sir G.
title: perfect rice!
body: i've been a long time Zojirushi user but decided to give Cuckoo a try, and it did not disappoint! we consume multigrain brown rice mostly. Z's setting left it really soft. as a family of four, cook time is important. Zoji took well over an hour; we cut it to 47 minutes using their "Quick" setting, but that gave the rice too firm a texture. PROS: multigrain turbo setting is perfect in both cooked rice texture and cook time (33 minutes). smaller footprint than my Zoji, but have to slide it from the wall to access the drip tray (see CONS). CONS: Cuckoo has a drip tray, a small one. it overflowed during an AutoClean session. Zoji design requires no drip tray. Cuckoo doesn't have a rice scoop holder; Zoji does. (i applied a stick-on holder. ) Cuckoo steam vent is LOUD (sounds like a pressure cooker) despite reviews claiming it's silent. as expected, stainless steel bowl takes effort to clean compared to non-stick. will use both AutoClean and SoakClean functions regularly. back-to-back cooking will be an issue, but fortunately these events are rare. despite more CONS, Cuckoo's perfect rice in shorter time trumps them

author: Amazon Customer
title: Consistent rice every time!
body: This is meant for stickier style rice by default, but tweaking the temperature and My Mode settings + using a little less water below the recommended marked lines on the pot gives me the exact rice I want every time (fluffy and separated grains). The timer countdown isn't available until the last 10 minutes (or 5 on Quick mode) so that's a bit disappointing, but not a major con. The overall construction looks and feels high quality, the pot has a decent thickness. The non-stick coating is very good functionality-wise, but it does get cosmetic "micro" scratches easily even though I've only ever used the rice spatula it comes with. You can't see them unless you hold it up to the light and after a month of everyday use, it hasn't affected the rice sticking at all nor the line markings so I don't foresee this becoming a problem. One thing of note, when you set the time for the Steam function, add 10 minutes to the amount of time you need because the timer starts automatically, not when the water comes to temperature like one would think! It otherwise steamed my sweet potatoes perfectly, I love the steam basket that comes with it. It's kept my rice warm perfectly, I have never had any browning or drying out on the bottom or edges which is impressive to me since my last rice cooker always dried the rice out on the bottom. The Auto Clean was actually really helpful when I made oatmeal, it softened everything up and made it very easy to sponge away, so definitely recommend. Overall, I love this rice cooker and will be updating on using the GABA mode and Stored Rice mode in the near future.

author: DLH
title: Cooks rice perfectly, easy to clean - but wish it had cooking time on the digital display
body:
Up until this point, I have been using a very old, very simple (and very small capacity) rice cooker. So this Cuckoo rice cooker is a huge step up in many ways. So far, I’ve used it to cook several types of rice - and in every instance and volume, the rice was cooked perfectly and evenly. I love how easy it is to use (with the water markings and the different settings for the different grains), and how easy it is to clean the non-stick inner pot. The controls are simple and pretty straightforward (haven’t used the manual functions yet). I was surprised that the display does not show a cooking time countdown - just shows a rotating circle after you press Start, until the last few minutes (then has a countdown). A full countdown would be really handy.
The other surprise for me was the size of the cooker. The product photos just show it from the front, so you don’t get an idea of the true size, which is bigger than it appears (7.75” high x 8.75” wide x 12” long). I imagine that is compact size for this capacity, but was a surprise compared to my little (low capacity) rice cooker.
Overall, this is a great rice cooker, especially for big volumes. A bit pricey for what it is.

author: T West
title: Expensive, but worth it
body: We eat quite a bit of rice in our household so we took a chance and upgraded to this 6 cup machine.  Of course, this can cook other things for you and is pretty versatile, but we've been using this for rice so far.  The controls are pretty intuitive, my wife (who is in charge of rice making duties) didn't need to consult the manual to operate.  Still, since there are a lot of options, I'd recommend keeping the manual handy.  We also like that we can leave this on the countertop as it very attractive, as far as appliances go.  Lastly, we like that you can cook your rice to different doneness with the touch of a button.  Thisbis a nice feature depending on the dish you're preparing.  A little hard to get past the price tag ($149.99) on this one, but it really is a fine machine.

author: Ray
title: Extremely high quality
body:
This entire rice cooker just exudes high quality. The inner pot is hefty, the design is a fresh take on the classic zojirushi design, and the rice comes out delicious and well-textured. It's super easy to clean as all the parts inside can be removed and cleaned. There is even a self-cleaning feature where you can put water in and have it steam the inside. This can both disinfect, and soften any residues from the rice so that you can easily rinse it out.

I only wish it had an "off" button, so that you didn't have to unplug it after each use. There is also quite a learning curve to using this rice cooker, since there are just way too many features. Definitely keep the manual on hand.

author: Mouse45
title: Easy and fast
body: This rice cooker has so many settings and options depending upon style of rice or oats and veggies. The ratio to rice and water is different than if you were cooking it on the stove so read the instructions carefully. Thankfully they are very detailed instructions. I found that this cooked a larger amount of rice faster than if I had used the stovetop. This cooker comes with a great rice spoon which was a nice bonus. The display does not count down time, which I wish it did, but it does have a quiet beep when it’s complete. It was very easy to clean too. I am not sure about dishwasher safeness as I do not own a dishwasher but when washing by hand cleanup was still easy. Takes about as much counter space as a small microwave. Would definitely recommend.

author: Dr Zelski
title: Gorgeous and practical.
body: I love this rice makers! The rice turns out perfectly every time. It's extremely easy to clean. Many of the harder to clean parts come out. The interior of the lid and the steam vent are both removable for easy cleaning. The outside is so smooth it's easily wiped down. It's not giant but holds plenty for a group. I am very pleased with this.

author: Diana Gil
title: Love it
body:
I absolutely love this rice cooker. Rice is one of my favorite foods, and I am very picky with it. I love making and eating rice. I have used a couple of rice cookers before, but I usually prefer to make it the old fashion way, because it usually tastes better that way. However, this rice cooker comes very close to making rice taste just like rice made the old fashioned way, except is much easier. Although it looks complicated at first, it's actually very easy to use, it also comes with easy to follow instructions. It has multiple settings to get the desired texture, and options for many other foods and rice types. This rice maker is excellent, it's good quality, easy to clean, and it comes with everything you need.

Overall, this rice cooker is better than expected, I absolutely love it and most definitely recommend it.

author: WSP
title: LOVE, LOVE, LOVE, THIS POT!
body:
I had been looking for quite a while. I wanted to update my old rice cooker's inner pot with one that had numbers-for water and rice- which I  could read (older one was black on black).  I was never able to simply replace the inner pot, so opted for a new cooker- this is it!  I like the low profile of this pot, the light color on the outer housing is nice- and I really like the matte finish-easy to wipe down. The clincher for me though, is the VERY READABLE-inner pot. It is black metal, with WHITE measurement guides, small (in comparison to my older cooker)-but is absolutely sufficient in the amount of rice it is able to cook. I measured the depth from outside the pot and it is 4.1/4" D  X  8"W. The pot is hefty, but can be held in one hand!  The cooking experience: It is quiet, low profile, easy to clean, outer timing display is easy to read, and, I can read the numbers and water ratios before starting the process.  The controls are intuitive- but there is an instruction booklet and it helps. This pot was so quiet, I wasn't sure it was working! Perfect outcome on my rice. After I cook rice, I am able to put the inner pot in the dishwasher. There are even some recipe suggestions with this pot.
I use a rice cooker often- mostly for Jasmine and or Basmati rice- but this cooker even has instructions and guidelines for Quinoa, Brown/GABA, rolled oats and other grains-all on the inner pot-very convenient. There is a steamer basket and rice paddle included too. Highly recommended!

author: YT
title: reliable and versatile rice cooker
body:
The CUCKOO Rice Cooker is a popular choice for home cooks who want a reliable and versatile rice cooker. It uses induction heating to cook rice evenly and consistently, and it has a variety of cooking functions to choose from, including white rice, brown rice, porridge, and steam.

Pros:
• Induction heating for even and consistent cooking
Variety of cooking functions, including white rice, brown rice, porridge, and steam

author: Chris Wilson
title: Easy to use, high capacity, limited recipe selection
body:
This is one of those "set it and forget it" style of devices that really makes cooking rice easy.  We have a much less expensive cooker with a manual type dial setting that we use exclusively for cooking persian rice (one of our favorites around here).  I have had to modify the persian rice recipe to fit the older cooker since it really only cooks a maximum of 2 cups uncooked rice.  This cooker has a much higher capacity so I can cook up to 6 cups of rice with it.  I found the only modification is to the down side.  The cooker has markings for water level based on the amount of rice you are cooking in the 2 -6 cup range.
What this means is that if you are cooking 1 cup of rice you'll have to measure the water using your own measuring cup vice the markings in the cooker.  For my test I only had 1.5 cups of brown rice so I had to do some guessing with the water level to cook it.  After cleaning the internal lid and pot and rinsing my rice I added water and rice to the cooker shut the lid and selected the "brown rice/gaba" selection and hit start.  I was expecting a time indicator to immediately come up on the display, so I was a little thrown off when it didn't.  The rotating cooking indicator stayed on until there was 10 minutes left in the cycle so I had to go by what the instruction manual said as far as cook time goes (72 minutes for brown rice).  Seems to me that the display should indicate overall cook time, but that doesn't happen until the end.  The brown rice turned on par with what I can achieve on the stovetop.  This was my first try so I expect that the quality will improve as I learn how to use this new gadget.  The advantages of this cooker are it's capacity and ease of use, there are a few user defined settings that allow you to modify the cook on the white rice/sushi setting, but if you want to cook something like persian rice you are in some uncharted territory and will have to do some experimentation with the timed cook (which I haven't tried myself).
A quick search for "persian rice" on the cuckooamerica.com website yield zero results, so I'll be in experimentation mode in the timed cook mode to get there.  To summarize, very easy to use, high capacity, easy to clean, with a decent number of selections....but no persian rice setting, expensive and a very limited recipe selection on the cuckooamerica.com website.

author: Alan Brinton
title: Confusing Instructions, had to improvise
body:
I experimented for a long time and experienced a lot of frustration. I'm making white Basmati rice. I finally figured out how to get fluffy rice with good separation between grains, just the way I want it. My procedure seems ridiculous, but it works.

For 1 cup Basmati white rice: I prewash my rice and then follow the indicator line for determining the mix of rice and water. I then press the glutinous rice setting. The time setting does not appear until the point at which steam stops appearing. Then I shut the Cuckoo off, pull the plug and immediately stir my rice and serve it.

It takes about 27 minutes for the rice to be fully cooked. This is the point at which the broken rectangle display is replaced by the number of minutes (10). At this point I immediately pop the top, stir the rice and take the pot out. I can set the timer on my phone or whatever for 25 minutes and then observe the display for the exact time.

So I'm getting perfect rice, very nice tasty Basmati. But I'm only cooking white Basmati, and I have to watch the pot. The timer is useless except to indicate that when it starts counting down (from 9 or 10), the rice is already done. I never use my Cuckoo, nor have I used any other rice maker, to keep my rice warm after it's cooked or reheat it.

author: T. McClure
title: Great Gadget for Small Household with rice eaters
body: I always wanted a rice cooker as I appreciate the perfect every time rice I get from my favorite Asian restaurant. Since they are expensive, I did my research. Buying  the Japanese brand z.. was recommended and to make sure the machine was made in Japan not China. I live alone and did not want to spent the $150 plus that brand's small cooker  costs.  The Cuckoo was also recommended. It is made in Korea. I purchased mine from the Amazon Warehouse for about $35 less than the current price of $99. I have used it  for a month now and I love it. I only cook one serving at a time which most rice cookers just can't handle. With the Cuckoo, rice never tasted so good. The keep warm feature holds the rice perfectly and never is the rice overcooked or dried out even after several hours. I have found it best to cook sprouted brown rice on the glutinous white rice cycle as the brown cycle makes it is too mushy. I cook white and brown rice. I want to try other grains but first I will look for the "how to" online. I am so glad I purchased this Cuckoo rice cooker. Try this one before you buy that pricey Z brand especially if you live alone or in a small household. And yes, the high end fuzzy logic rice cooker rice comes out way better than a pot on the stove top or those cheap "off/on" cookers you can get for $20 bucks.

If I make more rice, I can make enough rice to last two days.  It’s small and doesn’t take up much space. Because it’s smaller, it is also easy to wash and keep it clean. Now, I’m not sure of the difference but make sure you get the one made in “Korea”. I read and hear there is a sizable difference in quality.

author: Tom B
title: Very cute, makes great rice
body:
We have owned four computerized "fuzzy logic" rice cookers over the last 20 years -- Tiger, Zo, Panasonic (Japanese) and now the Cuckoo (Korean).

This is a beautiful design with a very small footprint. It holds 3 dry cups of rice, which makes 6 generous servings of cooked rice. Most people do not need a 6 cup, let alone a 10 cup rice cooker. Get the small one.

We mostly use it for 1 cup (2 servings) of Jasmine rice on the "Turbo" setting which takes about 20 minutes.
For Jasmine I go slightly below the 1 cup marking on the pot (slightly less water than indicated) and rice comes out perfect -- fluffy with nicely separated grains.

We also put frozen salmon and tilapia chunks on the rice after adding the water, and end up with perfectly steamed fish on perfectly cooked rice -- the Cuckoo just seems to know how to do the right thing.

I wish it didn’t have a non stick bowl but it is really hard to find those, especially in a small unit. This is a “small” rice cooker but you can still cook a large amount of rice. (3 cups of raw rice makes up into like nine cups of cooked rice, right?) It is much easier to store and move around than the 30+ year old rice cooker I finally parted with.  It’s easy to use. The directions are clear with some funny but understandable translation errors. One downside is that when you first unbox it, there is a weird chemical/plastic smell. I washed it well but it still had a weird smell so I made a small amount of rice in it and then threw it away, washed it again and the smell was gone. I used it enough that when it finally died, I figured I'd upgrade and started reading up on nicer models, the problem is, as a single person (who intends to stay that way), most nicer models are just too big for me. When I found this 3-cup model, I thought it would be just enough, so I took the plunge and dropped what is the most I've ever spent on a kitchen appliance.

The difference between a base model and something like this is like the difference between a bicycle and a car. Instead of just my rice, I can make full meals in this baby!

I have to admit, the directions are a bit tricky, they might have used Google Translate there. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the "auto steam cleaning system" because I can't find anything about it in the manual or online. Didn't break a tooth or anything, but dried up brown rice pieces felt like a piece of rock on my teeth.  I use half brown & half white rice.

My previous $30(?) rice cooker was 16 years old, but was still working fine.  I'd freeze most of cooked rice, and then microwave later.  Bought this small Cuckoo to avoid microwaving, but nope.  A lot of work to clean up different parts too.  Cuckoo has extra features, but nothing that I ever use.  At least didn't go for the $500 rice cooker. Minor quibble is the rice paddle which has no nubbies to keep the rice from sliding when serving....and the paddle holder is not big enough to use a different paddle.  But this is minor.
A big plus is that there is no pool of water nastily sitting in the rim....(a problem I've had over the years with other rice cookers especially with the Sanyo). This really does cook a lovely pot of rice.  One word of advice though...... I would definitely buy the insurance .  It's cheap enough and the latch seems to be precarious in closing..... author: Customer
title: This model is comparable to the average InstaPot, and made in China
body:
This particular model worked well in cooking rice.  However, it is a toned down version of the other Cuckoos. NOTE: The multi-cookers, especially this model, still produce less pressure than Cuckoo's top-tier pressure rice cookers.

This model is trying to appeal to the Western market and be a direct competitor to InstaPot with its feature set and cheaper price point.

Here are some of the major differences compared to the other models:
1) The pressure capacity. The other Cuckoo multi cookers boast a pressure capacity of 25 PSI or 178 kpa (the industry standard for pressure cookers, it seems). The rice cookers go even higher at 29 PSI or 200 kpa.  This model only goes up to 12 PSI or 80 kpa which is comparable to InstaPot (this makes it easier to adapt InstaPot recipes to this model).

2) On the other models, people were complaining about how cook times calculated the TOTAL time with the preheating time included. This model does not include the preheating time which is supposed to be more in line with InstaPot recipe directions.

3) Some of the cooking modes (beans, chili) on this model seem really geared towards the western market.

4) This model was manufactured in China and NOT South Korea like the other models so the materials and quality probably won't be as top-tier. However, the appliance seemed relatively heavy duty and has a very nice locking mechanism.

In summary, this multi-cooker model seems comparable to InstaPot and the sale price was quite attractive. So it is a good value for what it is and doesn't have as big of a learning curve.

author: RatherHonest
title: So far, it's great! Read this before use!
body:
I got this mainly to cook rice, I was a little worried at first because instruction say rice might be scorched lolol but i didn't need to.

First things first, do put the pressure weight on before cooking and definitely wait 5 minutes before turning it to release. I recommend using the plastic rice scooper to turn it from the side. I tried to flip it with a stick from above and the steam that shot out with the hot water almost got my hands lol

Secondly, it's 1 cup water per 1 cup dried rice. Use the cup provided. DO NOT use the finger trick. Im talking to all my asians. It will not work on modern rice cooker. U'll just end up with a lot of water overflowing lol
Pressure on low.
Timer to 20 minutes (doesn't matter how many cups you cook, but 6 is max)
It will automatically turn to keep warm if you cook rice.

How to cook white rice is on page 15-16 of the recipe book that comes with it. It used 4 cups in the example, I did 3, works like a charm. Rice is great. No sticking to the bottom at all.

DO wash the metal pot inside. With a littlr bit soap and a none scrub sponge, gently.

DO NOT wash anything else! It's spot clean only.

There is no off button. When you are done, unplug to turn off.

Everything is dial based, with select, cancel, start, and setting 4 buttons. If rotating knob selection isn't your thing, there might be a learning curve using it.

Make sure you remove the blue tape on the plastic cup behind the cooker.

do not press down on lid when you try to close it after u cook something. It won't close if u press down.

author: TTMD
title: Simplicity At Its Finest!
body:
I own several animals, and have been in need of an air purifier for a very long time. I was very fortunate to have come across this Cuckoo air purifier, as it has turned out to be exactly what I have needed all this time. It is truly hard to believe what a difference this air purifier has made. I use it in my living area which is quite a large room, and I now breathe easier, and perhaps best of all, lingering pet odors are now nonexistent.

This air purifier is very well constructed, and I quite like the design. The Hepa H13 filter is positioned at the base of the unit, and this air purifier essentially works by taking air in through the base of the unit, which is then passed through the filter and as a result clean purified air is vented through the top of the unit. The air purifier is powered by a separate power supply which plugs into the back of the unit. The included power supply is quite long, and affords the ability to position the air purifier quite far from the power outlet if desired. Setup was very easy, but be sure to remove the plastic around the included filter before powering on the unit.

This air purifier could not be more simple to operate. The control panel is conveniently located at the top, and offers several different functions. The default mode is automatic mode, and this mode utilizes a built in dust sensor to automatically adjust the fan speed of the air purifier according to the level of pollutants found within the air. Air quality is measured in real time, and is displayed using a color indicator where which the illuminated color corresponds with the current air quality. For example, the indicator will illuminate red when the air quality is found to be bad, orange when the air quality is found to be moderate, green when the air quality is found to be good, and blue when the air quality is found to be excellent. The settings are then automatically adjusted accordingly.

The second mode is turbo mode, and this mode essentially runs the fan at full speed in order to quickly capture and eliminate air pollutants. The third mode is sleep mode, and this mode will run the fan at the lowest speed setting so as not to disturb your sleep. The fan is surprisingly quiet, even at its highest speed. To change the filter, you simply remove the bottom cover by rotating it counterclockwise, lift the old filter out, replace with a new H13 hepa filter, reinstall the cover by rotating it clockwise, and finally press and hold the filter replacement button to reset the light.

Overall, I could not be more pleased with how this air purifier has worked for me. The air purifier is constructed very well, does an excellent job at removing contaminates from the air, and quite literally could not be more simple to use. The filters are affordable and easy to replace. This unit is built to last due in no small part to its simplicity, and I expect that it will serve me well for years to come. I would highly recommend this Cuckoo air purifier to you.

It's a simple and sleek design that will fit with most bright living rooms or bedrooms. And you can turn off the LED if you don't like it. The build quality is nice. It doesn't feel like cheap garbage plastic, and doesn't creak when applying pressure.

Personally, I don't use the timer. Instead I wish it was replaced with a schedule. So I could set it to turn on when I'm at work or sleeping, and turn off when home. Though, for the price point, it's not a big deal.

Replacement filters are easy to find despite what people say. You can find them on Amazon for $40 or on Cuckoo's own website under "Replacement Parts" for $50.

So if you want an air filter for a small to medium sized room, and don't want to spend a Fortune, look no further.

author: neelordeb
title: Works perfectly with homes that have sunlight levels to activate it.
body:
This review is for the CUCKOO Air Purifier with 5-Stage H13 True HEPA Filter for Large-Sized (470 sq. ft.) Rooms, delivered on time and in perfect condition from Amazon.

This Air Purifier works well when it works. It has an automatic sleep mode, when the daylight sensor shows it getting dark, it automatically goes into sleep mode, cutting off activity lights and going into a slower mode to allow for easier sleep.

The button to put it in sleep mode is absolutely sufficient to put this in sleep when needed, the Auto light sensor is nothing but problematic at best ..

My house is situated north to south (front to back) and as the sun tracks it does not actually shine through the windows, but indirectly lights the inside of my house. This sensor always is activated so the only option for me is to set to medium speed and let it run all the time in order to have this make a difference in my home - thus cancelling the auto, energy savings mode. This feature should not exist, or be set to actual dark situations - not activate when just dim. I am perfectly able to set the sleep mode manually.

author: Middle Path
title: Mixed review - filters great but has some issues
body:
UPDATE:
TL/DR: Filters great, but needs natural daylight to function as it should. Otherwise, it's in sleep mode, which the manual says you have to put it in, but mine goes to sleep mode when it's not bright enough. This means it only senses air quality and filters accordingly from about 7:30 am to 6 pm. Huge disappointment. Also, when the air is the worst quality like when I sear a steak and the whole place is cloudy with beef vapor, it doesn't turn on the TURBO mode and therefore doesn't make much of a dent in the vapor. I think it goes to medium or high. When I manually turn it to turbo it's great, but otherwise leaves a lot to be desired. Downgrading to 2 stars. I also stopped moving it into the bedroom to sleep because what's the point?

I did not look at its size prior to pressing the "order" button and it's about 5x larger than I anticipated! The photo appeared to me like another desktop model I have so I was shocked when the waist-high box showed up at the door of the temporary rental I'm in for another 6 weeks at most. When I pulled The Beast out, I thought at least it looks kinda pleasant, let's see how to make this thing filter.

PROS:
It's reduced allergic reaction over the last two days. Was having sneezing fits in the morning and lots of drippy nose, even a little minor nosebleed when I woke up a few days ago, adjusting to a new desert climate. Yesterday (after first night of use) I had ZERO allergies, didn't even use one tissue or sneeze. Today I've had a sneeze or two, needed to use 2 tissues so far. I've been moving it into the bedroom while I sleep, and back out into the main living area during the day and it's not hard to move around using the convenient handles.

CONS:
Firstly, I thought I received a broken unit. It was dusk while I first tried it out, and I noticed the air-quality light would turn off after a minute. Kept pushing the button, timing how long it stayed on, etc. I read the manual back and forth, it said when you put it on sleep mode the light goes off, which made me think it would be ON at all other times when you did not ask it to go to sleep. Next morning in the daylight the light detector stayed on. So I guess it sleeps automatically? I can't tell if it's detecting and changing speed of filtration accordingly during this lack-of-daylight-auto-sleep mode.

It also provides an extra (?) allergen filter, but there's nothing in the manual about how to use it. I didn't know if there's one already in use out of the box, or am I supposed to attach it? Is this a replacement filter? And if so, why are there instructions how to change or clean every other part of the filter and nothing in the manual about the allergen filter? Even the photo of the filters in the manual doesn't look anything like the gossamer sheet of allergen filter in a bag provided. There are instructions for how to replace the pre-filter, and how to replace the air purifying filter but NOTHING about the allergen filter other than it needs to be changed every 4 months. Would appreciate if they can post a video how to change it because it's unclear and I've spent a lot of time going back and forth through the manual unsuccessfully.

author: TT & The Bears & The Lion & The Witch & The Wardrobe
title: A very nice air purifier for larger rooms
body:
Recently I've been noticing an increasing amount of cigarette smoke seeping into my apartment from the neighbors. The air purifier really moves a good amount of air and purifies the room fairly effectively. While this air purifier has a 5-stage HEPA filter, some odor-causing particles are smaller than they could filter. The nice thing about this air purifier is that it has a fine particle sensor (smaller than 2.5) so it will adjust its pollution sensor much more quickly and accurately. I have an AQI sensor unit and so far the air purifier sensor seems to correspond very well with it.

Pros:
- This unit is not super heavy and it is easy to move it around to different locations.
- The filter unit can be cleaned with warm water so you don't have to constantly buy expensive HEPA filters every number of months.
- The air purifier is quiet at lower settings.
- The air purifier moves a lot of air through its filtration process allowing for quicker purification of a room when you need it to. I could literally feel a draft drawing in towards the air purifier when it is on the "turbo" setting.
- There is a sleep mode so that if you are easily bothered by the lights at night, it can operate discreetly.

Cons:
- The panel is a bit difficult to remove when you need to access the filter and clean the sensor. There are two panels that look the same and it was hard to distinguish which panel should be removed in the manual. I wish this was made a bit more clear with a better mechanism to remove the panel since this air purifier will need regular cleaning and maintenance.
- At "Turbo" mode, the air purifier is pretty loud but I feel like I would need to set it in this mode in very rare occasions.

So far this air purifier is working well and I would highly recommend it if you're looking to clear the room of second hand smoke smell from neighbors. It is important that you also seal any and all gaps that the cigarette smell can enter your space. This air purifier will not magically "clean" the air if someone is actively smoking in the room. It will definitely help to get rid of pollutants from second or third-hand smoke so that you are breathing cleaner air.

For example, I noticed that when I changed my bed sheets or put on some perfume from the master bathroom, the air purifier in my bedroom immediately detected the change and started working to filter out any dust and odors. It was quite impressive to see how sensitive it was to even the slightest changes in the air.
⠀
Overall, I am extremely satisfied with the Cuckoo air purifier and would highly recommend it to anyone who wants a high-quality air purifier that is both effective and efficient. It is definitely worth the investment and has made a noticeable difference in the air quality in my home.

author: mostlyharmlessx
title: Great indoor grill, shape/size allows more space to cook
body:
This device cooks fairly well as a grill, and is compact for the cooking area provided. We have a Ninja Foodi which overlaps a bit with this cooker, but has less space for cooking due to the round shape.

For straight indoor grilling, this is better; more space and easier to work with. I like the grilling accessory alot (pictured), very nice and not too hard to clean. The interior cookpot cleans out pretty easily, there's a nice non-stick surface there. The controls are not hard to learn, just keep the instructions handy the first time or two. There's a recipe book included that gives instructions for cooking using each of it's functions.

The grilling works well, meat came out pretty similar to cooking on a gas grill. The size is great, you can cook for 2 at once pretty easily, or 4 if the portions are smaller. The grill pan is lifted off enough to allow extra juices to run off, good design and function all around. I did not try baking yet, but it has several recipes that show you how and looks like it'll work well.

Construction overall is pretty solid, and the buttons are easy to use. This unit has both touch-controls and knobs, and both work well. The unit itself, the inner pan, and grill grate all look impressive and well-made. The mesh basket for air frying looks a little flimsy and might be hard to clean, but I can't speak to that yet. However, it'll provide plenty of space for french fries or tater tots.

Heating and cooking is pretty quick, much quicker than our big oven. This is a great appliance for one or two people, you can cook quite a few different items and have plenty of food with leftovers. It does what our oven can do but quicker, and cleanup is not bad. I normally grill outside and cook more meat at once, but if you want to grill inside or do smaller portions, this is actually very decent. Like our Ninja Foodi, this isn't a small appliance, so you'll need either a countertop or cabinet to put it in when not in use.

author: mr. opinionated
title: Perfect for 2-3 person household
body:
We have been countertop cooking for years.  We rarely ever turn our stove on.

We have a larger countertop convection oven however there are times when we are making two items for a meal that require different temperatures.  We would cook one and keep it warm while the other was cooking.  Not the greatest method.  With this to augment our other oven, meal prep will be much easier and faster.

We use countertop convection over a standard gas or electric stove as they do not heat up the house like the stoves do.  They also use less electricity than an electric stove.  We find they also cook faster and more evenly than an oven.

This oven is all that and a bit more.  It has a nice size.  The controls are clear and bright. It is fair easy to operate.  It comes with a great selection of accessories to include a rotating spit.  We will be trying that feature out over the weekend.

I had to try it out as soon as I could.  I cleaned the parts and then grabbed a bag of frozen onion rings.  The bag was just a bit more than the basket could hold, but I threw caution to the wind and piled the few remaining rings on top of the others.  The onion rings were fully cooked in the minimum recommended time.  They were piping hot and were crispy.

Other uses will be dehydrating foods and drying nontoxic clay projects.

I feel we will be very pleased with this oven.
