date: Reviewed in the United States on April 29, 2025
author: joseph
title: Decent Bread Maker, but Not Without Its Flaws
body: I bought the CUCKOO Bread Maker Machine because I wanted an easy and flexible way to make homemade bread without all the manual kneading and guesswork. After using it consistently for about a month, I feel it‚Äôs a decent machine that gets the job done most of the time, but there are enough small frustrations that I can only give it three stars overall.First, the positives: The CUCKOO bread maker has a sleek, modern design that looks good on the kitchen counter. It‚Äôs relatively compact compared to some older bread machines I‚Äôve owned, so it doesn‚Äôt dominate the entire space. The control panel is intuitive, with clearly labeled buttons and a nice digital display that makes selecting programs easy.The 15 menu options are a definite highlight. I appreciated the variety ‚Äî from basic white and whole wheat breads to dough, cake, and even jam. The ability to choose from three different crust colors (light, medium, and dark) is also a nice touch and gives a good amount of customization depending on your personal preferences. I found the medium crust setting generally gave the best balance between texture and flavor.The machine runs fairly quietly and has a decent non-stick bread pan that makes it easy to remove the finished loaf without a fight. Clean-up afterward is simple ‚Äî a quick wipe and rinse, and you‚Äôre done.However, despite these good features, the CUCKOO bread maker has a few significant drawbacks:1. Inconsistent Results:While it produces decent bread most of the time, it‚Äôs not particularly consistent. I followed the same recipe exactly on different days and got noticeably different results ‚Äî one loaf would rise beautifully, and another would come out dense and undercooked. It feels like the internal temperature control isn‚Äôt always spot-on, which can lead to unpredictable outcomes. For beginners or anyone who expects a ‚Äúset it and forget it‚Äù machine, this can be frustrating.2. Weak Kneading Power:The kneading function seems a little underpowered, especially with heavier doughs like whole wheat or doughs that require a lot of elasticity. It struggles with larger batches too. I noticed that sometimes the dough wasn‚Äôt fully incorporated and had to pause the machine, open the lid, and manually adjust or push the dough around to ensure even kneading.3. Limited Customization on Some Programs:Even though there are a lot of presets, you can‚Äôt always fine-tune the settings. For example, you can‚Äôt always adjust kneading or rising times individually, which would have been really helpful for adapting recipes or accounting for different flour types or humidity levels in the kitchen.4. The Manual Could Be Better:The included manual is basic and doesn‚Äôt explain some important things like troubleshooting uneven loaves or adjusting recipes. There‚Äôs no guidance on ingredient order, substitutions, or what to do if you live at a high altitude ‚Äî things that can really affect baking success. I had to rely on trial and error or look up tips online rather than being able to trust the manual alone.Summary:The CUCKOO Bread Maker Machine is a stylish and mostly capable kitchen tool that will definitely work for casual home bakers looking for fresh bread without too much effort. It offers a nice range of settings, looks good, and is easy to clean. However, due to the inconsistencies in performance, weak kneading on heavy doughs, and lack of customization flexibility, it falls short of being a truly outstanding machine.I still use it regularly and enjoy the bread it makes when it turns out well ‚Äî but I wouldn‚Äôt recommend it for serious bakers or anyone looking for absolutely foolproof results. Solid mid-tier bread maker if you catch it on sale, but don‚Äôt expect professional bakery-level results.Three stars.

author: Laurel S.
title: Good features for a mid-priced bread machine
body:
Well we needed a new bread machine, since one of our girl's has a gluten allergy our old bread maker went away.  We specifically ordered this one because it has a gluten free setting.

The Cuckoo bread maker was simple to use and the directions were clear and easy to follow. I made a gluten free loaf and used the GF setting - fun to have that option programmed in! I also think it’s nice that you can choose your preferred shade of golden for the crust- lots of ways to customize your breads. There is a nifty little gadget to pull the paddle out of the bottom of your loaf when it gets stuck in there. I never would have thought of that, but it was indeed needed. I took the bread to my Supper Club and got compliments.  I’ll definitely experiment with recipes, but for my first try, I was happy with the way it turned out.

*Note-I received this product through the Amazon Vine program  at a significantly reduced cost (I pay taxes on this item, so it is not totally free) in exchange for my honest review and opinion/experience with the item.
*After reviewing hundreds of items, this is how I generally rate the products I receive. I strive to be fair and honest, rather than overly enthusiastic just because I received it through Vine. I try to base my review on how I would feel about it if I had paid full price:
*5 Stars - I really love it!  It might even be better than described, or a better design or quality than similar items.  It is a good value, I would not hesitate to pay full price for the item for myself or for a gift and highly recommend it.
*4 Stars - I like it a lot, it is accurately described, and in comparison to similar items in the same price range seems to be a good value.  It might not be perfect or knock my socks off, but I would consider paying full price for the item for myself or for a gift.
*3 Stars - The product is as described, average quality compared to similar items, and priced fairly.  It might not be as well designed as similar items.  It probably has a lot of competition and there might be better choices, I would shop around but might purchase if the price was right.
*2 Stars - The product is well below my expectations for the price and quality compared to similar items, has significant issues or damage or poor quality control.  I would not spend my money on it and would recommend you seriously consider the flaws before doing so yourself.
*1 Star - This would be a very bad product (perhaps bad customer service on top of it).  This is a product I would throw away and not even donate, and would recommend you do not purchase.

author: Mary E. West
title: Makes perfect sized loafs for our small family
body:
This is our third bread maker, so we are familiar with the process.  We still have one other bread maker, but we ordered the Cuckoo because it makes the loaf sizes that fit our needs now and has the additional feature of the Automatic Fruit & Nut Dispenser.
We initially found the programming of the Cuckoo bread maker a little confusing and we still need to refer to the manual when we are trying different options.  It would have been nice if the manufacturer had included some recipes in the manual.
The bead that we have made in the Cuckoo has always come out beautifully, but a little denser than I prefer, but tweaking the recipe may fix that issue.  We recently tried making cinnamon raisin bread using the Automatic Fruit Dispenser and that didn't go as well as we had hoped.  For some reason only about 10 to 20% of the raisins ended up in the bread, the rest was either still in the dispenser or outside of the baking pan.  We did not flour the raisins as suggested in the manual, which might fix that issue.
While the bread loafs a larger than most standard size bread, this seems to be common with any bread maker we have had or reviewed.  While we are still learning how to use the Cuckoo Bread Maker, overall we are pleased with it.

author: Brett Combs
title: The Bread Maker That Delivers on Price, Quality and Convenience
body:
I recently ordered and received this bread maker, and it's been a fantastic addition to my kitchen.

What really stands out to me, beyond the great pricing, is the Crust Color Customization. Whether I'm in the mood for a lighter crust or something with a bit more crunch, I can dial it in perfectly. The option to choose between three different loaf sizes is also a nice touch, especially when I'm baking for just myself or a group.

The Automatic Fruit & Nut Dispenser is another feature I love—it’s incredibly convenient. No more hovering around the kitchen waiting for the perfect moment to add my mix-ins. It takes care of that for me, ensuring everything is evenly distributed during the kneading process.

One of the best parts? The Quick Bake Time. This machine shaves off up to 20 minutes compared to others I’ve used, which means fresh bread faster—what’s not to love? The bread comes out bakery-quality every time, thanks to the wide-shaped pan that ensures even heat distribution. The texture is spot on—soft inside with a perfectly crispy crust.

It also comes with all the essentials: a product manual, measuring cup & spoon, nonstick bread pan, paddle hook, and kneading paddle. Everything I need is right in the box, making it super easy to get started.

And to top it all off, the unit itself is an attractive stainless steel, which adds a sleek, modern look to my kitchen.

Overall, this bread maker is a fantastic find because of its price and its features.  If you are in the market for a great bread machine, give this one a try.

author: HonestReviews
title: Time Saver!
body:
UPDATE BELOW OLD REVIEW (14 OCT 2024)
___________________________________________
I generally make bread a couple times a week, which, unfortunately, can take hours out of your day each time.  Although it can be time-consuming, the results are worth it.  I don't eat grocery store bread anymore because it tastes - off, in a bad way - compared to a good homemade bread recipe.

Using this bread maker removes any remaining major complaints I have about making my own bread.  It literally takes a couple minutes to measure out the flour and put the rest of the ingredients in before you just hit a few buttons and walk away.  The bread comes out tasting great and perfectly baked, and more importantly, it's insanely easy to clean.  Just pull out the mixer blade from the bottom and clean everything out really quick and it's ready to be stored (after it cools down).

The only negative I can say about this is that because it's a machine, you can't expect the quality of the bread to be as good as if it's done by hand.  Kneading the dough by hand, such as in the case of sandwich bread, will produce a nice, spongy texture that is uniform and pleasantly chewy.

Using this machine will produce bread that still tastes great and has a nice crust, but the texture is more porous, and due to the mixer blade at the bottom during baking, you'll end up with an indentation at the bottom of the loaf.  It's a tradeoff, though.  If you want the machine to do the work, you'll sacrifice a little quality but get back a lot of time.

Besides that, the only other complaint that I have is that during the mixing process the machine can start knocking loudly for a few seconds.  It's not a big deal.  Startles the cat sometimes, but he's gotten used to it, so it's fine.

The build quality is great, the machine itself doesn't get too hot to touch, and more importantly, it doesn't noticeably heat up the house like the oven does.  I'm in Arizona so that's a big plus in the summer.

I hope this thing lasts a long time because I plan on using it for a long time.
___________________________________________
UPDATE:
After learning how to use it more, I've been able to achieve a nice, soft, pretty much non-porous sandwich bread in the machine that I don't feel is a big compromise in anyway.  Updated to five stars, mainly for the convenience.

Also, here's my recipe:
- Machine setting 1 (Basic, 3:10 hours)
- Light Crust setting
- 1 1/3 cup cold milk (to help keep rise down a little and get a better shape - warmer for more rise)
- 1/4 cup oil (vegetable, canola - your preference)
- 450g bread flour on top of oil/milk, put pit in middle for yeast (shallow enough to not get down to liquid)
- 1.5 tsp instant yeast in the flour pit
- 1.5 to 3 Tbsp sugar in one corner (taste preference, could affect rise)
- 1.5 tsp salt in another corner
- Bake

Try to avoid cutting into the bread for an hour so after it's done so it truly finishes the bake.  I fail at that every time personally, but still.  Top texture and flavor comes after it hits roughly room temperature.

Enjoy!

body:

The most challenging part is always the dough-making process, which I find tedious due to the time it consumes, even though I own a reliable Kitchenaid mixer that can handle large batches. However, when I only need to make a small amount, I prefer using an automatic bread maker like Cuckoo. Cuckoo is a known Korean brand name and reputable in kitchen products. I also own another Cuckoo rice cooker and they works great.

The menu is user-friendly, offering numerous preset options. My initial attempt at making dough was a triumph! By the time I wake up in the morning, the dough is perfectly risen and ready inside the bread maker. I simply shape it, wrap it around the sausage, let it rise again for 10-15 minutes, bake it for another 12 minutes, and voilà – freshly baked bread for the family in just 30 minutes.

title: This is my first experience with a bread machine‚Äîand I'm hooked
body: I've never made bread before‚Äîwith or without a bread machine‚Äîso I have a lot to learn. But the instructions for this compact little machine are clear and well written; so with a little study, I'm learning how to use it. And it is easy to use once you understand the simple programming.The owner's manual includes basic recipes that are easy to follow, and my first attempt was a small whole wheat loaf. I won't post a picture, because it's hilariously lumpy and misshapen. We all laughed at it‚Äîand then couldn't stop eating because it tasted so good. It was just like you'd want a rustic, whole-grain loaf to be. Crusty but not tough. Dense, but not heavy. It was a great first try and I learned from it (next time I'll add a little more liquid to the dough).This machine is simple, easy to assemble and use, and easy to clean. It's a nice size and doesn't hog too much space on my counter. The owner's manual is informative and well laid out. I'm looking forward to baking more and better loaves of bread with it. Recommended.

author: Dr. T
title: Versatile, works very well, makes good bread, but loaves are inconvenient size for sandwiches
body:
I was highly impressed by this bread machine and its variety of settings. The first loaf didn't have enough liquid in the dough (I used my handmade loaf recipe) so it came out very dense, but a few tweaks to the amounts of ingredients, and I am now getting lots of compliments on the bread I'm baking.

Any bread machine will take some getting used to, this one seemed to have a much shorter learning curve than I expected. Bread comes out with excellent crumb (that's the part of the loaf that isn't crust) and flavor. The crust seems a bit dark and thick, even on the lightest setting. But I like crusts anyway.

Two things that aren't my favorite: first, the "Home made" program allows customization of each step, but it doesn't retain the settings, so it has to be reprogrammed each time. This substantially detracts from its utility because it takes a while to program and the user interface takes some getting used to. Second, while the loaves are beautiful and perfect, they are the wrong size for sandwich slices. They make fabulously huge french toast but not so practical for lunches. This is a "feature" of many bread machines these days, not unique to the Cuckoo.

How I'm using this machine now, mostly, is the dough program, and then baking in a Pullman loaf pan. Maybe someday I will get a Bosch mixer for making large batches, but for single loaves this machine is perfect.

Four out of five stars because of the loaf geometry and the volatile memory on the custom program, but I would definitely order again.

title: Perfect brewer in both form and function
body:

I've brewed a cup a coffee nearly everyday from this unit for the past 8 months. I've tried several brands of K-cups and used freshly grounded coffee on occasions. For a majority of these brews, I was provided a consistent temperature and quality pour. The flavors have been spot on with not much to complain about.

This Cuckoo brewer has a super simple interface There are only couple of capitative buttons on the front display to control the volume of your pour and enable brew mode. Once you press start, it'll take less than 5 minutes for the water to heat and eventually pour your coffee. When brewing, its not very loud. Maybe a little quieter than an old school coffee maker.

I appreciate the design of this unit. Its dimensions fit really well in my coffee corner. The water container is easy to remove too for clearing and its super easy to fill it up.

Overall, I'm happy with this purchase and haven't came across any issues after 8 months. I've tried a few Krieg models before, and I find this Cuckoo coffee maker easier to use and just as good at brewing.

Clearly written the User Manual is easy to follow and operation is straightforward.

The water tank holds 40 ounces of water so refilling is required less frequently. The adapter that holds the loose ground coffee with the recommended quantity being 1 tablespoon coffee for each 5 ounces of water but as I’ve found with other similar adapters it is difficult to get a sufficiently strong cup of coffee. I like the idea of the grounds adaptor and have found using a dark espresso roast works best.

Dark roast coffee is helpful but finding a satisfactory quantity to strength of the finished cup will require trial and error adjusted to suit individual preferences. Cup size selections are 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14 ounce cups. I brewed both a prepared k-cup capsule along with coffee grounds in the other adapter and both worked well. The booklet includes cleaning instructions and troubleshooting. Good basic k-cup brewer.\

author: Luckyin
title: Compact and sleek, but slow
body:
I got this coffee maker knowing that Cuckoo is a highly reputed kitchen appliance brand (i.e. rice cookers) and was intrigued at their foray into coffee.  I'm a novice coffee snob, but can appreciate the compromise in convenience vs. quality in K-cups.  Here are my thoughts after initial use:

Pros:
- Compact & sleek: It is very lightweight and occupies very little countertop real estate. It looks very nice and would fit in any modern kitchen.
- It comes with two adapters: One for regular single-use K-cups, and a reusable K-cup adapter to add your own grinds.  This was important for me as I have a grinder and wanted to reduce waste from plastic K-cups.
- Very easy interface: Just one button to cycle through cup size (with highly customizable volumes of 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14oz), and another button to brew.  No fancy touch-screens that are failure-prone.
- Removable water basin in the back: This allows very easy filling as I can bring the basin directly to my sink and reattach it to the machine without having to lug an additional pitcher around to refill.
- Regular Kcups seem to taste pretty consistent with other Keurig machines

Cons:
- Time to brew: This was a big one for me, as one of the biggest advantages of Keurig machines nowadays are how quickly they can brew.  An 8oz cup takes 175 seconds (per the manual).  That's a 3-minute brew cycle, which is much longer than other machines I've used.  If you want a bigger cup, the 12oz and 14oz brews take 220 seconds and 245 seconds, respectively.  Granted, this device is smaller than others that I've used, so the heating element is likely not as efficient, but definitely worth noting.
- Resuable Kcup flavor is weak: I have my own burr grinder that I used to fill the resuable K-cup adapter to the max fill-line.  Despite the maximum addition of ~12g of fresh coffee grinds, the 10oz brew was still quite weak.  I may need to experiment with grind size and quantity, but overall the depth of flavor was lacking.  This does seem par for the course for reusable Kcups though, so I don't think this product is inferior to anything else on the market, but obviously cannot compare to a traditional drip coffee machine.  The metal mesh strainer also does let some grinds through, so I was left with a few grinds at the bottom of my cup.  Perhaps a single-use paper filter may fix this, but then adds to the complexity/waste as well.
- I can't fit my travel mug under the machine to brew directly into it: I need to brew into a regular mug, then pour into my travel mug.

All in all, this product is great for what it is: a sleek, low-footprint Kcup maker that is simple to use.  It's an elegant addition to any compact kitchen that seeks to conserve counter space.  However, the small size does compromise brew speed.  Great anyone looking for a basic cup of coffee.

date: Reviewed in the United States on March 31, 2025
author: I Candy
title: Programmable Timer For The Win
body: As someone with a busy schedule, the programmable timer feature is a lifesaver. I love being able to set it up the night before so I can wake up to freshly brewed coffee without having to wait. The 10-cup capacity is perfect for me, as I drink multiple cups during the day, and the machine does a great job keeping the coffee warm for a couple of hours. I do wish it had an automatic shut-off feature, but overall, I‚Äôm happy with how easy and quick it is to make coffee in the morning.

author: Jin.L
title: Attractive design
body: This coffee maker offers a straightforward user experience, with an operation so simple that I sometimes wish it featured more functions. Its sleek design complements my Breville Barista espresso machine nicely. While it comes with a washable mesh filter, I recommend using a disposable paper filter for easier cleaning.

author: JGil_Design
title: Great Value!!
body:
Picked this up to replace the coffee maker that my boyfriend uses everyday. It's got the ability for programming, and I thought that would give him the ability to sleep in a little bit more before he heads into work.

It's easy to use, feels sturdy and looks very sleek on the countertop. Overall it's a great coffee maker for the price.

author: Bryan
title: Clock has military time only; not disclosed in product page or instructions
body:
The clock on this unit only runs in military time - I.E., when it's 10:30 PM, the clock reads "22:30" instead of 10:30 PM. There is no way to change this, and this quirk seems to not be disclosed in the product description or the instructions. I like all of my clocks to run on 12-hour time, especially in the kitchen. I have a Keurig machine that can do this - not sure why this machine can't.

Additionally, there is some blue plastic hanging out of a crease between the control panel and the silver trim on the front of the unit that I couldn't pull away. It seems to be stuck to the inside of the unit somewhere and had escaped through the crease, but was anchored to whatever is behind the crease so there's no way to fully pull it away and it will always be visible as a blue interruption to an otherwise silver and black facade.

Cuckoo needs to think through these better, and do better QC on the final products, before they start distributing.

author: Pamela Armstrong
title: Coffee pot
body: My coffee pot broke recently so i was excited to find a new one to try. This is a 10 cup pot. The water tank in the bank has a clear and marked window to allow you to fill it up as needed to 2 cups up to 10 cups without adding more water than you need. It has a reusable filter so no need to spend more money on filters. It makes coffee fast  and tastes great.

author: ROBOTO
title: Decent Attractive Coffeemaker
body:
This coffeemaker from Cuckoo is a nice looking device and performs as expected.  Nothing complicated about the technology in this coffeemaker- water drips down and soaks thru coffee grounds and down to the glass carafe.
The water drip spout has six holes that water drips down from.
There is a "strong" brew option, which takes longer to brew a coffee- like maybe 2 times longer.
The stainless steel and black trim is nice looking.
The coffee this makes is about the same as any other cheap coffeemaker so I deducted 1 star because its too expensive at $69 on Amazon when you can buy a cheaper maker that performs the same.

author: RJD
title: Perfect Coffee Maker for My Son’s New Home
body:
I bought this coffee maker for my son’s new home, and it has been fantastic! The quality is excellent, with a sturdy build and a sleek design that looks great on the counter. It’s easy to use, and the programmable timer is a great feature for having coffee ready in the morning.

The two brew strength settings allow for customization, and the reusable mesh filter is a nice touch, saving money on paper filters — my sons favorite part. The glass pot pours smoothly without dripping. Overall, this is a well-made, reliable coffee maker—my son loves it, and I highly recommend it!

author: The Doctor
title: 10 cup coffee maker, nice style, works great!
body:
This is very similar to my Krups brewer that is old and starting to fall apart. I like the basket style coffee makers as this one is, more of a V shape than a bucket. I'm not a fan of the "permanent" filters, I like using the Melita #2 brown paper disposables. Seems to me that the paper filters provide a better brew but it's a personal choice - at least a filter comes with it.

This is a 10 cup coffee maker, works great for me as I only need to make 6 cups a day. Easy to pour in the water, lights work (as does the timer) and bottom line is that it makes a great cup of coffee! Highly recommend.

author: Keith P
title: Makes life easier and with stronger coffee if needed
body: A good-looking drip coffee maker that is simple to operate with thorough instructions. The coffee strength option works great, and the 8 points of contact with 3 rubber feet make this a stable machine. Simply looks good runs well and no need for filters. Super buy!

title: Makes a great cup
body: The coffee maker makes a great cup of coffee rivaling that of more expensive name brand pod makers. But it requires an extra step to get it there. I used freshly coarse ground coffee beans to bring help bring out the flavor and set the machine to the strong setting. This makes the coffee maker take a little longer, but it's well worth the wait. Overall a great buy for a great cup of coffee. Just use freshly grinded beans.

I‚Äôd prefer if the plastic top covering the glass carafe covered a larger portion of the top. There‚Äôs a wide open space for the coffee to lose heat more quickly. Also, the current selling price at $70 puts this in cuisinart territory and I‚Äôd go with a cuisinart over this but if this were $55 or less I‚Äôd give this 5 stars.

author: Sparky
title: Makes a great cup of coffee
body:
I know the Cuckoo brand best from their excellent line of very durable rice makers, so I jumped at the chance to try out their coffee maker.

First impressions: It is a very clean modern design, black with brushed stainless-steel wrap-around accents, 10-Cup capacity and a permanent cone filter basket. It is slightly smaller than our old one, which is great because it fits much better under our upper cabinets. It has a clock, two brew cycles [regular and strong], and some programming options - it is all very simple [not gimmicky or complex]. Our first cup of coffee was delicious. My wife especially likes the carafe's handle - says it really fits her hand very well.

We are happy with our new Cuckoo coffee maker. We like its design - it has attractive clean lines and subtle character, plus it sits well on our worktop. And best of all, it makes a really nice cup of coffee!

author: HK
title: Experience Cooling Bliss: I Highly Recommend this fan
body:
I've been using this Fan, and it's proven to be a fantastic addition to my home. What stands out the most is its versatility. With 12 different speed settings, I can easily adjust the fan to suit my comfort needs, whether I want a gentle breeze or a stronger cooling effect.

The 360-degree oscillation feature is a game-changer. It ensures that the entire room benefits from the fan's cooling effect without the need for constant adjustment. What's even better is the fan's near-silent operation, even when running at its highest speed. This makes it perfect for use in quieter environments like bedrooms or offices.

The included remote control makes it incredibly convenient to switch between the four different modes: Normal, Natural, Sleep, and Smart. Each mode serves a specific purpose, and I find myself using them in various situations throughout the day.

The ability to adjust the fan's height is another practical feature, and with an impressive 80 feet of air circulation, it effectively cools down a substantial area.

Not to forget, the fan's sleek white design adds a touch of elegance to any room. It's a well-built, durable product that I can see lasting for a long time.

Overall, this fan has become a reliable and versatile cooling solution for me. It combines performance with ease of use, making it suitable for any home or office space. I highly recommend it to anyone in search of a quality standing fan that delivers both functionality and convenience.

title: Good Budget Alternative To Pricier Name Brand Version
body: I have the Shark version of this fan and this one really compares favorably to it. Battery life is great and it's light and compact but still puts out a decent amount of air. body: The product is of good quality and performs well both indoors and outdoors. Its cordless design allows for convenient use near the pool or at the beach. It is also lightweight, making it easy to handle. While it would be an added bonus to include a water spray option, it still functions very well overall.

author: Mr reviewer
title: 10 stars
body:
This is a portable folding air wonder has exceeded all my expectations. Its cordless and portable design means you can take it anywhere without any hassle.
I love the 12 speeds, the fan tilt adjustment when unfolded, the battery life, the remote control. This fan is great for those summer days when I don't want to rely on air conditioning.
The fan is very quiet, which makes it perfect for use while I sleep or work. It's also easy to fold and store, which saves me space.

author: Amazon Customer
title: Modern and functional
body:
Not necessarily a powerhouse in terms of wind speed, but its compact and portable design sets this fan apart from most. Its cordless operation creates an opportunity for convenience when outlets aren't available. It can run for about 30 hours on a single charge. You still have the option of plugging it into a standard outlet, too.

I take it with me outside to my patio where no outlets are accessible. That in itself is worth it. It's great for camping purposes, traveling, or for everyday household use. The swing feature on this fan is pretty cool also. The base rotates and moves the entire fan. It's very unique and modern in that sense.

There are 12 levels of wind speed. It lacks a little in this area. Even though there are 12 speeds, I can't feel much of a difference between some of them. Also, I would have assumed obtaining a stronger breeze with applying the top wind selection, but it is very average. I guess I've been a little spoiled with high velocity fans and how powerful they are. Regardless, this fan isn't bad, but its wind speed is equivalent to probably a box fan.

You can adjust the height of the fan to accommodate the space you're using it in. It makes a great bedside fan and comes equipped with a remote for full access to all of its functions. I like that it can be completely folded down and stored inside the included storage bag when not in use. It makes it easier for transporting and general storage.

body:

There are quite a few things that I like, which are:
- Ability to open and clean the fan
- Compact size
- Fan wind speed (fast) and low noise
- Remote control
- Portability
- Battery life

- Price

Aside from that, I like that it folds easily and the height is easily adjustable. I wish it went higher than 3 feet though. Quality is definitely good and I foresee it lasting a good amount of time if cared for. I also love the long battery life.

5/5!

author: PrettyFly
title: High Power Portable Fan!
body:
The Fan set includes a carry case, the fan unit, power cord, a remote, and instructions.

The fan has a manual toggle switch on the back.  Once turned on, the fan LED display shows, and you can start the fan.

The fan has a lot of features for it's portability - including oscillating fan movement, changing speeds, setting timers, and more.  The included remote is very handy, as it is magnetic and circular in shape.  This allows it to be magnetically attached to the front of the fan when not in use.

One of my favorite features of the fan is it's versatility.  It can remain folded down for compact use, or the back pole extended to make it a "floor fan".  The fan head can be tilted up and down as well, so you can adjust for the best comfort.

I am very happy with the fan speed/power - especially considering it is running on batteries.  The rechargeable feature would be great for camping or outdoor events - but I personally like that it can be moved around the house without the need for power cords.  Hot in the bathroom when getting ready?  Get the fan.  Kitchen hot while cooking?  Easy to grab the fan.

When not in use, everything folds up and fits in the included carry case.

Not something that I would remove a star for, but a couple of suggestions for the future:

- It would be nice if the fan came in other colors.  The fan would look great in black.
- It would be nice if you could charge the unit via USB-C instead of the barrel plug connector.  I can see myself loosing the plug, and USB C would be much easier to replace.

title: Versatile and Efficient, But Overpriced
body: The CUCKOO One-Touch Personal Blender and Food Mixer (CFM-D60W) is a sleek and efficient kitchen appliance that performs well for daily blending needs, but its price point is higher than comparable options on the market.Performance & Features (‚≠êÔ∏è‚≠êÔ∏è‚≠êÔ∏è‚≠êÔ∏è)This blender offers a powerful motor that easily handles smoothies, protein shakes, and soft ingredients like fruits and yogurt. The two different blade types are a nice touch, allowing for more versatility when blending different textures. The one-touch operation makes it incredibly easy to use, perfect for those who prefer a straightforward, no-fuss experience.Additionally, the two included containers are convenient for on-the-go use, and their compact design makes storage simple. The ETL certification adds an extra layer of safety assurance, which is always a plus.DrawbacksWhile the blender is certainly effective, the price is noticeably high compared to similar personal blenders that offer similar power and features. Some competing models come with additional accessories or larger capacity for a lower cost. Also, it struggles with harder ingredients like ice or frozen fruits unless cut into very small pieces, which limits its use for certain smoothie recipes.Final VerdictIf you're looking for a reliable and stylish personal blender that is easy to use and clean, this is a great option. However, the higher price may not justify the features, especially when more affordable alternatives exist with similar capabilities. If you're set on the CUCKOO brand and don't mind the premium cost, it‚Äôs a solid purchase‚Äîbut if budget is a concern, you might find better value elsewhere.

author: Debbie Lee Wesselmann
title: Leaks Too Easily
body:
This corded Cuckoo personal blender is more powerful than my cordless personal blenders, but that doesn't make it better.  The worst part is that it leaks too easy, and when it does, the liquid can drain into the motor.  The blade assembly screws into the bottom of the container, but even when I tightened it, frozen ingredients moved it just enough to leak.  To get it safely in place, you have to tighten it strongly, and that means it's then difficult to remove the base.

I would have given this personal blender four stars if not for the leaking, but that doesn't mean it is great otherwise.  Even the large container is smaller than my Ninja and Nutribullet.  Again, with frozen ingredients making a thick smoothie, it has issues.  When you remove the blade unit from the bottom, you'll get too much around the blade.  Due to the threads, you cannot drink comfortably out of it.  I had to use a thin silicone spatula to get my smoothie out from around the blades and from the container into a glass.  It did not fully blend my 1/2 frozen banana, but it did the frozen cherries along with the yogurt and almond milk.

You have to hold down the pulse button to blend.  That gives you some control, although I found even with non-frozen ingredients, that I had to stop and start a lot to get the ingredients to the bottom.

It does have good power for a personal blender, but that's because it plugs in, rather than working cordlessly. I really wanted to like this blender, particularly since I've heard good things about the Cuckoo brand, but I don't.

--Debbie Lee Wesselmann

author: Monks pepper
title: Good water boiler but didn’t last.
body:
Update: the Cuckoo died on Dec 2, 6 months after ordering. We gave it a workout, boiling a pot of water at least 10 times a day. The lights come on, the temperature setting looks like it’s working, the colored light comes on like it’s heating, but it doesn’t warm up. Reset the plug, played with the buttons—not much else you can do. It’s got power, just doesn’t work.

This is our third electric tea kettle in 9 years after using one in an Irish hotel where we loved it. The first one we bought lasted 7 years; the second lasted 2 years; now we’re into this Cuckoo for a month. It seems like a quality appliance but it is the costliest. The previous ones were simple pots that only boiled and automatically shut off. The Cuckoo has variable preset temperature settings with auto shut off and 3 beeps to let you know it’s finished. Others that we considered had individual buttons for each temperature but the Cuckoo has up and down buttons to select the temp — some may prefer the individual buttons.  I chose the Cuckoo because its handle shape keeps my hand down and away from the steam — our last one allowed your hand to ride up to the top and cook your hand. We’ve never bothered with the tea making features so I have no comment on its effectiveness. It’s not double-walled like some others but we don’t have little kids reaching up and touching it. The Cuckoo has a removable top for filling while our previous models were flip-ups. Capacity, boiling speed, and noise are all acceptable.

I can check on the heating cycle by glancing over at it to check the color of the lights.  I then have an idea when it will be time to drop the tea into the water.  When it is time, it alarms to tell you it's reached the temperature that you've set.
When you take the tea out it has a regular lid to replace the tea apparatus.  And finally, it will keep the tea warm to whatever temperature you set. So, easy to use, boil speed is 5 minutes.  Some noise but that helps you know without looking what's going on.  I love this teapot.  I have no idea how durable it is.  I've only had it 2 months.  But I hope they
keep making it.

title: Does not keep warm 48 hours. Keeps warm for 2
body: This is a nice kettle. It does what I want, and it does it quickly. The LED lights are a bit bright for my taste, but as it is behind me when I turn it on, it really isn‚Äôt an issue. The minor issue of the kettle itself I find is there is a metal lip inside, where glass meets the metal, causing a bit of a blockage for the water. You really need to tip it over as you pour when you get to the last of the water left if you want every last drop.The rod of the tea infuser I find to be a bit on the wobbly side. The basket and rod are both made of metal which is great. However both the infuser lid and regular lid, while made to look like metal, are plastic. Not thrilled that steam is going upwards onto the plastic, exposing it to heat, and then dripping back down into the water. I was trying to have less plastic exposure in my life.The real issue I have with this thing is the keep warm function. Up top, it emphasizes that it can keep warm up to 48 hours. Not just in the product description, but the pictures too. It can‚Äôt. The manual itself says for TWO hours. I‚Äôve tested it both using the keep warm option where you just set the temp after boiling, as well as the press the power button then set a temp to keep warm option. With both methods, after two hours, it make a few beeps and then shuts off. The keep warm for the advertised 48 hours was what sold me on this kettle, and it stinks that it doesn‚Äôt do what it claims.Overall, I don‚Äôt know what to make of this thing. I thought Cuckoo was supposed to be a good brand. I don‚Äôt love it, but I don‚Äôt think I would recommend it. I don‚Äôt really hate it either. I guess my feelings overall are lukewarm at best, just like my tea.

author: Kiwipine
title: Quick and quiet
body:
I kinda wish this kettle didn't look like a disco ball when it's on. The colored lights seem to be programmed to change color as the water temperature increases but, for me it's not really necessary. (I have yet to figure out if I can turn them off).

The kettle itself looks to be a well made, quality kettle - it boils quickly and quietly. It holds a good volume of water - 1.7 L is perfect for my needs. It's comfortable to hold and pours well. I don't think I will use the tea infuser - It's perfect for a tea drinker, but not mandatory if you're not. Personally, I don't like my coffee tainted by tea. The timer is a nice addition ... but I don't know anyone who would want to keep their water (or tea) hot for 48 hours. More is not necessarily better ....

.... and honestly ... do I care what temperature my water is heated to? Can I tell the difference in my coffee if it's 150 or 200 degrees? No, not really - as long as it's hot. I'm sure some people enjoy micro managing their beverages, but I'm happy to simply have enough water hot enough to make a french press full of wonderful , delicious coffee each morning. This kettle can do that ... and more !

author: Fred C. Dobbs
title: A Good Choice for Us. Has the Features We Like and Meets Our Criteria.
body:
My wife and I are familiar with the Cuckoo brand, having owned a Cuckoo rice cooker for a number of years. Recently, we've been looking for a new electric tea kettle. When I saw the Cuckoo electric tea kettle advertised on Amazon -- with all of the features we like and knowing the brand -- I figured my finding it was a stroke of good luck.
For starters, it's a nice size, shape, and weight for us. The Cuckoo tea kettle is especially easy to operate. The infuser is a feature we may use, although most of our tea-making these days is limited to tea bags for just the two of us, and we have our own favorite teas. The LED lights are a feature that wasn't on our list, but now that we have them on our Cuckoo tea kettle, we like them. We also appreciate having a kettle made mostly of glass, which allows us to enjoy seeing the bubbling water and is a healthier option than having it made some other materials.
Overall, the Cuckoo tea kettle is a good choice for us based on its ease of use, performance, and likelihood of reliability and durability based on our experience with the brand. I'm rating it at 4.5 stars and rounding up to 5 stars.

Plus, it comes with two tops‚Äîa standard one and an infuser for tea, though I probably won‚Äôt use the infuser since I don‚Äôt brew large quantities of tea.On the (slightly) negative side:- I wish the markings on the side showed cups instead of liters.- The temperature control increases in increments of 10 degrees Celsius, which can feel odd when set to Fahrenheit.- The cord length is a bit short; I would prefer it to be twice as long.I also conducted some non-scientific temperature tests. After the water reached the set temperature, I tested it with a probe thermometer. At higher settings, it was pretty accurate, but at lower temperatures, it was off by a few degrees. I didn‚Äôt expect perfection, but it‚Äôs something to consider.Overall, it‚Äôs a great kettle that does exactly what I need‚Äîboil water quickly! title: Perfect glass tea kettle!
body: I searched quite a bit for a temperature controlled electric tea kettle without contact with plastic, and stumbled upon this one. So glad I did! I‚Äôve never heard of the brand before, but went by the reviews. It lives up to the hype. It‚Äôs made of a high quality, durable glass, and the spout is made of stainless steel. It looks so nice on my countertop too. The lid is lined with stainless steel. There are two lids‚Äîone that that has the tea infuser attached, and one that is just the lid itself. I‚Äôve just been using the standard lid without infuser. It‚Äôs very easy to use‚Äîyou can increase or decrease the temperature to specified setting depending on your preference (for example, 176 F for green tea, 194 F for coffee, or 212 F boiling.), and there are several temperature settings. It can also be switched between Fahrenheit and Celsius. Once I turn on, I increase the temperature to my desired setting, then the kettle works automatically to heat the water and beeps when done. It‚Äôs really cool to see the water boiling and it also has color coded lights that change at certain temperatures (from green when cool, to blue, to pink/purple, to red near boiling and boiling point.) The temperature control also shows the temperature at all times while in use, and the kettle has an automatic shut-off feature. It works exactly as described, looks sleek, and is decent quality. The opening is wide, so refilling and washing are easy. The only thing is that the lid needs to be removed by hand to refill or wash the kettle, rather than have a button to push, but it‚Äôs a minor issue for such a great product. I‚Äôd recommend it without hesitation.

The previous ones were simple pots that only boiled and automatically shut off. The Cuckoo has variable preset temperature settings with auto shut off and 3 beeps to let you know it‚Äôs finished. Others that we considered had individual buttons for each temperature but the Cuckoo has up and down buttons to select the temp ‚Äî some may prefer the individual buttons. ¬†I chose the Cuckoo because its handle shape keeps my hand down and away from the steam ‚Äî our last one allowed your hand to ride up to the top and cook your hand. We‚Äôve never bothered with the tea making features so I have no comment on its effectiveness. It‚Äôs not double-walled like some others but we don‚Äôt have little kids reaching up and touching it. date: Reviewed in the United States on March 1, 2023
author: LIZA
title: I THINK I love this multicooker? But it is a commitment.
body: I've had this for about a year and just started using it a few months ago, after a ton of research. It's a beautiful, sturdy, GIANT machine, and as one person I hate the idea of this sitting permanently on my counter, but I'm fine with my new Cuckoo station. (After all these reviews I bought the rice cooker also, since most likely I'd want rice with whatever I'm cooking in this.)No, it doesn't speak Korean (which annoys me too); it really is enormous; the lid is hydraulic and smashes into my upper kitchen cabinet unless you handle it carefully, both handed.The manual has many issues, since it's inconsistent, vague, and same with online recipes, etc. There is no clear answer on anything really- I've researched this for months now after trying to use it and though it's a nightmare to pore over everyone's input, I think I'm finally figuring this out. I generally know how to cook normally, but this is infuriating since you have no idea when it's at pressure; it's vague whether steam cook is at pressure (it claims not, but the pressure button lights up; the manual says to do something impossible to turn it off or is defective- so here it is contradictory.)Rice: in the Amazon description it specifically states this setting is for LONG GRAIN ONLY; I took a risk and used it for short; it turned out on the very gloppy end. Apparently ppl like to use the steam function, but there are so many variables I have not figured this out yet.  Good thing I also got the actual rice cooker.Multicook- what is this exactly, someone please explain. There is no clear answer anywhere. The top level seems too hot; the lower levels take ages to sear/brown anything.Presets: how to change them is inconsistent, as I'm having a HARD time pressing the buttons, and the menu is difficult to see unless you are looking at it head-on. So this means crouching down and squinting in the 3-second time window to have to figure out what you are pressing.I do love that the handles are not hot and that there is a stainless steel inner pot. However, is defeats the purpose if it comes with a plasticine steamer plate.I do love that it doesn't stink up your kitchen or spew smelly liquids out of the pressure spout. The auto clean is easy buttime-consuming. The buttons are so hard to press that it is a two handed situation, as well as opening the pot, or it will jump otherwise. That or ruin the opening spring. This I find ridiculous for it otherwise being a well designed pot (?)Also the lack of precise documentation is infuriating. It's good for people who just like to press one button and not know why it works.  Or not.That said, I will update if anything else crazy happens...

author: Peter K. Evans
title: Advanced features, great looks, but one serious design flaw that ruins it
body: I used the Cuckoo for a couple months before throwing in the towel. The Cuckoo has some very advanced features, not found in other multi-cookers, and looks fantastic. The main problem is the timer. Most recipes call for "pressure cook for x minutes" - but you can't program the Cuckoo to do this. You can only program the timer for the entire time it's cooking, from warm-up to finish. I constantly over-cooked or under-cooked recipes because of this. I switched to the unit recommended by America's Test Kitchen - which isn't as advanced, nor as well built, nor as good looking - and never looked back. The Cuckoo is like a Cadillac with wobbly wheels - great unit but the engineers need to go back to the drawing board and fix this fundamental design flaw.

author: Andrew
title: Do not purchase as a primary rice cooker
body: I've heard rave reviews, particularly from the Korean community both online and in-person about the Cuckoo line of multi-purpose pressure cookers so we decided to give this one a try. On the first impression, build quality is great with solid plastics and metals with included accessories like a measuring cup and rice paddle. We purchased this with the intention of primarily using it as a rice cooker and after a few rounds of cooking and keeping rice warm, the overall impression goes down. The thing speaks to you throughout the whole process from selection of function, pressurizing of the cooker, and even the release of the pressure with simulated pressure release sounds.If purchasing this for use primarily for cooking rice I would steer clear and go for a Zojirushi. It can cook rice, but not to the standard of an almost $200 rice cooker. Uneven cooking, some parts cooked, overcooked, and even undercooked. The keep-warm function has to be the worst. Steam isn't necessarily being released because of the locking mechanism meaning but even when not locked completely and kept on the keep warm function, actual puddles of steam would collect and continue to be absorbed by the rice. By the end of a 3 hour keep warm, almost all the rice would be too soggy to even enjoy.If you plan on using this rice cooker to cook small batches of rice which would be consumed right away this could be the solution of freeing up counter space for a rice cooker/pressure cooker/slow cooker making it perfect for smaller kitchens. Otherwise, if you're particular with your rice and prefer to keep rice warm for several hours skip this pressure cooker and shop for a dedicated rice cooker.

date: Reviewed in the United States on March 30, 2019
author: Ryan McLean
title: Timer Flawed - Fundamentally Fails as a Pressure Cooker
body: tl:dr - Cuckoo pressure cooker timer is for total cook time, not time at pressure. This is contrary to how all pressure cooker recipes are written, making this electric pressure cooker essentially pointless for following pressure cooker recipes.I took a chance on this Cuckoo Multi Pressure Cooker over the ubiquitous instant pot. I was excited about the possibility of the automatic steam valve and overall aesthetic. Unfortunately it is getting returned.All pressure cooker recipes are written and based on time-at-pressure.This is done because once a pressure cooker has reached pressure it is at more or less a known temperature (Similar to preheating an oven). The time it takes to get to pressure will vary depending on the size of the pressure cooker, how full it is, and the actual makeup of the stuff (More liquid versus more solid).To account for this - most (probably all - I double checked the manuals for 4 popular brands) other pressure cookers have a timer that doesn't start counting down until the pressure cooker actually reaches pressurization.Design Defect Number 1Unfortunately the timer on this Cuckoo works differently - the timer starts counting down as soon as you start cooking, and doesn't take into account whether the cooker has reached pressurization or not. This presents two big challenges.Following recipes written for other pressure cookers simply will not work, because the pressure cooking times given on those recipes assumes the timer will not start counting down until the pressure cooker reaches the pressurization stage.One example of the result of this - All pressure cooker recipes require some liquid for the pressure cooker to pressurize and work. This can just be plain water or a broth or sauce. In this cuckoo, starting with cold versus warm liquids would affect the outcome of a recipe because the starting temperature of these liquids would affect how long it takes for the unit to come up to pressure. In other pressure cookers, this could still somewhat affect the outcome, but the effect would be much less since the most important thing in pressure cooking is time at pressure.Design Defect Number 2The machine does not give you any indication whether it is at pressure or not - so even if you wanted to take your own run at adjusting recipes written for other pressure cookers, it's impossible (or at least would be very difficult) for you to know how much to adjust the recipe by, because you basically have to just guess whether it is at pressure or not.I don't know how Cuckoo overlooked something so fundamental to pressure cooking. I would not recommend this unit to anyone.

author: TheBlindLife
title: Mostly Accessible for Blind
body: I was waiting for a sale on this unit. Being blind, a hefty investment. I even got Easy Pay with my Chase Amazon card.I wanted a multi - cooker that was accessible to use. This is definitely accessible with the voice guide. Cuckoo failed in one big area with the voice guide.... The unit doesn't speak temperature, or time when being set. Its not impossible to use, but you need to be able to calculate where you are when setting. Luckily, it saves your last setting you set.For blind customers... This is a sturdy device. Definitely built with safety in mind. Most important, no pressure needs to be set. Its automatic. The unit tells you when engaged and when it's safe to open. It also tells you when lock is engaged properly.Their are 8 buttons on the unit. They are slightly raised, but I still used bump dots. The Cook, and Cancel button are the only ones that have an actual tactile bump on them.I'm confident I will get much use with this cooker. If Cuckoo had the unit actually announce temperature, and time level... It would be a perfect addition to any blind cook. I'd give a 90% rating for accessibility.Update:After making a few dishes, I'm updating my rating to 5 from 4. While I was not happy about temp and heat level not having voice... I've managed to do ok. I just have to note my last meal setting, not being able to see the display.I've used the meat, brown, slow cook, and multi - cook settings. All meals came out wonderful.I feel safer. The unit doesn't get as hot on the outside as my Crock Pot. It also sits lower, not as tall. This is actually a safer thing for a blind cook. It also happens to make serving easier.

author: James K
title: TLDR.. For Korean rice, use 6 min
body: The time to replace our old rice cooker was long overdue.. We had a Cuckoo for 7yrs and in the last year, the rice wouldn't stay fresh in the pot and usually had to be thrown away if not eaten by the next day.  I didn't want to pay $400-700 for another rice cooker.. just seems too expensive for just making rice which is the only thing we use it for.  So I ordered this one..The first few times cooking rice, we used the default setting for Rice and it said 8 mins (not including heat up and pressure release).. overall, it takes about 40mins from pressing the cook button to being ready to eat.  While the rice was cooked and ready to eat, it came out a bit too soft and mushy for our taste..  From years of cooking rice, we basically know how much water to put in by eye but then again, this is a larger pot so I thought maybe it was different.  However, lowering the amount didn't help much.  I then decreased the cook time to 6min and the rice came out perfect.  Plus, the cooker kept the rice fresh for several days.  I haven't tried it for anything other than Korean rice but for that, it's fantastic.

author: Radio Ross
title: Excellent Cooker - Not so excellent manual.
body: This is an excellent all-around cooker and it does a great job on *most* things.  If you are a rice aficionado, it may not be as satisfying as a dedicated Cuckoo Rice Cooker - We have one too and, IMHO, it is the best out there.  If you only want one cooker, this is definitely the one to get - far better quality than the cheaper versions.  One caveat: Cuckoo's philosophy for this cooker is, "I Cook, You Rest" which means that their default settings for time and temperature will work in most cases.  You do have the ability to change cooking time for all options but temperature is only adjustable for about half of the options.  While this sounds like a limitation, in practice it is not.  Just be mindful that the temperature setting options are by "level", not degrees Fahrenheit.  That means there's a learning curve but once you get used to this, you'll love this cooker.  One other thing... Do not be tempted to fill the pot above the maximum mark with any liquid - particularly if you are using it in a pressure cook mode.  Doing so guarantees that liquid will spew out of the steam vent and overflow the collection cup - Spoken from experience.I do have one negative:  The user manual is not particularly helpful for cooking practices and the cookbook that's packed in with the cooker is only marginally better.  You WILL have to experiment so don't invite guests for dinner until you've played around a bit.

title: Perfect Rice and So Much More. Cuckoo for Cuckoo!
body: Excellent rice cooker (and so much more)! So far I've used this to cook rice (long grain, jasmine, brown) with ease and consistency as well as to make soups and chicken tacos (I am hoping to try baby back ribs soon). The cooker is extremely spacious and can make dinner for multiple families in one go. It was also great for a sushi making party, cooking up perfect rice in a huge quantity at the press of a button. The party was a surefire hit (I recommend buying the little bamboo mats for rolling your sushi).The cooker itself, while easy to use, is pretty sophisticated, so I would definitely recommend reading the manual through to get the most out of your Cuckoo. According to the marketing jargon, it uses an algorithm to adjust cooking according to the quantity of rice and water, and I am inclined to believe given how great the rice has come out each time, despite my less than precise measurements (a scooper is provided, but I prefer to eyeball). On the rice side, this is certainly designed for white rice varieties, and it is cool that it can create different textures (sticky, soft, etc.), but I have also found it to be great for brown rice as well. Plus, it does so much more than cook rice, as noted by the various settings.This machine also talks! I'm not so sure how I feel about the little voice??equal parts useful, terrifying, and just plain bizarre??but there is a mute option that provides immediate relief for those that find it off putting. I am keeping it on for now as the charm remains. It can sometimes even feel cheery. Regardless, it does little to take away from this amazing machine. Go Cuckoo!

date: Reviewed in the United States on March 18, 2018
author: Honest Professional Reviews
title: Excellent Korean-made construction & attention to detail; Easy to use controls. This is the multi-cooker you want.
body: Before I got this Cuckoo multi pressure cooker, I had never used a pressure cooker before. Sure, I HAVE an old fashioned pressure cooker. I am not sure where I got it, but I got it decades ago and it sits quietly on the shelf where I occasionally look at it. But I've always considered it's reason d'etre to be unclear, and the idea of many bars of pressure inside this pot scary.So maybe I wasn't the obvious target for this new do-everything-for-you pressure cooker. Or maybe I was EXACTLY the correct target.Anyway, intrigued by the idea that it does do everything--both pressure cook and release the steam automatically and safely afterwards--I took a flyer.I should add that it doesn't just generically pressure cook. It can also braise/fry in the pot. Which I found fantastically convenient, since it means you can truly make a "one pot" dinner.OK, so for my first attempt at pressure cooking, I went with pulled pork. That's a full day enterprise using other methods. With the pressure cooker, it takes about 1 hour and 15 minutes. I took a 3 pound pork shoulder, added a few tablespoons of oil, browned both sides using the "browning fry"  setting, tossed in some bbq sauce and water, and let the "pressure cook" setting do its magic for 1:15. The machine talks to you (and plays celebratory music--cute), and at 1:15 it let me know everything was done. And it was! I took out the now fully cooked port shoulder, pulled it apart with two forks (could also use a food processor or blender for this), tossed the result back in the pot with part of the sauce that the shoulder had cooked with and a little more bbq sauce, brought it to a simmer using "browning fry" and served. The result: Perfection! (See photo of the original pork shoulder and the final result).It was really really easy and it worked just as it was supposed to. There was never any worry about "is it too soon to release the pressure?"This spoken by someone who has NEVER used a pressure cooker before.Some additional comments:1) It runs SUPER quiet. In fact, the only time I really knew that it was running is either when it said something to me (like "done") or when it was letting off steam. During most of the cooking process, you could forget it's running.2) The documentation could be a bit better about the various cooking modes. Some are obvious, such as "pressure cook", "slow cook", "browning fry" and "clean". (Yeah, it has a self-cleaning mode. Just add 3 cups of water and press start--very nice). But what exactly does "Multi Cook" do? It's never explained anywhere in the manual, and even online I couldn't find a straight answer.3) The parts that come in contact with the food (the bowl, the interior cover) are easily removable for cleaning. The bowl is non-stick on the entire surface (not just the bottom like the cheapo competitors like InstantPot) which is convenient.4) It's a fairly large appliance. Bigger than a bread machine, and it needs a decent amount of clearance above the cooker for the top to open.5) There are many safety interlocks and checks, along with automatic pressure valves that will let off steam if needed to keep the pressure from getting too high.6) Quality is top notch. Everything fits together with tight tolerances and everything works smoothly out of the box. This is made in South Korea, not China, and it's of the expected high quality.7) If you have never used one of these before (raises hand) expect to spend at least half an hour just familiarizing yourself with the cooker and reading through the fairly lengthy instructions.8) Cooking modes include: Pressure cooking, steam cooking, slow cooking, browning/frying.9) Specific food type modes include: soup, meat, vegetables, porridge, rice,10) There's also a "keep warm" mode for delayed serving. And you can set a timer so that cooking starts in the future (up to 12 hour delay).11) As a FYI, here's a list of sample food types for which the manufacturer provides cooking modes/settings. As you can infer, this is a jack of all trades: cauliflower and potato soup; french onion soup; ginger and butternut squash soup; black bean soup; baby back ribs; one pot beans, sausage and greens; teriyaki pork loin; eggplant and roasted red pepper dip; zucchini ratatouille; brown butter fingerling potatoes; horseradish mashed potatoes; breakfast porridge; purple yam barley porridge; jasmine rice; sausage and cheese frittata; mashed potatoes; chile Colorado; creme brulee; New England clam chowder; red lentil chili; steamed artichokes; crab legs; steamed ribs with glutinous rice; turnip cake; Korean steamed ribs; pomegranate sauce; sour cream; yogurt. And obviously the list can go on and on.12) The LCD screen is big and bright. There aren't that many buttons, and selection is mostly done by scrolling through the options on the LCD screen. It's pretty easy-to-use and intuitive--something that does not appear to be the case with many of the competitors.One the whole, this is one fantastic appliance that actually justifies the precious counter space it takes up. Highly recommended!

I also like that there is only one rice function. 30 minutes was the maximum time it allowed and the rice came out perfectly. (I add beans and squash to my rice if you're wondering about the picture)- MULTI- FUCTION - no need for separate rice cooker and pressure cooker! This device does it all, and frees up my counter space in the process.- BEAUTIFUL - clean, classic, white and rose gold - if only all my other kitchen appliances made me feel this good.- GREAT QUALITY - the nonstick surface makes clean up a breeze. Personally, I've never seen nonstick quality this good on other pots and pans.- interactive - lights, sounds, and whistles make the cooking experience feel more modern and luxurious. My son also enjoys helping out pushing the buttons.Cons:- BULKY - it doesn't have to be so bulky, but it is.- EXPENSIVE - but worth it, given that it serves multiple functions.

date: Reviewed in the United States on February 3, 2018
author: Trang
title: Smart Technology, Versatile and Stylish - A Wonderful Multi-Cooker!
body: I've had the Cuckoo ICOOK Q5 Premium for about 2 weeks now and so far I like it more than my Instant Pot. With smarter technology, this multi-cooker is versatile, easy to use and stylish. The function buttons are simple and intuitive. Use just one "Menu" button to cycle through the different built-in programs: SOUP, MEAT, VEGETABLES, RICE, PORRIDGE, BROWNING FRY, MULTI COOK, STEAM COOK, SLOW COOK, AUTO CLEAN and then use the "Selection" button to adjust the cooking time. Press "Cook" to start...super easy!Two differentiating features intrigued me right away:#1 Auto Clean - releases a strong jet of steam to clean and sanitize the interior of the multi-cooker. I love this function and used it to sanitize my new cooker before cooking food for the first time. Since then I've used it multiple times.#2 Adjustable Keep Warm - lets you set the temperature from 154-176 degrees Fahrenheit. I like having the ability to adjust this and have found the static "Keep Warm" can be too hot for certain foods.Pressure cooking, steaming and cooking rice are the functions I use most and having all of these in one appliance is a huge win. I tested the "Rice" mode first and it cooked jasmine white rice perfectly in about 30 minutes. The unique feature to note about the "Rice" function is it pressure cooks and then steams the rice.Using the "Meat" mode, I pressure cooked 8 sticky rice and banana cakes (thick roll cakes) for 45 minutes and they were cooked perfectly. (If I had boiled these on the stove top, it would have taken about 1 1/2 - 2 hours, a huge time-savings.)I like the steam plate is included and not an accessory for additional purchase. So far I've steamed broccoli using Level 1 for 15 minutes and they came out soft but not mushy. My wish for the "Steam Cook" function would be an option to steam for less than 15 minutes. Some foods are delicate and don't require 15 minutes of steaming. The workaround is to cancel when the needed cook time has elapsed, not a huge inconvenience.I thought the 5-quart pot would be a bit small compared to my 6-quart Instant Pot. So far, it hasn't been an issue. I will have to make a few more family-sized recipes to weigh-in on this further. Perhaps Cuckoo will offer an 8 or even 10-quart multi-cooker size in the near future.I like the look and design of the Cuckoo ICOOK Q5 Premium Multi Cooker. It's an egg-shaped, minimalist design and quite attractive. It's a nice appliance to display on the kitchen counter.The Smart Voice Guide is novel. She announces what the multi cooker is doing like "Steaming is starting" and "Rice is complete". It's really cute and a great way to monitor cooking without having to watch it constantly.In addition to the instruction manual, the multi cooker comes with a 30-recipe cookbook. The recipes are easy and a great way to get acquainted with the cooker and enjoy some yummy dishes. There are also more recipes offered on the Cuckoo website.

author: Amy Pell
title: 4-month review
body:
I've had this rice cooker for a little over 4 months, and I've made basmati rice (but only basmati) many times now -- sometimes with veggies, and sometimes not.

I'll say up front:  It cooks 2 cups uncooked basmati in about 27 minutes, and it's better  (overall) than i can make on my gas stovetop.  The leftover rice is also better coming out of the fridge for some reason.  If you eat a lot of rice, I can recommend you at least consider this unit.

That being said:

1.  I have a general dislike for single-use appliances.  This one at least has the added value of also steaming your vegetables, but it still takes up a lot of precious countertop space for what it is.

2.  Speaking of steaming vegetables, it does an OK job of this.  However, at the time the rice cook cycle is done, the veggies are a little underdone to my taste.  This is personal preference, but I like my cooked veggies a bit more done.  They will continue to cook after the unit switches to "warm" which helps the veggies, but this also serves to overcook your rice, which leads me to...

3.  While the bulk of your rice gets very nicely cooked, there will be a layer on the bottom that gets overcooked.  If you catch it soon enough and stir the whole batch, it's not too bad.  However, if you let the unit go longer (such as if you want your veggies cooked longer; or if you simply left the unit on "warm" until you come back for a 2nd helping), the bottom layer continues to brown and stick together.

4.  We have a general rule (with just a few exceptions) that if it can't go in the dishwasher, it doesn't belong in our house.  The photos of the bowl and steamer basket are after several washings in our dishwasher.  The bowl received a big dent after colliding with another dish, as it's extremely thin metal.  The steamer basket has oxidized significantly because it's made of untreated aluminum.  I'm sure the oxidation could be removed by scrubbing, but I'm not going to waste a scotchbrite pad on that cheesegrater surface.

All this is to say, it's kind of a "cheap" unit.  Sometimes I think I'd rather have a nicer unit that doesn't feel so cheap, but I don't think it would be worth it to upgrade in my case.

Overall: This CUCKOO CR-0601C is an all-around great buy. It combines speed, convenience, capacity, and easy cleanup into one essential appliance. Highly recommended for anyone looking to simplify their cooking routine!
