author: J
title: Really not good enough for the price they charge...
body:
Does it work? Yes, it actually works decently. I usually cook jasmine rice, it cooks that to a decent consistency. It comes with everything you need to cook and steam too. It cooks it fast, within ten or fifteen minutes for two uncooked cups.

But I really can't get over how cheap it feels and not in terms of physical materials like cheap plastic or something, but the design and the lack of features. Pricing and features are always in an intricate dance, companies have to set prices and cut costs by cutting features in a way that satisfies consumers. If they do this correctly the consumer will be satisfied because even though they paid less the features were appropriate and they didn't feel like they were being ripped off, this thing is an example of when the dance goes wrong, they cut too many features, they cut way too deep that the price sticks out like a sore thumb because it doesn't match, there's no value here, you're getting way too little for what you're paying.

Here's my biggest gripes, you can judge for yourself:
❌ While it cooks the rice decently, it's nowhere near as good as the ones with a gasketed lid that holds the steam in, those produce a much fluffier rice than this one.
❌ The rice pot spins and jumps around. Other rice cookers (other Cuckoos too) have pots that are keyed to the unit, meaning a part of the pot juts out so it fits/locks into the cooker and prevents the pot from spinning. Since the pot is completely round it spins as you attempt to scoop rice out which is annoying, you can't hold the pot still either since it's hot. The pot actually lift outs too because it's light and the rice acts as a glue between the pot and your scoop, the stickier the type of rice the worse it will be.
❌ The unit has no power button: how much could they have possibly saved by not having a power button! It means every time you plug it in it turns on, when you want to turn it off you have to unplug it from the wall which wears out the power outlet unnecessarily, for older people with poor dexterity (no grip strength) in their hands this is going to be impossible to deal with. If you have a kitchen where the power outlet is not easily accessible like there's stuff in the way, it's behind something, it's at the back of a long counter-top, etc it's also going to be impossible to deal with. In today's world where electricity prices are through the roof you can't really afford to waste electricity with out-of-touch nonsense like this, you should only buy this if you have a switched outlet or an extension cord switch thing, to give the rice cooker the power switch it should have come with from the start!
❌ When they say "One Touch" they mean it, once it detects the rice is done and goes from "Cook" to "Warm", you can't put it back to "Cook" for whatever reason, there's a thermal fuse or something that prevents the button from going back to "Cook" until the unit completely cools. This means if you have to cook multiple batches you're out of luck unless you wait for it to cool.
❌ There is no alarm, sound, indicator that anything is done, when it finishes cooking the thermal fuse resets the "Cook" switch to "Warm" and that's it. You might prefer a rice cooker with an LCD display that shows you a countdown timer, a warm timer, and at least makes a beep when it's done cooking (or talks to you with speech like the more expensive Cuckoos do).
❌ The rice cooker is light and has no rubber feet so it slides around on the counter-top easily.
❌ The power cable sticks out of the right side of the unit, why they made it stick out of the side is beyond me, putting it at the center back would be neutral to every counter-top layout, putting it on one side means it's extremely awkward for any kitchen where the rice cooker is on the wrong side of the outlet. Since the power cable doesn't bend easily (it's very rigid/stiff), if your power outlet is not on the "correct" side of the rice cooker that has the power cable, the power cable will make the cooker rotate so that the power outlet is at the back, which means the front of the unit with the "Cook" switch isn't facing forward its facing a side, because again the unit is light and has no rubber feet to prevent the cable from rotating the whole cooker.
❌ There is no seal between the lid and the pot, no gasket, it's a metal ring on the lid that sits on the rough texture of the pot, so if you leave your rice in there it will dry out quickly (the large ventilation hole on the pot lid doesn't help). Other rice cookers, other Cuckoos even, have silicone gasketed lids that latch on and make the pot mostly sealed tight to keep moisture in, aside from a steam vent, you can leave cooked rice in those without it drying out.
❌ It's made in China, the more expensive Cuckoos are made in South Korea, and honestly it seems like they picked a generic Chinese rice cooker and slapped their name on it. I sincerely doubt Cuckoo had any engineering or design input into this, go shop around you'll find lots of cheap rice cookers that look very similar to this one, except they cost half the price this does...
❌ The exterior is made of cheap-feeling white plastic, you would expect brushed stainless or matte black plastic for appliances, white plastics tend to stain from food and turn yellow over time especially when exposed to heat which this thing will constantly.

Some of these problems like the missing power button, inability to cook on-demand, and the lack of a pot lid seal are so bad it seriously makes you consider paying more for a more expensive unit, which I ultimately did by moving up to a $60 Gourmia unit which has none of these issues.

$40 for this seems like they priced it this way due to the brand name, if you showed this rice cooker to 100 people with the brand name hidden by tape (a blind test), I suspect the majority would price it at $20, they cut too way too deep on the features for this to be worth any more than $20. Actually when I look at the sum total of this thing, just sit there and look at it from the outside with a finger on my chin pondering, you know what it reminds me of? Its size... its functionality... the build quality... the feel of the cheap plastic exterior... not a "rice cooker"... but a wax melter! If you've ever been to a salon to get hair waxed off, there's a machine they put the solid wax pellets or wax tin in that heats it up until it turns into a liquid and keeps it warm? This thing has the size, features, and feel of a wax melter, I'm not even joking, and not the average wax melter, the cheapest kind, because even an average wax melter has a power switch and temperature dial...

However, I do think there will be some trial and error with cooking, as the instructions are essentially non-existent. author: Beth A
title: Does a standup job cooking white rice, and steaming foods – separately or at the same time
body:
If you're looking for a really good, basic 1 to 6 cup (uncooked) rice cooker at an attractive price, look no further!  So far I've only cooked varieties of white rice in it, as I haven't yet found the instructions for brown rice or other grains which the product description indicates this will cook, but it does a terrific job with white rice which is what most people will want it for; and the price is right.

We've had a rice cooker for a lot of decades, and find it one of the most helpful small kitchen appliances there is.  Just measure your rice with the cup included (sized to measure the amount of rice per one regular measuring cup of water), rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then add water up to the marked line on the inside of the rice cooker for the amount of rice you're going to cook (or use a regular measuring cup to measure water for very well drained rice), pop the lid on, and plug it in.  Fluff when you see the light color change or hear a click indicating that it's gone to warm, and enjoy your rice sometime in the next 12 hours.  I love that it's got a steamer rack for dumplings, veggies, meats/fish, or reheating something to go with our rice.

Our first rice cooker was basic, like this one, and gave us perfect rice almost every day for over 30 years.  Unfortunately, without getting any input from me, my husband then went out and bought the first cheap rice cooker he could find, but fortunately (considering how unevenly it cooked the rice), that one bit the dust in a few months.  I made sure its replacement was from a very reputable brand.  Being a newly redesigned basic rice cooker from the leader in the field, Cuckoo, I trust that this should last a good while.

I see this as an entry level rice cooker for new homes or dorms, but we'll be taking it with us in our travel trailer, so that we can have freshly cooked regular rice with our meals.  It's quite lightweight, so tucking it away in or removing it from a cupboard should not be difficult.

Thank you for reading my review.  I hope you found it helpful.

The steamer tray doesn't really fit in the pot, it tips easily, so handle with care since it's hot. Zero instructions other than the box flap, although the booklet keeps referring to detailed instructions that don't exist. It claims to make a variety of food, but really it's just to warm up or steam something quickly. It's a one button affair, no idea how it decides that fish is thoroughly/safely cooked. Lastly, the rice had a bit of a new Teflon smell/taste, like when you plug in a curling iron for the first time, but it wasn't that bad and I imagine that will go away quickly.
The rice was good, auto shutoff/switch to warm worked and cooked faster than expected.

(2) removing the rubber gasket from the inner plate is a bit of a chose and it's easy to damage the rubber gasket, so be careful - must be done though because it traps rice water steam which will grow bacteria

(3) the user interface is not great and instructions are written in microscopic font. wish they'd spend some time making the instructions clearer, simpler and larger font.

on the whole though I really like this as we cook enormous quantities of rice for 2 active people and a hungry dog every week!

author: Tobi
title: Great Affordable Starter Rice Cooker
body: I bought CUCKOO Rice Cooker when it was on sale and it was worth every penny. I do also own a more expensive model (with more bells and whistles), but when I moved states for a short term stay (6 months) I bought the cheaper version and was impressed by the value.For the price, this rice cooker delivers great results. The quick cook function is a huge plus, cooking rice in under 10 minutes. I have played around with the other settings and I get rice of the perfect texture nearly every time. The built-in measuring cup system, makes it super easy to gage the correct amount of water-to-rice as well.I liked how lightweight it is compared to the other models, that were extremely heavy.  On the downside, I have to hold the lid when opening since it will swing open and topple over (learned that the hard way).I also appreciate how easy it is to clean, between the non-stick pot and the fact its dishwasher safe.The only negative, is that I felt the fuzzy logic system on this model isn??t as advanced as the higher-end CUCKOO models, so it may not offer as much precision or extra features.For the price, it??s a great option for anyone looking for a reliable rice cooker without breaking the bank.

author: Fordhouse
title: Beautiful, but with flawed controls and markings.
body: I looks absolutely great compared to my old and trusty zojirushi, and the pot feels a lot sturdier, though there is major design flaw. My old Zojirushi was a 3 cup model, compared to the 6 cup capacity of this one, so I am not sure if that is a fair comparison. Maybe Zojirushi's higher capacity models also have sturdier pots. The downside of this model is the controls. They are not pleasant to use at all. Often, in fact almost always, I must press buttons several times before anything happens at all. Trying to cancel something, or to turnoff the keep warm setting can be frustrating when the buttons wont respond. Another downside is the markings inside the pot. Unless you are in an extremely well lit area, the measuring indications inside the pot are very difficult to read. Unlike the zojirushe, they are just raised stampings, and do not have a contrasting color. Having to use the flashlight on my phone to see how much water to pour in is frustrating. If you are using the rice cooker in a sufficiently lit area, this might be a non-issue, or at least a smaller issue. I also miss the little tune my that Zojirushi rice cookers plays when the rice is done. The rice comes out fine.

author: TW
title: This is NOT a pressure rice cooker like other Cuckoos.  Very disappointing.
body: This is NOT a pressure rice cooker. Be sure you understand that before buying.  It is just an ordinary rice cooker that cooks by steaming.  That makes it different from other Cuckoo rice cookers.  But that is not made clear in the product description.  Misleading description.  One of the great advantages of other Cuckoo rice cookers is that they cook by pressure cooking.  Not only does it speed the time, but it makes the rice come out exceptionally well.  Unfortunately, this is not like a normal Cuckoo rice cooker.  It just cooks by steaming.  And it is very poorly made compared to the high quality of other Cuckoo rice cookers.  It is way overpriced for what it is.  If you want a rice steamer of this quality, you can get one for a lot, lot less money.  Extremely disappointing.  Additionally, the rice sticks to the inner pot in a way that was not true of my previous Cuckoo cooker, making it harder to clean.  If you are looking for a good quality, traditional  Cuckoo rice cooker, look at one of the other models.  Do not buy this one.  I make rice every day and have used a Cuckoo cooker for years, with great happiness.  But this model is a piece of junk.  And it does not even do a good job of cooking rice.

body: Bought this Micom during Dec sale. I haven't tried korean cooker models before. My findings are its  consistently delivers well-cooked rice, regardless of the grain type. The multicooking feature is particularly handy, offering convenience and freeing up time for other tasks.However, one potential downside is its relatively large size, which may take up more counter space than expected. . author: EL
title: Perfect for Baby Food and Beyond!
body: I used to own an expensive Cuckoo rice cooker, but after a couple of fixing attempts, I decided to donate it. When I saw this cooker on sale at a reasonable price, I thought, why not give it a try? Primarily, I use it for making baby food and steaming veggies. I've also explored multicooking, especially when preparing oxtail soup for my baby. Although it takes a little over an hour and a half, it's more convenient than constantly checking manually, and the meat turns out soft enough for my little one.I've even utilized the soup without meat to make porridge for my baby. Over the past year, it has worked perfectly for my needs. If you're only using it for cooking rice, it's just okay. Expensive rice cookers tend to make the rice sweeter and shinier, whereas this one is more basic in that regard. However, I'm delighted to continue using this rice maker for preparing a variety of foods. It's also easy to clean, which adds to its appeal.

author: Dobbs
title: Frustrating
body:
This is a very poorly-designed piece of tech and I do not recommend it.

The inner bowl, which is the only place that specifies the amount of water necessary, is basically illegible. I've attached a photo of mine. It simply cannot be read. I've literally carried the bowl into each room of my house to see if the light can make it more legible. Nope. You need this information every time you use the machine, so essentially you're frustrated every time you use it.

That info (amount of water needed) is not in the manual. It's not on a sticker. It's literally only in one space and cannot be read.

Next, the lid doesn't stay shut. Each time you press a button on the lid to change the program or start or end the process, the lid rattles and makes a click sound.

In order to press the button to open the unit, you either need to use two hands or have the back of the unit up against a wall so stop it from moving. Only have one hand or only have one hand free? Forget it, you ain't getting your rice unless you slide the unit to the back of your counter.

Then, when the lid does open, the whole pot leaps off the counter. Doesn't matter if the bowl is full or empty.

Also, you know how modern manuals are in English, and then there's a French section and then German, etc. Nope. This one has French and English seemingly randomly spread. Two pages of English, one of French, three English, two French...

I will be sending this back and will instead purchase a model that, at the very least, has legible markings in the bowl. I hated using this device.

title: Fluffy Rice All Day, But with a Tricky Lid
body:
I recently bought the CUCKOO CR-0675F Micom Rice Cooker and it has been a fantastic addition to my kitchen. It consistently produces exceptionally fluffy and delicious rice, which is a big plus for any rice lover.

One of the standout features for me is its ability to keep the rice perfect throughout the day. It's wonderful to be able to cook a batch in the morning and still have perfectly warm and fresh rice for dinner.

However, there is a small drawback. The button to open the lid requires a bit of effort, often needing two hands to operate. This can be a bit inconvenient, especially when you're multitasking in the kitchen.

Despite this minor issue, I'm very pleased with my purchase. The CUCKOO CR-0675F is reliable, efficient, and maintains the quality of the rice for hours. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a high-quality rice cooker, just be prepared for a little extra effort when opening it.

author: MOHAMMAD MOHTASHAM
title: Good all around rice cooker
body:
I am Iranian, and my wife is Chinese. We have distinct preferences when it comes to eating rice. Chinese cuisine leans towards sticky rice, while Iranians prefer their rice to be well-grained and scorched at the bottom. That's why we opted for this rice cooker, allowing us to prepare rice in both styles. Since it is designed more for Asian cooking, it excels at making sticky rice using the quick and regular modes. However, crafting scorched rice takes approximately 1 hour. While it does a decent job, the rice tends to be a bit too sticky for the Iranian style, though this doesn't bother me personally.

In terms of cleaning, the pot is easy to clean, but reassembling the lid can be a bit challenging.

The touchscreen control buttons have a sleek appearance, but they are not as user-friendly as physical buttons. The captions are not easily readable from different angles, which might be a slight inconvenience for some, although it doesn't bother me much.

I do wish it had a dedicated power button. Currently, the only way to turn it off completely is to unplug it, which can be a bit cumbersome as it requires the use of both hands.

Despite these minor drawbacks, I am considering buying this rice cooker again mainly because of its scorched rice feature.

Sadly, the Cuckoo doesn't measure up.

Pros :
its a very good quality rice cooker with all the features that I wanted

Cons :
it doesn't have a quick cook mode
the cup/water level marks are impossible to read (black on black!!!)
the water level marks are not correct!  I need to add more water that indicated or else I get "crunchy" rice!
the Oatmeal setting is worthless (i have to cook at least 3-4 times at that setting to get an acceptable bowl of oatmeal!!!)
No cake mode!  (I need this to make fluffy japanese pancakes).

Summary, I wish I had just bought another Zojirushi instead of this.

Sure, it makes great rice if you know how to overcome its idiosyncrasies, but everything else is a huge let down.

body:

I would say the rice cooker was pretty perfect. Except since all the wiring and buttons are on top, the balance on the rice cooker is a bit funny when you open it.
The button to open is at the front of the rice cooker on the sides. When clicked open the top part becomes heavy and makes the rice cooker unbalanced, leaning toward the side with the most weight. It did cause a concern since I would like to open the rice cooker without holding it down. I usually hold the back end of the side before clicking open. This cuckoo should be opened carefully. title: Love the modern look but missing some details
body:
i purchased this cuckoo because i wanted to try a different brand than my previous rice cooker, which was a top japanese brand.  i was super happy with my previous rice cooker which i've been using for about 20 years.  i assumed the cuckoo would be just as good in design and cooking.

i received the unit in good condition, it was packed very well and came with a rice paddle and rice measuring cup.  out of the box, this cuckoo is beautiful.  i stared and admired it for a few minutes then pressed on the button to open the top lid....when the heavy lid swung open and tilted the unit back a bit, this was my first disappointment.  then i realized the cord was not designed to be retractable, nor does it have a place to keep the cord tidy.  the unit also does not have a handle.

i was still excited to use the unit and the cooking buttons are not as intuitive.  also delayed cooking timer has to be set by how many hours later you want it to cook...not the time you would like the rice to be finished.  also, if you brush by the 'cancel' button with your hand, it will stop the cooking.

the rice does finish perfect.  we've tried oatmeal and that cooks fine as well.

overall, i can't say it's the best rice cooker i have ever had.  i've have had quite a few in my lifetime.
this cuckoo does cook rice very well but there are some missing features that will probably shift me back to the top japanese brand next time.

author: Secret Angel
title: Reliable and Efficient Rice Cooker
body:
I recently purchased the CUCKOO CR-0675F 6-Cup (Uncooked) Micom Rice Cooker, and overall, it has been a reliable addition to my kitchen. This rice cooker offers efficiency and ease of use, delivering well-cooked rice consistently.

One of the standout features of this rice cooker is its compact size. With a capacity of 6 cups (uncooked), it is perfect for smaller households or those with limited counter space. The compact design doesn't compromise on performance, as it cooks rice evenly and thoroughly.

The micom (microcomputer) technology employed by the CUCKOO CR-0675F ensures precise temperature control and cooking times. This results in well-cooked rice with a desirable texture and consistency. The rice is fluffy, and each grain is properly cooked without any undercooked or overcooked portions.

The user-friendly interface and simple operation make this rice cooker accessible to both beginners and experienced users. The clear LCD display and intuitive buttons allow for easy selection of cooking options and adjustments. Additionally, the programmable delay timer is a convenient feature, enabling you to have freshly cooked rice ready at your desired time.

The non-stick inner pot is another positive aspect of this rice cooker. It prevents rice from sticking to the bottom, making cleaning a breeze. The inner pot and accessories, such as the rice spatula and measuring cup, are of good quality and durable.

author: Hard2Please
title: Not perfect, but makes good rice
body:
Preface: I'm on a quest for the perfect, reasonably priced rice cooker. Sadly this is not it the one for me. My family eats white, sticky rice every day, so I'm looking for a rice cooker that looks good on the counter and not only makes tasty rice, but also keeps it warm and soft for days. My old Panasonic was retired after 25 years. It was replaced with a Zojirushi NS-TSC18 which made tastier rice, but after a few months, it started drying out rice on the keep warm setting. I tried going back to a basic Zojirushi with no bells and whistles (Zojirushi NS-RPC18FJ), but I realized that a micom (microcomputer) rice cooker does actually make rice with better taste and texture.

As for the Cuckoo CR-0675F | 6-Cup (Uncooked) Micom Rice Cooker

PROS:
- cooks rice well
- keeps rice warm without drying it out
- high quality non-stick finish on cooking pan
- versatile menu options
- compact design
- attractive appearance (important since mine lives on the counter)
- affordably priced

CONS:
- push button on front (the whole unit slides back when you push the button)
- top-heavy lid (in order to keep footprint small, electronics are in the lid. When you open the lid, it has so
much momentum that the entire unit rocks back and forth)
- quantity markings inside the pan are hard to read (black on black)
- I prefer a longer soak time in the programming (of course one could just soak the rice before starting the
cycle, like I used to do with my old rice cooker; it really does improve the taste and texture)
- not a retractable cord
- no spatula holder

For the money, it is a decent rice cooker, but for me, there are too many annoying things about it to put up with every day.

title: There are better choices
body: I use my rice cooker to make rice a few times each month, and to make oatmeal practically every day.  I generally make the oatmeal using traditional "old fashioned" rolled oats and I only make enough for one serving which is about 1/3 cup of uncooked oats.  My old rice cooker, a brand that started with a Z, worked great for both of these tasks for 5 years until it broke (the handle latch).  Instead of having it repaired I decided that the cookers with fuzzy logic must all be similar, so I purchased this one in the 3 cup version.  I usually make jasmine rice and so far it has tended to be on the dry and hard side, despite following the instructions exactly.  I'm sure in time I'll get it adjusted to be right.  The oatmeal however has been a great disappointment.  My old machine made delicious creamy oatmeal, though once in a while it would spill over and make a mess.  I never could figure out why that happened when it did.  This Cuckoo machine has belched out a gloppy mess through the vent every single time.  I've tried adjusting all settings including cooking time, warming temp, ratios of oatmeal/water, rinsing longer, etc.  all to no avail.  I switched to steel cut oats and it no longer spills over so I'm hopeful that I'll get a good end result eventually, but I prefer the traditional oats.  I also prefer to put them in the night before on timer so they are ready in the morning.  This process was much easier on the old machine.  I'd set it and it stayed set.  This one requires re-setting of the timer duration each night.  In general, this machine probably offers more user adjustable functions, but the old one was simpler and just plain worked better.  I'm quite disappointed.  The manual is also very poorly written.

author: N. Morris
title: Barely lasted a month
body:
I really wanted to like this pot. My friends joke that I'm one of the few (only?) Asians they know who doesn't use a rice cooker. Even my mom used a rice cooker when I was growing up. But I married a non-asian who barely cooks but knows how to boil rice. When he showed me how, it was so easy, so I just made rice on the stove for the past 18 years.

After one  burnt rice incident too many, I was finally sold on the thought that I can program the rice cooking and avoid burning my house down

Cuckoo seemed like a good option. Good reviews, not too big, cute enought to sit on my counter; not too expensive but not suspiciously cheap. She arrived carefully and beautifully packaged.

I did not understand her buttons, even after studying the manual. So I decided to keep things nice and simple between Cuckoo and I as we got to know each other. Wash rice in a different bowl, drain,  pour rice into the rice cooker pot; measure water; wipe everything dry and pop everything into the cooker. Set Sticky White Rice -> Start. Seemed easy enough.

First time I used it, the jasmine rice cooked nicely. Second time I tried sushi rice and it didn't cook through.  Could have been my mistake with measuring the water but I figured I'll start understanding Cuckoo better soon and things  will improve. Third time, I got an error mid-way. There's no off button and the error beep would not stop. I had to unplug then reset the cooking options.

Well, this should have been the point that I decided it was time for goodbye; but no... Cuckoo and I continued like this with me trying to coax her and she sometimes obliging. I thought, she comes with a warranty maybe they can fix her. I called the customer service line and got a kind-sounding lady who didn't speak much english.  I finally understood everyone was out at lunch and I should call back.

A few days later I tried again and got someone who spoke a little bit more english. My options were to ship them Cuckoo (I would pay for shipping) and they would then figure it out and ship her back. At this point I wasn't keen at at all in pouring more money into this.

Unfortunately I was 2 days beyond the Amazon return window. I hate the thought of tosing a $100 pot that barely lasted a month; so I may just bite the bullet and send it back for repair. In the meantime, it's just me and my trusty old quart pot and I'll try not to burn the house down. But really, it is very easy to cook rice on the stove.

title: Better rice cooker = better rice
body: I think like most people, I assumed any rice cooker is just as good as the next. Dear God was I wrong. We had the old throw down Oster rice cooker that we've had for years. I think we paid $15 for it at Wally world back when my wife and I first got together, and we made plenty of rice in it over the years.Finally much to our chagrin, it died. It was a peaceful death and we had a beautiful celebration of life ceremony for it, right before we threw it in the trash can. That's when I went on the hunt for a new one. I knew I wanted a slightly larger cooker, since we had felt like we couldn't make enough rice for dinner parties. That was basically my only requirement when I started looking.I had no idea that there were so many rice cookers out in the world, nor did I know you could pay in excess of $500 for one. Who knew?I found out rather quickly that cuckoo was a very widely used and respected brand and slapped down about $100 for this one. Doing a little better than I was 15 years ago, I figured why not.And that's when I realized that I had been eating terrible rice made by a cheap rice cooker all these years. The first time I made rice in this cooker I couldn't believe how much better it was. This thing consistently churns out the best tasting rice I've ever had. I legitimately eat rice at least three times a week now. And I can't believe I went this long eating the gruel that my old cheap cooker was producing.It's got more options than you're likely to ever use. But it has 4 different settings for white rice. Savory is my favorite, even though I takes the longest. There is also a quick rice setting which cooks in a comparable amount of time as my old one. But still makes better rice.I would highly recommend this machine if you're in the market for one. As I said, buy a better rice cooker and you'll get better rice.

body: This is so much better than I expected. Second, everything that is touched by steam easily comes apart for cleaning & drying! Not only that, it has a self clean mode! Then you just take all the steam touched parts out to dry, genius! author: Char
title: The Basics Only: A Functional But Average Performer
body:
The CUCKOO 6-Cup Micom Rice Cooker is a sleek, modern-looking appliance from a brand known for high-end pressure cookers. However, this specific Micom model feels like a "lite" version of that famous technology, aimed at those who just want the basics without the premium price tag.

Why the results are underwhelming:
- Mediocre Consistency: While it handles the simple task of cooking rice, the result isn't awesome. Instead of the distinct, fluffy, and evenly cooked grains you’d expect from a specialized Korean cooker, the texture can be inconsistent—sometimes a bit too soft on the bottom while being slightly under-textured on top.
- Build Over Performance: It looks great on the counter and the interface is easy enough to navigate, but the actual cooking logic (the Micom brain) doesn't seem to "fine-tune" the heat as effectively as higher-end models or even some cheaper competitors.
- Nonstick Inner Pot: The pot is easy to clean and the 6-cup capacity is perfect for small families, but the thinness of the pot might be contributing to that average heat distribution.
- Basic Features: It covers the standard white rice and brown rice settings, but it lacks the "wow" factor that justifies the Cuckoo brand name if the rice quality is just "okay."

author: Keith
title: The Hidden Cost Nobody Tells You About — Stay Away
body:
I wanted to love this rice cooker. Cuckoo is a well-known brand, and at $119.99 it seemed like a reasonable investment. It wasn't.
The fatal flaw: the nonstick coating on the inner pot starts flaking off after just 6 months — and I'm a single person only cooking a couple of times a week. This isn't heavy commercial use. This is the lightest possible household use imaginable, and the coating still failed in half a year.
Before you think "no big deal, I'll just replace it" — replacement inner pots run $50 each. That's $100 per year just in replacement pots for a $120 rice cooker. After two years you've spent over $300 on what should be a simple, reliable kitchen appliance. That's completely indefensible.
Now here's the part that really stings: the inner pot is not covered under the warranty. Cuckoo classifies it as a "consumable item." Read that again — the single most essential component of a rice cooker, the part that actually touches your food, is considered disposable by design. That 1-year limited warranty everyone points to? It won't help you one bit when your pot starts flaking.
And if you're cooking for a family — using this thing daily, multiple times — don't expect to get even 6 months out of the inner pot. You'll likely be replacing it even sooner, with zero warranty protection every single time.
Flaking nonstick coating isn't just a money problem — it's a health concern. Those flakes go directly into your food. That's not something anyone should have to accept, especially when the manufacturer's own warranty policy acknowledges the pot won't last by treating it as a throwaway component.
The rest of the unit has its own shortcomings too. It's non-pressure, which is hard to justify at $120 when competitors offer superior cooking technology at similar prices. The 3-cup uncooked capacity is small, there's no voice guide, and that 1-year warranty — already thin — covers far less than you'd expect.
Cuckoo markets this with phrases like "premium quality" and "superior durability." A nonstick coating that fails under minimal use in 6 months, on a part the company won't even warranty, is neither of those things.
Do not buy this rice cooker. The sticker price is just the beginning. Spend your money on a brand that stands behind every part of their product — not one that quietly classifies the heart of their appliance as a consumable.

author: Aloysius B. Canterbury
title: A Very Great Value Good Rice Cooker
body:
I purchased it used-like new for around $66 from Amazon, mid September 2024.

How it arrived:
Upon opening, there was no visible defects on any of the equipments (cooker, pot, rice spatula, and cup). The cooker came in a cardboard box. The contents (pot, spatula, and cup) was located inside the cooker wrapped in plastic. Everything came clean with no dust, debris, food particles, etc, inside.

How I use it:
I cook 2 cups of rice, wash it, then fill with water until it reaches line indicator for 2 cups of white rice on the soft white rice setting. It always cooks perfectly soft rice in about 40 minutes.
Ocassionally, I will place chicken thighs on top of the rice before cooking and the chicken always comes out perfectly tender and cooked (using the same settings as above).
I have not tried its other cooking capabilities such as steaming or baking so I am unsure how well it performs those.
I use it everyday and cook rice about every 2 days.

I find cleaning the pot and spatula very easy. If I only cooked rice, I add a bit of water and scrub the insides of the pot and any remaining bits of rice effortlessly comes off. With soap if I cooked chicken or something else in it. The inner cover, steam vent, and stagnant water catcher is easy to detach when needed and is very easy to clean by hand.
Washing the pot and spatula in the dishwasher always results in a perfectly clean pot without ever damaging it. Not sure about the other parts.

Size-wise, it does not take too much space on my counter, but it may vary from person to person.

I have yet to encounter a problem or defect in my 6 months of using it. It works just like new from the day I bought it. In my opinion, it is a very great value for money purchase.

author: Juliana Childress
title: Cooks rice well, but a few caveats to beware
body:
I’ll start by saying this cooks, warms, and reheats rice perfectly. From a functionality perspective, this cooker is fantastic. A little pricey, but great.

All of that said, I want to echo a lot of what the other reviews said. It’s pretty massive, so for storage purposes of something that’s frequently used, make sure you have plenty. If you ever open it underneath a cabinet, be very careful. The lid is extremely spring loaded and shoots up fast. I dinged my cabinet the other day. We are a family of 4 and typically don’t ever need more than two cups of rice. We love the cooker’s finished product, but it seems like overkill. Unless you exclusively eat rice as a family of 6, you probably don’t need something this big.

Lastly and probably most importantly, it’s extremely important that you let the inner parts dry out after every use. It’s very easy to disassemble via embedded clips, but the steam and condensation produce somewhat relevant accumulation of water after each use. If you let this stagnant water sit over months at a time, you’ll be steaming your rice in mold. Just beware that a smaller cooker is probably sufficient for the average family.

author: Molly W.
title: A few design changes would make this rice cooker nearly perfect
body:
Cooks rice pretty well, as most reviews state. If you like your rice softer, as we do, you need to add more water, or less rice, than is called for. Because of the fuzzy logic technology, the cooker adjusts the time to have the rice cooked to a set level of doneness.

I like the modern design and small footprint. It does take longer to cook rice than my old Tiger cooker, so definitely pre-soak your rice to speed that up. For 2 cups, it takes about a half hour to cook. For 3 cups (the capacity of the model I bought), it can take anywhere from 45 minutes to an hour, depending on whether and how long you presoak the rice.

Some improvements would make this a nearly perfect rice cooker. First, I really wish it had a retractable power cord like the Tiger models. It's a hassle to have to plug and store the cord somewhere when the cooker stays on the counter.

Second, the inner bowl is black, so it's incredibly difficult to see the engraved water line levels. I literally have to shine a flashlight on the inside of the bowl and tip the bowl slightly to see where those lines are. If the bowl was gray (like my old Tiger rice cooker), it wouldn't be so hard to see.

Third, as other reviews state, when you push the button to open the lid, the weight of the lid tips the entire rice cooker  backward, so that if you're not careful or ready to catch it, the whole thing would tip over. I had read those reviews so I know to use my other hand to stop it from flipping.

Fourth, it would be really nice to have an attachable caddy to hold the rice scoop like other brands. Instead, you have to dirty a plate or bowl to hold the scoop. Also, unlike other brands like Tiger, the lid cannot be pushed and held partway down (not shut) once it's done cooking. This lid can only be completely open or completely shut.

I've only had it a month and only used it about 8 times, so I don't know how durable it will be, especially given the electronic controls, which generally are the first problems that arise in newer technology. I also haven't used it for anything other than plain white jasmine rice. For the price, so far it seems to be a decent investment.

author: ShoppingwEase
title: Attractive rice cooker, good for solo or couple
body:
My review is based on having used the rice cooker twice (successfully). Upfront - I like the cooker. It looks good if I were to leave it on the counter and cooked my rice nicely. It does have a very springy lid, but that’s not a deal breaker for me. I’ve have only tried one setting (which is what I usually use the rice cooker for) and it worked great. Lots of button and options on top - try not to get overwhelmed by them.
Extended review:  I cooked 3 cups (dry) of short grain rice using the White Rice and Quick setting.  The rice cooked just fine and the time was about 37 mins. (A little long IMO, but rice was cooked.) I don’t think I could have made 6 cups (dry) in this cooker.  I fear that it would take the rice over the top, or at least touching the lid and have uneven cooking. My 3 cups already went beyond the halfway mark on the pot. I made 2 batches of 3 cups of rice for my dinner party, but for just me this rice cooker’s size is just fine. I left the rice in the pot on the warm setting and it indicated a time after a while so I know how long it was sitting warmed. Not sure if it has an auto off setting - need to read the manual more. I also need to see how to remove the moisture capture cap in the back since it didn’t easily slide out. I like that the top of the inner lid can be removed for cleaning. Wish it had a holder for the rice paddle.

So you need two hands, one to prevent door from flying and one to press the button that is hard to engage. Finally get it plugged in and the touch-sensitive buttons are not sensitive, so I have to sometimes press multiple times to register a press.

I have used National (Panasonic) rice cookers from the 80s that have lasted 40 years with no such quirks, and somehow this new design just makes things worse. Really makes me wonder how this has thousands of 4+ star reviews. I'm going back to Tiger or Zojirushi where making rice is simple, fast and good. This device just is just annoying to work around, and the final dealbreaker? No spatula holster in 2025. Are you kidding? Who is this rice cooker for even?

I’ve been wanting a cuckoo rice cooker for the longest time so I had purchased it when it had a sale. Looks like we have to return to find a different model ☹️

author: A.R.M.Y13
title: Does the job....
body: This the second Cuckoo rice cooker I have purchased. The first one stopped working after about 5 years. So I stuck with the brand and change the cooker only. TBH I am not able to get the quick cook function to work right. I only use for cooking rice and that is 1 or 2 times a week only thus got this on sale. :-)

author: Cass Robert Callaway
title: Operation buttons stop working after 3 months. Do not buy.
body: Do not purchase this cooker. It is very poorly designed. The press buttons on top stop working after about three months of ownership. When it worked, it was great, but I believe an appliance should last longer than three months. Buyer beware. Very poor quality product.

author: disinx
title: Excellent cooker. Bad design
body: Cooks rice in the different modes very well, but would not recommend. Button placement to open is on the front forcing you to hold the unit still to keep it from sliding backwards if sitting on a smooth countertop. The touch control buttons are on the top of the cooker requiring you look straight down onto the flat top and requires bright lighting as there are no contrasting colors or backlight to the "buttons".

author: lyly
title: Not easy to open
body: I love this rice cooker! It keeps rice warm and perfectly soft. The only downside is the button on the front—it’s not very easy to use, and the heavy lid makes it a bit inconvenient to open.

author: Tnoat
title: Bad lid, pot function was okay
body: The rice cooker was okay. The rice came out great! However, I had to return it because of the lid. When you open it and don't hold on to the lid as it opens, it makes the pot jump. I don't know why the designer for this model did not put in a damper for the lid?? Like if you're going to make it a press and auto-open lid, at least put in the damper to slow the lid down enough so the whole bloody pot doesn't jump! Yes, it still jumps even when the pot is filled with cooked rice!

author: Jay
title: Lid malfunction. Don’t buy!
body: Stopped working after a few months. The display in the lid failed to work, particularly after closing the lid. Looks modern, but don’t get deceived by the look.

author: Margaret D. Langenberg
title: Worthless
body: Does not work. Could not return during window due to car broke down so lost almost $100. DO NOT WASTE your money. Extremely disappointed. Lost and now garbage.

author: Mai Huynh
title: Not easy to use
body: Not easy to use

author: Mika
title: Good
body: Bottom of rice pot scratches/peels. I thought it was from the dishwasher, but I only used the dishwasher once and have been hand washing since. The peeling keeps getting thicker. It's a good size pot, not too bulky. Power cord plugs from the side of the pot. Functions as a rice pot should. Overall good quality. It holds a lot of moisture. So I do tend to leave it open a little after it's done cooking to dry out, just so the pot doesn't mold.

author: Joabella
title: Screen doesn’t work after just a few weeks
body: The screen doesn’t turn on anymore

author: HJ
title: Undercooked rice after less than a year of usage
body:
I've been using this rice cooker for less than a year, & it's already starting to have problems. I've had more than one instance in which the rice was undercooked, despite using the precise amount of rice & water as instructed.

My older rice cooker - which was half the price of this one - never had this problem.

My recommendation: if you have money, go for a Zoujiroushi or Tiger, if you don't, go for a cheap no name brand. Either way, no need to waste your time with this one.

author: myriam castrillo
title: Terrible rice cooker
body: It’s a hit or miss with this thing. I always make 2 cups and always put the same amount of rice and water and sometimes it cooks perfect and sometimes it leaves it super moist that it looks like Risotto. Maybe I got a faulty one?? Very disappointed and now looking to purchase another brand. Waste of money

author: Yen
title: Not as good as expected
body: Taking too long to complete a cooking cycle. just missed the window for returning :(

author: Zahra Ireanna
title: No replacement or brand loyalty
body: I’ve had this pot for a year and it works okay. You can’t replace the inner pot which makes the product ineffective long term. I would look for other models or brands. I’m not happy and this is supposed to be a reputable brand.

author: Potato
title: Overall Pleasant Experience. love the aesthetic. 2 things to note
body:
Gets the job done overall. Rice is perfectly cooked and moist. The functions are all very helpful and I love the timer function that gives an estimate on how much time is left during the cooking process. I got the smaller version for 2-3 cups cooking a day which fit my needs perfectly. Love the aesthetic and overall design.

Two things to note….

When opening the rice cooker by pressing the button to unlock the lid, if you don’t have ur hand on the lid, the lid will open very strongly. With nothing stopping it, the rice cooker basically flips/teeters backwards on its hind “legs” before falling back down into place.

The water reservoir in the back is a little difficult to pop off. And takes some fidgeting sometimes.

author: Amazon Customer
title: NOT made in Korea!! Chinese knock off …
body: From China NOT Korea!!! Replica knockoff … we were wondering why the rice didn’t have that superior Korean rice cooker taste and quality. Sure enough … MADE IN COMMUNIST CHINA!!!

author: Ying S.
title: Not worth a penny
body: Worst pot I've ever had. Trashed it out and ordered a simple cheap slow cooker.

author: Dirk Zuckmantel
title: The electrical function stopped working completely.
body: I purchased this cooker because of all the great reviews.  I used it maybe ten times and all of a sudden in the middle of a cooking cycle it stopped working.

author: BLACKPINK
title: Good size but not the best product
body: I like the size, it is good for 4 people. It is very small compact and looking nice as well. But it doesn’t have any buttons nor on / off buttons so you have to unplug it. It also makes selecting different cooking options harder for my mom without the buttons. Old people seem to have hard time using sensor keys.

author: Amazon Customer
title: Peeling Pot, Unsafe Advice, and Zero Support
body: The outer pot of my Cuckoo rice cooker started peeling in less than 3 weeks. I contacted Cuckoo customer support and was told it was “safe to use,” which is alarming. Paint and heat don’t belong near food. They refused to replace it and showed zero concern for safety. Poor quality, worse support. I expected more from this brand. Would not recommend.

author: Hyun M Lee

body: Easy to use.

author: Amazon Customer

author: Jose & Aleksandra
title: Nice
body:
Cooked rice in it - my husband said it was the best rice I've ever made, - yeeey! Lol. But you have to remember to season it before turning on the cooker, as you can't open the lid midway through cooking, which I found weird at first (I always like to try it mid-way), but it works.
So far, I hate how fast the lid opens, and even if I put the cooker away from the cabinets, it still bounces back and hits them with every opening, I'm scared the top will get damaged very fast.
Other than that it looks nice, quite big, will need to find space for storage.

author: Tanzim Khan
title: Extremely Disappointed – Stopped Working in Less Than 3 Months
body:
I bought this rice cooker in March 2025, and it didn’t even last three months. The first month, everything seemed fine, it looked great and cooked rice well. But then it started overflowing water during cooking, and just a few days ago, it completely stopped working.

I had high hopes for this product, but it turned out to be a major letdown. If I could give it zero stars, I would. Totally disappointed, and I will never buy or recommend this rice cooker to anyone.

author: Wayne Merritt
title: Works great
body: Works as expected

author: Khin Maw
title: Not good
body: It not doable. I didn’t like it at all.

author: M SHOP
title: Cooks Great Rice, Just a Bit Slow
body: This rice cooker does a fantastic job at making fluffy, perfectly cooked rice every time. It's easy to use, and the non-stick pot makes cleanup a breeze. I also appreciate the keep-warm function — super convenient for busy days. The only reason I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is that it takes a little longer to cook compared to other models I've used. Still, the results are consistent and delicious, and for the price, it's a solid buy. Great for small families or everyday meals!

author: Kimberly Garcia
title: Fast rice cooker
body: Cooks my rice very fast and it makes it taste delicious

author: Amber Dawn
title: It seems like it’s all here so overall I think it’s great

author: Apinr
title: Very impressed by a long time Zojirushi owner.
body:
Actually not bad at al for the pricel. I've been swearing by a Zojirushi for the past 10+ years but it's time to replace my trusty rice cooker. So I wanna try something more modern without spending $300-$500 on a newer Zojirushi (plus I never use the rice cooker for anything but cooking rice). This little rice cooker can make a perfect rice with good keep-warm function for my family of three (we always have rice made). I don't know-- maybe the fluffiness and taste of the rice is a little different than my previous Zojirushi but may just be my imagination. Even if it is, it's not $200 better!

Edit: after using it for a few weeks, I have to ding a star for the keep warm function. It’s just not as good as my old Zojirushi although it does advertise that the keep warm is up to 24hrs. More than that and your rice will burn at the bottom like a lot of the old school rice cooker as I found out.

author: Michelle
title: Stopped Working After Two Years
body: I bought this rice cooker in 2023, and it has already stopped working. Very disappointing quality — it only lasted two years. For a product that cost nearly $100, I expected better durability. Unfortunately, the warranty only covers one year. Do NOT buy it.

author: William Leonard

body: It worked well for 18 months and then completely died. Because it has been over a year, I was told the warranty has expired and there is nothing they can do for me.

author: Stephanie Trochez
title: Problematic buttons, unresponsive
body: It's really hard to press the buttons. The rice maker works pretty well, the rice comes out yummy, but the buttons are not it. I'm thinking of returning it for this reason alone. They are unresponsive unless you press really really hard. And even then, sometimes the touch doesn't register. It feels like im going to damage the machine eventually, from how hard I have to press them

author: Stanley Kite
title: Working good but…
body: The rice cooker is working good , little smaller than we expected , and the quick cooking option is little slow compared to my old rice cooker , and the price is little higher too.

author: Carolyn
title: Poor opening
body: When opening the rice cooker, the lid snaps back forcefully and caused the entire rice cooker to become unbalanced. The front of the rice cooker literally goes into the air. It makes it feel extremely cheap and poorly designed.

author: Toughtoy4x4
title: It's okay, but inconvenient.
body:
I bought this rice cooker because my old, reliable Zojirushi cooker became not-so-reliable. It still cooks rice very well, however, the keep-warm feature no longer kept rice at the proper temperature so the rice dried out and became overcooked in half a day.

The new Cuckoo cooker cooks rice very well and it keeps rice at the proper temperature without drying out or overcooking so the rice is ready for serving over a couple of days.

It is, however, missing a couple of convenience features that, I believe, should be standard on any rice cooker. It does not have a handle or any means of transporting it anywhere. I can't even move it to my table if I want to. It is also missing a holder for the rice spoon. This is very inconvenient and I have to have a clean plate or some other surface on which to lay the serving paddle. Both of these features are standard on my Zojirushi cooker, and many other brands I have used.

Lastly, programming this cooker for different rices, porridge, and other foods is inconvenient and confusing. the written instructions do not match with the labels on the cooker top.

I may be sending this back.

author: Shalikina Weeden

body: Other than the menu toggle button being a struggle, I like it. My rice came out perfect! I absolutely love the auto clean feature!! The beep alerts when done are very beneficial.

author: H. W.

body: Makes great rice.  However, wish the markings on the inside of the black rice pot was easier to read.  Also, wish there was a handle to make carrying the rice cooker more convenient.

author: WIWO

Every time I try to open the lid, it slams open forcefully, which feels unsafe and awkward—especially when there’s hot steam involved. Even worse, the entire cooker jumps/ shifts while opening, which makes me nervous leaving it unattended on the counter. It cooks rice fine, but the build and safety issues really take away from the experience.

author: J J K

body:
Terrible product made in China not the South Korea.
Three different hardness of the cooked rice in one pot.
Don't bother

author: Amy [Book Addict Reviews]

body: Can’t even use it. There was no power cord included. Was excited to try it out.

author: Orkhontuul lkhamsuren
title: Too small
body: The description on this rice cooker’s website said it makes 6 cups of uncooked rice and 12 cups of cooked rice, but in reality, it’s extremely small — it can’t even hold 6 cups of cooked rice. Also, the top lid was cracked. I’m very disappointed, so I’ve decided to return it.

author: HF
title: poor quality
body: I have used it 2 months, and. the inner pot is peeling, I tried to contact the customer support, and they said it is not including the warranty, and I need to buy another one. I don't think it's the good support. It does not make sense for me, the innter pot is the important part for the whole rice cooking product

author: Sheila V. Siuda
title: Only less than a year, one star for the look 😟
body: This is a good looking rice cooker, used less than a year and now it doesn’t work at all. Tried to plug in it will show the menu on top but will not turn on no matter what button you press, decided to unplug then plug back in and you’ll see nothing at all… i am not sure what happened, it’s not wet… looks fine but doesn’t work. I wonder if someone has the sane issue.

author: Emily
title: Stopped working after 3 months, Heavy lid, small cook area
body:
small and neat. I’ll try it out for the next three days and return if the product doesn’t fit my need. It’s too small if you’re wanting to cook stew (something I was hoping for). And the lid is to heavy that the whole porridge bounced when I open.

Update* Broken after 3 months of use. This thing started not reacting to any of the button all of the sudden. Waste of money. Do Not Purchase!

author: NC
title: Inner Pot Coating Flaking Away
body: The coating on the inner pot started flaking away, making this rice cooker not usable anymore.

author: mikem
title: I’m changing the rating
body:
I’m changing this to 4 stars.  It’s working fine, cooks the rice well.  I do think the instructions could be better, especially for someone who has never used one before.  A “quick start guide “ maybe.

This does work, maybe I can’t figure it out but it is supposed to be automatic.  So far we have ruined several cups of rice.  The directions are awful.  It seems like you’re supposed to just throw the rice and water in and it cooks.  Then there’s a bunch of instructions on how to cook rice.

author: TAMMY
title: Won’t turn on after a few months
body: Bought this beautiful rice cooker a couple months ago and loved it. We make rice about 1-2x week a most so the size is perfect for a meal for two. However, just after a couple months, the rice cooker will no longer turn on! The digital screen doesn’t show anything at all. So disappointed. We bought this to replace our 15yr old simple one button rice cooker. Guess some things really just don’t need to be fancy, they just need to work.

author: ARSP LINK
title: It’s very tiny
body: Too expensive

author: MzBrandyGrl
title: It’s just ok… Save your money
body: A couple things… the price doesn’t match the product. It’s expensive and not worth the money. The numbers can’t be seen on the inside of the pot. When you press the button to open it, the lid pops up and back making the rice cooker come off the counter making all kinds of unnecessary noise. There’s too many buttons. It does however, make scorched rice. But so does my quart pot. It is esthetically pleasing.

author: Cali
title: good！
body: At this price, I hope it can have more features.

author: Angie
title: Looks and works great
body: Love the clean look of this rice cooker and works great so far. Gave it 4 stars because I feel the button to open the lid is not convenient. I feel like I have to push it against the wall to open it if using one hand compared to the other rice cookers I’ve used which was much easier to press. Overall still  good purchase.

author: Katherine Dahlgren
title: Only lasted a little over a year when…
body: This rice cooker served us well for just a little over a year till it over flowed during a very normal sized 3 cups of rice and 4.5 cups of water batch. During the cooking phase water started bubbling over from the vent and almost instantly the top control panel went out. It was still cooking but I could tell what was happening or if it went to “warming” cycle. I would have expected a little hot water to make the unit completely useless. Now it doesn’t do anything when I plug in or try to select any options.

author: youreajaywalker
title: It’s okay for day of rice
body:
This cooker makes tasty rice. It’s a small minimalistic design that doesn’t take up too much space. However, if you want to make a batch of rice and leave it in the warmer, the quality of the rice goes bad after 30 hours or so.

I wish I could make a batch of rice that would last longer than 2 days. This isn’t the cooker for that. Spend a little extra if you’re looking for something more.

author: Esther Eller

I’ve tried resetting by unplugging and restarting but nothing. I basically can’t tap into the “quick cook” function anymore which sucks.

author: Sib Sib Hlub
title: It’s okay but wouldn’t recommend
body:

But sadly, it hasn’t been a year yet and the warm function is already ruining my cooked rice. After 4 hours the rice starts to smell and turn yellow bc the warm function becomes too hot and starts to overcook the cooked rice that should just be warm.
Do not recommend this particular rice cooker.

title: It’s a litte difficult to get used to

author: Serena

body: Everything seems to be good except it’s hard to see the lines in the pot when making rice

author: Pamela Brown
title: Very disappointed overall.
body:
The instructions for use are a joke.  For sure this item is made in  and whoever wrote the instructions is not well versed in English.

Apparently you can cook six cups of uncooked rice in the pot.  I have tried two and it boils over through the top opening.

It overcooks the bottom which often turns out crusty.
It is easy to assemble and the insert is non stick which makes clean up easy.

Made rice better than some other cheaper cookers but has a long way to go to be worth the price.

author: Lisa
title: Lid is too heavy for the pot
body: Too bad I didn’t read all the reviews, especially the video that one customer posted about the open button and the lid before I purchased mine. I have used it for a few months now and it’s cooking alright. However one must use two hands in order to support the cooker when pressing the open button, in order to avoid the heavy lid to flip and tilt.

author: captain norm
title: Works fine but manual method is quicker.
body:
It works fine, but unless I am making extra rice to freeze, I find my old tried-and-true method quicker and easier.
Rinse the rice, aadd to boiling water, simmer for 13 minutes and let rest, covered and off the burner for 12 minutes.

title: Lots of cons

body: I really like this rice pot for its price point, it cooks well and I like the keep warm feature, it keeps the rice for a few days although I won??t push it past 3 days personally. I??ve played with the customized cook feature and it??s awesome. I like our rice a bit stickier. My only issue with this pot is from day one, as it cooks it releases sticky starchy stream water as it cooks. It covers the lid and runs down the back all over the counter. And if you don??t catch it right away, it dries up to a paste that you have to soak to get off. The water on the cooker will just flake right off the plastic when it dries. But this nasty sticky counter water issue is pretty depressing. I??ve resorted to ??diapering?? it by setting the back end of it on a light kitchen towel and draping the other half of it over the top vent. It works okay, better than doing nothing. My steam vent cap and inner lid are washed every time, so it??s not plugged. I can??t figure it out. But other than that, rice tastes great, easy to use, nice to look at, the rice pot itself is strong and cleans up like a dream, it all comes right out if u let it dry. Truly nonstick!  And it keeps well for a while. I??d probably upgrade to a higher model next time but this size is great for the two of us.

title: Not what I expected
body: I bought this because my old Tiger rice cooker was slowly breaking. My husband and I went according to the chart that was suggested in the manual. We tried many different kinds to see how we can make our rice perfect. I was so excited to try this new rice cooker as it had so many different features. This Cuckoo model failed me immediately. As the rice was cooking (in turbo mode), the rice cooker was emitting this strange burnt plastic smell. That was already alarming. Just after 12 hours the rice has been cooked, all of the rice turned yellow and smelled old, as if it has been sitting for days. I ignored this and decided to give it a few more chances. Even after changing the modes and features, the results were the same. After a week of use, I decided to return the rice cooker. Thankfully, I kept my old Tiger rice cooker, so I??ll be using it until I find another. I was really hoping for long-lasting, white, and fluffy rice. title: This rice cooker from south korea is a TANK. Cuckoo is amazing.
body: My family have always brought Tiger brand rice cooker from Japan which lasted 10-15 years but after these new style of space pod like cookers came out, the Tiger brand from Costco, it would always go bad due to a lack of ventilation and condensation after the second day. I have no idea why the new models does not have a water collecting cup like the previous tiger brand but alas, it was returned. I have heard of cuckoo brand from watching my favorite streamer on Twitch when she did a cooking stream and thus, the person who owns it is a chef. I decided to jump the gun and buy one. Out of of the box, it does look like the newer style pods one however, it has a water collecting cup! This means that the rice will stay good for a week! Sure enough, after cooking it, the rice came out perfect and stayed the same throughout the week! After reading the manual, I activated the "turn off" during night time, but "reheat" again starting at 4am and that further preserves the rice! I have no idea how South Korea manufactures rice cookers but this is the Cadillac of all rice cookers! I will never go back to another brand!Con: the buttons are extremely difficult to press, especially with no rubber feet for resistance. You will have to press in with the other hand holding the back of the rice cooker for resistance. Also, the top flings open when you open it so you should be prepared with the second to gently catch it.Easy start mode: To start cooking, press "cancel" (to cancel the reheat option) and press "cook." Press it again if you want turbo mode (supposedly cook rice faster but I rarely use it). Nonetheless, it takes two buttons (cancel and start) to start the rice instead of a lever like in the older style rice cooker. Takes 40 mins to cook rice. Well worth it.Big enough to feed a family of four.

title: Great Rice Cooker but DOES NOT LAST
body:
This is an excellent rice cooker, especially the "quick cook" option which makes the pot of rice in a much shorter time, even as quickly as 30 minutes - most other rice cookers routinely require 60 minutes to cook a pot of rice regardless of the number of cups of rice.  I gave this a 4 star review only because of one problem - the rice cooker slides to easily on counter surfaces.  This is our second purchase because our first slid off of the counter when we bumped it while wiping down the counter with a cloth.  It hit the ground and the silver colored latch that holds the lid in place when closed popped off and bent.  We were able to continue to use it for another few months but over time, the lid sat more and more open and last week it popped open while cooking so we finally gave up and purchased a new one.  I tried looking for replacement latches online but none are available.  For the new one, I added these adhesive rubber pads to the bottom and the rice cooker does not budge when bumped.  Enjoy!

UPDATE: so we purchased a second CUCKOO because we thought that we broke the locking clip when the pot fell off of the counter.  Well, turns out that the locking clip for the lid is a faulty design.  Our second purchase is having the same problem after a few months.  I included pics.  I cannot find any replacement parts.  I WOULD NOT PURCHASE THIS.  It makes great rice and quickly but after a while, you will not be able to use it because when the locking clip fails, the lid will no longer stay locked down and the rice will no longer cook.

body: Spent 30 minutes unpacking and getting familiar with the unit, then did some basic cleaning of the inside. Followed the instructions and 60 minutes later we had a nice serving of really good white rice to go with the teriyaki chicken. We will tweak our recipe to get the rice just the way we like it, but for the first attempt it came out great! Might even get me to like brown rice if it??s cooked this well. We retired to a rural area that does not have any good teriyaki (my go-to comfort food), so we are learning to make it ourselves, and this Cuckoo rice cooker makes it that much easier. Great product, easy to use and appears to be well-designed and constructed!

No complaints.Edit: 6.5 years now and it's finally time to replace this and it was for the dumbest reason. The top plate has enough wore off of it where it was getting rust. The bowl is available to buy as a part but not the plate above it. Granted I was not careful and often dish washed it. Overall I'm not going to deduct a star though I do wish I can just buy a replacement part and keep trucking along. 6.5 years is a good run. I'll get a fancier Cuckoo and go from there and buy some replacement parts to have around.

author: D...
title: The inner pot is unlined alloy.
body:
This rice cooker makes excellent white rice with no problems. When I made mixed rice, it was delicious but during cooking, the water overflowed to the drain catch. That’s okay, just a little more cleanup than usual.
The dealbreaker for me is that the exterior of the inner pit is not lined with a nonstick coating. As a result, the pot reeks very badly of chemicals or unsealed, raw metal.
I thought the odor would dissipate with a few washes but the smell is even stronger when it gets wet. And as other reviewers noted, the inner nonstick coating is thin and the exterior of the pot can corrode very easily because it is unlined.
I will be going back to a zojirushi. My last one lasted 10 years before I dropped it.

author: Clara
title: Strong chemical smell that won't go away
body:
The inner pot as well as the rice cooker itself has a lingering chemical smell. Other than that it is a good product. I've purchased this exact rice cooker a few years ago with no problem, but the inner pot has a bit of scratches after years of usage so I ended up ordering a new one. It came a bit wobbly with a little squeak when I'd open the lid (it came new definitely); which is no longer an issue. But this chemical smell is very noticeable. I am taking my chance and ordering a replacement. Keeping my fingers crossed as many have said that they did not have this issue.

10/15/21

I've received my replacement and tested it out for two weeks now. I'd like to mention that I don't believe this particular one was new as the inside pot had smudge marks (oily?), and the time on the cooker was running (5:45 pm lol) unplugged like they do once the cooker has been used to make rice. But it looked almost new; maybe new.

This cooker also has a chemical smell, but a very slight one and I think there is a good reason behind that. The inner pot is smooth on the outside; polished? Whereas the other inner pot had a rough feel to it, as though it wasn't polished? sealed smoothly? ... not sure if that makes sense but I did notice a significant difference; chemical smell.

So, while I don't have to worry about the chemical smell so much, the new replacement I was sent has its own issue: the plastic attachment to collect the water from the rice cooker when it's cooking my rice doesn't catch any water at all. Why? Because steamy water droplets decides to stay inside on the top of the cooker, and all over around above the rice that's just been freshly cooked. And I didn't even unplug the cooker. Not a single water drop in the plastic thingy in two weeks because they all like to stay in the rice cooker. This was not the case with the other two I've had previously. Maybe this one is introverted ... hmm ... oh well

title: Such an improvement
body: I bought this to replace a 15 year old Zojirushi micom 4 cup that was starting to show degradation (rice wasn??t cooking well and lots of cleanup). Decided to go with the Cuckoo because several of my mom??s friends had them, and the price was more affordable than another Zojirushi. Wow, what an improvement. This is in no way saying it is better than a new Zojirushi...but it??s a definitely an improvement on my old one. author: Allaya Fleischer
title: Excellent rice cooker!
body: I really appreciate the thoughtful engineering in this rice cooker, particularly the stream collection cup in the back. The top plate on the lid comes off and goes on pretty easily, and is no trouble to clean.  I'm also pleased with the heavy weight of the cooking bowl, which no doubt assists in even coming of the rice. The reheat function is quick and effective, and I particularly appreciate the time cook function, which guarantees my rice will be done exactly when I need it. The insulation is very good, compared to other rice cookers I've used, which keeps the outside surfaces only slightly warm to the touch when it's in use. Even in warm mode, which I use frequently over Shabbat, it doesn't dry the rice out as much as my previous rice cookers.Although I have this rice cooker five stars because it  cook fantastic rice, there are a couple of minor things that you might consider before buying this rice cooker. First, if you aren't familiar with rice cookers, or are not a terribly technical person, it's worth mentioning that the instructions aren't necessarily intuitive, and the English instructions for using the rice cooker are translated (sometimes badly) from Korean. There are many excruciatingly complicated aspects to the rice cooking that you can control, but for most people, simply pressing the "cook" button will work just fine. It in no way interferes with the functionality of the rice cooker, nor the event results, though.Also, in a perfect world, I'd have loved for this rice cooker to have a steamer basket. Unfortunately, you'll have to but one of these on your own, if you're interested in doing any streaming, and to my knowledge, the company does not offer one for sale. Since these things aren't really "standard" sizes, a silicone one might be the best option.Overall though, speaking as an Asian person who takes rice very seriously, I think this is a great rice cooker for the money, especially if you keep a busy schedule and will utilize all the timing functions.

author: A
title: Reliable for multigrain rice, high quality with a few quibbles
body:
My 12 year old Zojirushi neurofuzzy died and I bought this Cuckoo rice cooker to replace it in January 2018.  It's still working great being used almost daily.  Compared to the Zoji, this one doesn't have the steamed ricewater overflow from the top vent the way my old Zoji did, and also does a better job of cooking japgokbap (mixed grain mix to regular rice ratio of 1:3) --- I do a 30 minute soak of the mixed grains prior to popping into the cooker, and it turns out to be perfectly done each time on the mixed brown rice setting.  If you have had Korean food at a restaurant and are wondering what that slightly purple rice with other things is, that's japgokbap, and you can buy bags of the mixed grains to make your white rice a healthier/more fibrous option.

The parts and fit are high quality - nothing creaks or is out of alignment and it doesn't feel cheap.  It's made in Korea which may be important to some because a lot of Zoji are now made in China with questionable quality.

The couple of important drawbacks that I find annoying:

The black pan does not have any handles or any structure to prevent movement, so mixing the rice causes the pan to rotate/move around the base which can scratch the finish of the pan.  The Zoji I had had handles which prevented this from happening.

Because it's a smart rice cooker, cleaning it requires cleaning multiple small parts (the vent tube + cover, the water collector at the back, the removable top lid, etc) that take 10 minutes longer than a cheap no-setting one-tab rice cooker (with just a lid and a pan).  When you're busy it can be annoying especially if you cook rice every day.

Otherwise I am very pleased with my purchase.  I would consider buying one of the more expensive pressure-cooker Cuckoos in the future, but for now this meets my family's needs.

author: Amazon Customer
title: Just okay
body:
I was looking for a replacement for my Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 and purchased this Cuckoo. I ran this side-by-side to compare its performance.

The Cuckoo wins on the following points:
* Cooking time is shorter by like 8 mins
* Rice is ever so slightly better both in the turbo and normal modes, although it's so slight I can barely tell if it's better or the same.

The Cuckoo loses on the following points:
* The base was not even so it was slightly wobbly. Not a good impression of quality. I couldn't live with that wobble so I decided to return it for this reason.
* The lid was overly forceful. If I press the button, the lid swings open so forcefully that the entire unit lifts itself up. It's quite annoying. The Zoji's lid opens up quite gracefully.
* The buttons are hard to press. At first I thought it was defective because the buttons weren't responding when trying to set the clock. I had to really dig my fingers in to activate the buttons holding the unit with both hands (otherwise the unit would just move as I'm pressing the button)
* The line markings on the inner pan are indentations only (hard to read) and only on one side (hard to level the pot to line up the water level to the markings). The Zoji has white markings and on opposite sides of the pot.
* No handles on the inner pan. The Zoji has it and it's easier to hold.
* The spatula holder is not as good as the one on the Zoji
* There is a condensation cup in the back where you have to empty every now and then. The Zoji does not need one.

So overall, it does cook rice slightly quicker and a hair better than the Zoji. However, I think the Zoji is the better rice cooker.
