body:
Had this for several months.  We love that the vent and "cover plate" can be detached and cleaned.  Our last rice cooker's "cover plate" did not remove and would get gross between the cover plate and lid.

It has many cooking options for steaming a variety of other foods (standard with most cookers), and the instructions say you can control the sticky and fluffiness of the rice (unusual for cheap cookers).  However, we have not tried these cooking options (other than cooking standard white rice) to give a proper review.

Only wish for this rice cooker is for a retractable cord.

UPDATE: the little white plastic "drip catch" in the back broke when we tried to remove it to clean it out (after every use per instructions but, never looked dirty).  I would be docking .5 stars for that since it was silly for it to break so quickly but, we do not really think that was a very useful feature anyway.  I give 4.5 stars instead of the 5.

author: Joe
title: Wow! Not can match this appliance!
body: A few years ago a bought a Haan floor steamer. When I got that, it was the first South Korean appliance that I had ever had experience with. Everything about it was built like a tank and had the best components. The quality of the steel and plastics and even the sheathing for the wires was top notch. It's never let me down. When I started looking into a rice cooker I noticed this brand and had seen it in the Korean market where I buy my groceries. But until I started looking for this type of appliance, I did not know that this brand was the top selling brand in Korea. I am an American and proud of my country, and until I had this appliance in my hand and saw how it was put together and the fit and finish of it, I did not understand why it seemed like its price was high in comparison to other fairly high reviewed rice cookers by other manufacturers like Panasonic or Roval or GE. But now that I see it and tested it out and saw how it was put together, I can say that nobody holds a candle to So Korean engineers and manufacturing quality control. This thing is stunning! If America could make something of this quality and at this price, we would have every right to crow about it. But sadly, we don't. Literally, this thing is a Mercedes or an Audi vs a late 70's Chevy. I am sad that we no longer have the skills and standards to produce objects of such quality as this. I really wish that we did, because we would have every right to boast if we did. If you order this, just look at it. Look at it under scrutiny. Look at the inside lining of it, even the bottom of it, areas. It ordinarily looked at. It's a frickin' work of art! I would easily pay 75% more for it after seeing it in my hands. I am even thinking of checking out a Kia now that I've seen this. No joke, I know that you will be impressed if you but this. I think that this should be held up as a standard for the rest of the appliance world to look at what could be achieved and presented to customers. Unless there is some bizarre fluke, I am fairly certain that you will look this thing over in silence and feel a curiosity about what else could be coming from South Korea. I know I am going to start looking into it.

title: Beats my Zojirushi $426 Induction Rice Cooker. Cuckoo is a brand I have switch to and will never look at back Zojirushi again.
body: Beats my Zojirushi Induction Rice Cooker that I paid $426, that only lasted me 2 yrs. before the non-stick coating on the pot started to come off. It was such a big disappointment, not only because I spent $426 but because is no longer made in Japan with Japanese parts, instead they switch manufacturing to China. When I bought my Zojirushi Induction Rice Cooker, I didn't think they would of switch from Japan to China, since I own a 1982 Zojirushi Rice Cooker that works great still. Zojirushi is now a brand that I no longer consider High-End anymore.There are lots of different brand on the market today for a rice cooker. They range from $15 - $800. Since I no longer consider Zojirushi as a brand I want to buy anymore, I was debating between the Cuckoo & the Cuchen rice cookers. Those are the top brands of rice cooker in Korea. I went with the Cuckoo CR-0631F because since I have never used a Korean Rice cooker before I wasn't sure what the outcome would be.To my surprise, this Cuckoo CR-0631F give the one of the best rice cooking results since my Zojirushi Induction Rice cooker that I replace it with. The non-stick coating on this Cuckoo CR-0631F is different that I have seen. It has a metallic bronze color, yet it repels water very well. It was very easy to clean this pot, just using soapy warm water and a soft sponge, no scrubbing needed at all.The only thing that I need to get use to with this Cuckoo CR-0631F rice cooker is the terms they use for white rice, it's called GLUTINOUS. One of the best features that I really like about this Cuckoo CR-0631F is the KEEP WARM, my rice stays warm for 72 hrs before it starts to look a little yellowish. Now that was just a test to see how long it can keep warm. I usually only make 2 DRY CUP (4 total cups of cooked rice) and finish it within 1 to 1 1/2 hrs.This is one of the BEST rice cook money can buy and it's a brand that I have finally replace the old trusted Zojirushi (use to be made in Japan, now it's all made in China with low quality materials). I have had this Cuckoo CR-0631F for about 6 whole months before writing this review. Enjoy my video of this Cuckoo CR-0631F rice cooker.

Each batch comes out fluffy, slightly chewy, and evenly cooked, with grains that stay distinct—never mushy or dry. The result has that subtle “spring” and balance you typically expect from restaurant-quality rice.

The fuzzy logic technology makes a real difference, automatically adjusting time and temperature so the rice is always cooked to perfection.  It cooks a variety of rice types reliably and consistency with minimal effort.

It’s also very easy to use—just set it and forget it. The keep-warm function maintains moisture well, and the non-stick pot makes cleanup simple.

author: Jayski J
title: Does the Job, but Missing Key Items
body:
This rice cooker was received as a Christmas gift, and from a pure functionality standpoint, it does cook white rice well. No complaints there. white rice comes out evenly cooked and it’s simple enough to use for basic needs.

However, the bigger issue was the condition of the product upon arrival. Although it was purchased as new on Amazon, it was very clearly repackaged or previously opened. Several standard items were missing from the box, including the measuring cup, rice spatula, steamer basket (if one is supposed to be included), and the warranty card. That was disappointing, especially for a gift.

The included user manual doesn’t help much either. It’s extremely basic and provides little to no guidance.. If that’s all you plan to make is white rice, you’ll be fine. But for anything more nuanced, brown rice, jasmine, basmati, quinoa, couscous, oatmeal, etc… the manual offers no guidance at all. Water ratios and cook settings absolutely matter for different rice and other grain types, and none of that information is provided.

I also tried to find additional resources directly from the manufacturer, such as a cookbook, recipe pamphlet, or even online content. Unfortunately, there’s nothing helpful. The company website doesn’t offer recipes or cooking guidance, and there’s no official presence on YouTube, TikTok, or similar platforms to fill in the gaps. This is surprising, especially since comparable Japanese rice cooker brands often include recipe booklets or at least basic cooking charts.

Does this matter? Yes, a rice cooker should help you cook more than just basic white rice, and the lack of accessories, documentation, and learning resources really holds this product back.

Overall, the cooker itself works, but the missing items and lack of support make this hard to recommend unless you already know exactly how to cook different types of rice on your own.

author: Cynfelyn
title: Still Great After 3 Years of Regular Use
body:
After using this rice cooker for more than three years probably 2-4 times a week, I thought I should share my experience.
Pros:
The main thing is how well the non-stick coating has held up.  I only use a silicone spatula (not the hard plastic type scoop included) when scooping out the rice and I use a water spray and soap to clean, while only using a sponge when necessary (which is rare).  Normally I have to replace the cheap rice cookers in less than a year because the non-stick coating fails, but this one is still going strong.
The quality of the rice it produces still just as good and consistent as when it was new.  For Calrose rice, the "white" setting and water line comes out light, fluffy, and sticky (I prefer Nishiki brand calrose over other ones I've tried).  Japanese short grain rice is perfect on the "white" setting with the water up to the "brown" level inside the bowl.  I don't bother soaking, the extra water seems to be all short grain rice needs with this cooker.  Brown rice takes a while, but is nice and tender with the "brown" setting and water measure line.
Cons:
Didn't include a steamer basket.  I got a silicone steamer insert that I use when I want to steam Chinese Sausage and veggies to go with my rice.

With how easy a solution the only con has to me and how important quality and non-stick is, I think this fully deserves 5 stars.  Though, do get a steamer insert.  As long as you've not cooking more than 2-3 cups of rice and you don't crowd the steamer basket, it does a great job.

author: Robert
title: Well-made rice cooker. 5 stars.
body:
CUCKOO 6 Cup Rice Cooker (CR-0632F)

Pros:
* Price _ Costs less than half the price of Zojirushi or Tiger brands.
* Materials _ The cooking pot is solid, robust, heavy duty.  Molded differently, I could imagine it being used as a shield for medieval battles.
* Build quality _ Construction quality is top-rate.  Everything fits and feels right.
* Instructions _ Well-illustrated, clear instructions written by someone who is conversant in English (not the AI-generated nonsense sometimes produced for foreign products).
* Automatic warmer feature _ Upon completion of the cooking mode, the rice cooker automatically enters the warming mode.  The timer begins immediately, counting up the number of hours in the warming mode.
* Rice cooker _ Cooks a perfect pot of rice!

Cons:
* Slow _ 42 minutes (compared to 25 minutes for my previous rice cooker).
* No backlight _ Makes it difficult to see the LCD display, especially from a distance.
* No "on" light for regular cooking modes _ Relies on circulating LCD graphics to show that the pot is on, which because of the lack of backlighting is difficult to see.  I really wish that there was an "on" light when the rice cooker is in use.  Ditto for warming mode, I would have liked an indicator light for the warm mode.

Additional remarks:
* I purchased the silver model.  Note:  Amazon erroneously labeled my review as being for the pink model.
* I only use the rice cooker to cook rice.  I probably will never use any of its other cooking features (slow cooking, steaming, etc.).
* I haven't used the quick cook feature.  I'm generally not in a rush.  However, if I ever try it, I'll update this review.

EDIT:  9/27/2025, I tried the quick cook (white rice) setting.  It took 27 minutes +/- 1 minute to cook plus another 10 minutes recommended wait time for cooling down.  I tasted the rice at that time and it was indistinguishable from rice cooked on the regular cooking cycle.  So, the quick cook setting saves about 15 minutes.

Note:  All cooking times were done at 70°F to 75°F at sea level.

author: Vance N
title: Just right - solid pick
body:
I had a tiger and it finally broke. I wasn't looking for something fancy, more so consistency, durability and reliability. I bought a replacement Zojirushi (nothing fancy but simple warm/cook button design) and found that it was a bit cheaper in quality (likely a China factory vs Japan model), the inner lid was so flimsy. I tried the Panasonic with no LED screen but 4 or 5 modes, button panel but did not like the fact that you could not remove the lid or the inner lid for cleaning but to it's credit it worked well despite that. I heard good things about Cuckoo so I decided to try this even if it was fancier than I'd want but for the sale price I couldn't argue.

Pros:
- cooker pot was heavy duty! The weight and thickness was solid so probably accounts for their claim of cooking faster and evenly via induction plate
- inner lid can be removed for cleaning
- inner lid thicker than other major brands
- diameter aka footprint is compact compared to the tradition rounded with the handled lid. Certainly is a more streamlined design.

Cons:
- I just don't like the "slick" touch panels with a button behind them because eventually the plastics begin to crack and separate. It happens to all after so many presses (washers, dryers, dishwashers, etc). Functionally it's fine, I just know what's coming in the future. Never had to worry about that with the simple warm/cook toggle lever.

I will update when the panel plastic cracks but otherwise, it has left a better impression than my past Tiger - japanese made, Zoji - china and Panasonic - japanese. Again, this is compared to the basic+ models, not the fancy touch screen wifi enabled Alexa controlled blah blah blahs. If you want a just fancy enough workhorse that is easy to maintain and use, this is a good pick.

Update: After some uses, I confirm it is a solid pick. The rice comes out consistent and the maintenance is easy enough. I tried the firm and sticky rices and they come out as expected. Your water level is key, I find a good rinse and a sit in the water for 10 min before cooking get it just right what I like the texture to be. I haven't tried brown rice or anything but I have tried steaming frozen dumplings and shrimp shumai - nice job (clean it down asap after the shrimp shumai to prevent the seafood taste to leak into the next batch of rice - I may just use something else but good to know this can steam that too). A good tip for that is put a light wipe of oil on the basket so dumpling or shumai delicate skins won't tear.

author: Jamazon
title: Gorgeous and Cute - Math is Bad
body:
I bought this, opened it up to inspect, and carefully re-packaged to return.  Hear me out.  The rice cooker is very cute, the colors pop, looks like a hot little Alfa Romeo sports car.  The red is a beautiful McLaren sports car speckled sparkly red.  It's very nice.  It's a well respected brand name.  Many of my friends have $200+ Cuckoo rice cookers, for years.

But the math doesn't work.  Math never lies.  The 6 cup hash mark, as others have said is a bit hard to see, is 3/4's way up from the bottom. Rice doubles in size when cooked.  There is no way this will make 12 cups of cooked rice as stated.  I think this can make maybe 7 cups of cooked rice.  Should take care of a family of 4-5 for a dinner.  If this size works for you, then I would recommend it.  For the price, the looks, brand quality, I just wish it was a bit bigger.  Our family of 3, we use the InstaPot.  We wanted a convenient rice cooker for when we have 10+ guests.

author: Renee Aubuchon
title: An acceptable rick cooker
body:
I was curious about rice cookers, and this one was on sale, so I bought it.  While some families have used rice cookers for generations, they were new to me.  I had always made rice in a pan in on the stove and thought- well, that's as good as it gets.  Well- it's not.  I have found that it is easier to cook rice with a rice cooker, and the rice tastes better.  Somehow it is tender and yet has texture.  From now on I will be using a rice cooker to cook rice.

One of the things I don't like about this rice cooker, which was also pointed out in a review of rice cookers, is that the measurement indications on the inside of the pot cannot be read.  The pan is dark and the measurement indicators are dark, and it would darned near take a flashlight to be able to read them.  I bought a rice cooker cookbook that gives the appropriate measurements for all kinds of rice, and will be using that book to guide me.

The other thing I didn't like is that there is no steamer basket for this rice cooker.  A rice cooker that comes highly recommended and has a steamer basket also costs more than twice what this one does.

If you are looking for a rice cooker that is not very expensive and does a good job of cooking various kinds of rice, this rice cooker is an acceptable choice.

author: brooke18
title: Not non-stick!
body:
The whole point of a rice cooker is to make it effortless to cook rice. Not if you have to soak the pot for several hours, scrape the thick layer of rice stuck to it, and spend a good half hour scrubbing it (with a scrubber meant for non-stick cookware, of course).

There is no time countdown and it doesn't beep when it's done so if you're not watching it carefully, it will end but keep the rice warm. This is a terrible feature because all it does is make the rice overcooked and stick even worse to the bottom of the very not non-stick pot. When you cook white rice, it spews a sticky mess everywhere. I put a folded piece of paper towel over the steam vent, which allowed steam but captured the mess. But instead of going all over the place, it now dripped down the sides of the pot so I still had a mess to clean up.

When you press the lid to open the cover, it pops open with great force, almost tipping the rice cooker over. The feet are not non-skid so you have to hold it with one hand while pressing the buttons as it moves around. The curved front where the buttons are makes it more difficult to press the buttons.

Also, the manual is almost useless as it's written in broken English and a lot of it just doesn't make sense. Why not label it white rice instead of glutenous? I had to research what all these terms like GABA meant. Ridiculous. This rice cooker is not marketed for western culture, obviously.

The buttons don't always respond. Have to insert pot before plugging it in. If you plug it in first, it knows there is no pot and a symbol appears on the screen and you can't get rid of it. Even after you put the pot in, it won't show the menu settings (even if you press Cancel) so you have to unplug it and plug it back in. The menu defaults to whatever you last cooked so if you're now cooking a different type of rice, you have to press Cancel. But it doesn't work so you press it again. Then unplug it, try again. Then it seems to work if you press and HOLD the Cancel button.

The screen is terrible font and dim so very hard to read. Helps to use a flashlight. Took forever to change the time and once I did, I couldn't adjust it (when I realized it was off by a few minutes). You can't shut it off completely, so the battery is just going to run down as it's on 24/7.

If you have a big family and you eat a ton of rice, this is fine, so long as you don't care about squinting to divine the measurements, and the price point of this unit is most bargainous. But compare to the Zojirushis, which have white measurement markings you could read from outer space, and whose measurements start at half a cup of dry rice??to me this is well worth spending more. This Cuckoo is absolutely not a bad unit, it's just these little details that make it terrible for me. body: The instructions are a bit difficult to understand, but once you realize the included measuring cup is 1/2 cup and the measurements inside the unit for water are measured in cups, it becomes easier to understand. It uses a 2:1 water to rice ratio. Simple.To use it add in the rice (1/2 cup per person works with my family), pour in the water, select the rice type using the ??menu?? button (glutonous is short white rice and mixed is long grain rice), then press ??cook??. author: Dr. Sean Henry
title: Very nice nice entry-level Micon rice cooker, but ...
body:
I eat a lot of rice, steel-cut oatmeal, and grits (a.k.a. polenta). I had cooked these successfully up until now in my beloved 8-quart Zavor multi-cooker, but using such a big appliance is overkill to cook just a cup of dry rice or grains for a few servings in a single household. I chose this Cuckoo Micom (micro-computerized) rice cooker for its reputation and brand loyalty, great reviews (on CNN), size and multiple cooking functions. Plus it really looks cute on my counter!

This 6-cup unit is perfect for me and doesn't take up too much space on my counter. It works well and I like the way it cooks rice, but the instruction manual with bad English translations isn't always helpful. And exactly how user-friendly is the menu setting named "glutinous" for the USA market?  I had to search the internet for the best ways to cook my favorite rices, grains, and porridges in this device, but there is an active Cuckoo community out there with answers, and things are pretty simple.

Like other reviewers have noted, there is nothing on the bottom of this very light unit to keep it from easily sliding across your countertop like a figure-skater. You may have to hold the unit still with your extra hand while you press menu buttons. There ought to be skid-proof rubber "feet" on the base of this unit to prevent that, as is the case with many other small kitchen appliances.

I never got this cooker's clock setting feature to work correctly because the "Min/MyMode" button never changed over from "My Mode" to let me set the clock minutes, even after holding down the button for several seconds following the instructions. Fortunately, the minutes on the clock upon unboxing were only 2 minutes off from my local clocktime.

If you are older, like me, make sure to wear your reading glasses and turn on the overhead kitchen lights to operate this unit. The small digital screen has no backlighting and there is no light indicating that the rice cooker is even on, but you'll know in a couple of minutes when it starts to make a few cooking noises inside and lets off some steam and rice aroma.

This is a very nice "entry-level" Micom rice cooker that looks great on the counter, doesn't take up a lot of space, has a lot of versatile cooking functions, and produces its advertised results. I recommend it for those reasons. However, I am already upgrading to a pricier Zojirushi pressure induction heating rice cooker. Of course I (we) could all save money by cooking rice and grains the old fashioned way by sweating over the stove, but I love the convenience of a "hands-off" rice cooker, plus it gives off less heat in my hot summer kitchen!

body:

That said, I had to get my reading glasses to read the display.  The display may be sharp enough but the color and lack of contrast make it difficult to read.  "Glutinous" was the choice shown on the display.  I pressed "Cook" and it showed on the display that it was working.  I couldn't hear anything to indicate that it was working.

It took more than 30 minutes for 2 cups of rice but that's not unusual.  They were cooked nicely and there was no scorching or any other problems.

Since it has the micro computer controlling the cooking, many options are available to make brown rice and blends just as easy.

body:
Within mere months, the cook pot's teflon-like coating started to bubble up, corrode, and lift off. Unfortunately (for me) I discovered after eating full pot of cooked rice!!!
Reading other feedback, I see this is a common occurrence; just ONE MORE INSTANCE of Chinese manufacturers "ruining" good Korean designed products.
Not only is the coating faulty...but this cooker is plastic---most of Korean made Cuckoos are aluminum. Seems the Chinese manufacturer chose to squeeze a few dollars (maybe even cents) more profit by not using Korean quality materials.
And FINALLY...I was able to get refund through asurion warranty (thank you, Pastor Fritz)....now I see amazon is NOT OFFERING asurian coverage on this cooker!

****RUN QUICKLY AWAY from this cheaply built inferior cooker that can actually poison you!!****

Cuckoo makes many models in Korea still---they are much better in buildability, value, longevity....and safety.
Since amazon "chooses" to hide country of origin...simply contact Cuckoo USA and they will verify which models are indeed Korean made.

title: One stupid design flaw that keeps this from being a perfect rice cooker
body: As the title of my review suggests, there is one major and, honestly, stupid design flaw that keeps this rice cooker from being my all time fav: there is no place to put the rice paddle. Come on. That's so silly. It's a sleek, red, space-ship like design but you couldn't bother to design a holder or a place for the paddle? Seriously??? Even the cheap $11 aroma rice cooker I used to own had a little handle you could stick the paddle in. Come on cuckoo, this is ridiculous. Another minor design flaw that isn't as bad but is inconvenient is how hard the lid flips up -- the force of the lid flipping up, even with a full pot of rice, is so strong the whole rice cooker jerks backwards a little bit. So you have to keep your hand on the lid and then press the lid open, guiding the lid and not letting it just flip freely.

author: Lionel
title: Not as good as other Cuckoos.
body:
My gf has this one: https://www.amazon.com/Cuckoo-Electric-Heating-Cooker-CR-0631/dp/B007D5J6AK (model CR-0631) and it keeps rice warm/fresh for up to 2 weeks.

I bought this one (CR-0655F) thinking it would be the same. But it's not. It only keeps rice for 2-3 days before the rice starts browning and becoming dry. Still edible, but not nearly as fresh as the pink Cuckoo that I linked above.

Furthermore, it takes forever to cook - at least 25 mins for just 1 bowl of rice. Turbo mode shaves like, 2 minutes at most. Still takes forever. Even my old black & decker rice cooker is much faster, and sadly enough I go back to using that when I am in a rush.

Don't be fooled into buying this one just because it's Amazon-approved. The pink one (CR-0631) is by far the better rice cooker.

author: Bloom W.
title: ... upgrade our cheaper rice cooker and it's been a great change. It cooks the rice evenly and QUICKLY
body: We've had this for a few months now after I decided to upgrade our cheaper rice cooker and it's been a great change. It cooks the rice evenly and QUICKLY. I was surprised how fast it gets the job done. We mostly just use the white or brown rice option but apparently you can also do mixed rice and more. We have used the steam cleaning option that seems to have done a good job. I like the timer and clear screen. The buttons are in both English and Korean. It keeps the rice fresh for us for about 2 days. After that, the leftovers have to be thrown out. I like that it's not loud, doesn't bubble or spill, and we can store it in our cabinet after use. It's actually really easy to clean the inside because the pot is light-weight and soft. We have never had a problem so far with the rice sticking to the pot. The alert to let you know the rice is done is just a little beep. I wish the instructions were more clear about rice:water ratio because the English translation isn't perfect. Also, it's better to do a minimum of 2 servings. We've tried 1 and the rice just doesn't cook well.

author: adrian
title: Don??t expect fast cooking
body: I bought this particular rice cooker for the look primarily.  It is a beautiful addition to my kitchen.  My current rice cooker, an aroma brand stopped working after 2 years with it.  I figured since this one was over twice as much in price it was going to be amazing.  Now I may be wrong but I thought the purpose of a rice cooker was to save time?  The time rang for cooking just 1 cup of rice is about 35 minutes.  More rice increases the time to almost an hour. My previous  one cooked less than 10 minutes.  This one has a turbo mode but it recommends you presoak your rice before using. And even then it knocks the time down just a few minutes.  And on top of that when I came to check on the cooker the water vent had spewed droplets everywhere!!! So be prepared to lay a piece of paper over it!! I need to clean the outside of it immediately.  I don??t have too much experience with rice cookers so I don??t know if this is the norm.  But if this much vapor spurts with 1 cup of rice I can only imagine with a full pot.  I may go have to find my plain white 30 dollar rice cooker from before.  Not fancy but works way better

body: The cooking pot's interior coating started to peel after 4 uses. Luckily, this occurred 2 weeks before the "return/refund" deadline. If not, we would've been stuck with a new rice cooker that could potential harm our family if we used it. After owning two rice cookers manufactured in South Korea, I believe this particular Cuckoo rice cooker is a hunk of junk, because it's made in China. Although this is a Korean brand, it's not made there. Make sure to look up the models online to see where they're manufactured. We'll be making sure our next one is made in South Korea. author: Borimir4ever96
title: Such a step up from the old school style
body:
Oh man this rice cooker. I've always used cheapies and thought they were fine. I was so wrong and am glad I got this one. Not even that expensive (compared to Zojirushi) but makes restaurant quality rice. Can make a little or quite a lot of rice. The top liner comes out to make it easy to clean. White rice, brown rice, oatmeal and even baby food come out amazing. Would no brainer buy another if this one broke. It cooks pretty quick, maybe a bit slower than my "traditional" rice cooker but that is the cost of rice greatness.
It lacks a timer due to the "fuzzy logic" feature but takes a predictable amount of time. Takes like half an hour for white rice. GABA rice takes like an hour but it is incredible. Keeps temp well after it is done and everything on it is really high quality - the lid, the vent, etc. I could see the buttons eventually failing but they haven't worn at all so far and we've used it 100+ times.

author: Todd Guidry
title: Makes nicer rice than my previous cooker, but takes longer
body:
We bought this on a Black Friday sale because the boys are reaching their teenage years and the 3-cup cooker we got from walmart wasn't making enough anymore. Wanted to get one that was of high quality and reputable brand. (Anecdotally, wife and I started a GLP-1 and now 3 cups is plenty, for now).

Has WAY more functionality than I need at the moment. Various types of rice, porridge, steaming vegetables, etc. Has a large capacity pot that lets you steam vegetables if you'd like. Haven't tried veggies and rice at the same time. Probably not advisable, but would be cool. Have had 0 instances of rice burning. It usually comes out just right. If you leave it on warm for a long time with the lid open, the bottom and sides may get a little scale-y, but that's not a design flaw. Absolutely no water leakage either.

Biggest gripe is that it takes a LONG time to cook rice. IDK if it's the additional space it needs to heat up or what, but it takes close to 30 min to get it cooked. And the timer only starts with ~10 min remaining. Makes it hard to plan dinner timing. That's why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5.

author: JinSh
body:
Took a while to get it. “Glutinous” function here isnt meant for “glutinous rice”. Because there is no “regular rice” button so the button for “glutinous” is really for regular rice.
So far, I’ve cooked couscous (glutinous function) and it came out perfect.
Today, I made Hainanese chicken rice. 6 uncooked cups of rice yield a full pot (cooked rice to the brim - see photo).  I used hot broth instead of water when I cook the chicken rice. No burnt base. No spill over . Rice turned out good!

The spout does emit a lot of steam so I used a cereal box (cut open to shape like a cone shape hat) to cover it as it not only blocks the steam from going everywhere under my countertop, it also absorb the steam.

I wish it comes w a steam basket so you can use the steam function.

For those comments who complained and had videos showing the liquid spewing everywhere is BECAUSE THEY ONLY COOK ONE CUP OF RICE. It will happen to ANY rice cooker if you only cook 1 cup or very small amount of rice. Suggestion if you are alone or don’t need to cook for so many diners, is to cook more and then save the leftovers in the fridge. Leftovers overnight rice makes great fried rice.

The rice cooker takes up little space (compared to many others I’ve shopped) for a 6 cup rice cooker! Very good if you have limited counter top space.

The machine rocks back when you press the open button- whether with or without food in the pot. See video.

My biggest complain is the markings inside the pot are very hard to read. I need to put on glasses to use this rice cooker! I hope they will change the markings to something more prominent like other competitive brands.

The instructions suggests not to rinse the rice in this pot. I guess it saves the teflon from overuse.

body: I bought this particular rice cooker for the look primarily.  It is a beautiful addition to my kitchen.  My current rice cooker, an aroma brand stopped working after 2 years with it.  I figured since this one was over twice as much in price it was going to be amazing.  Now I may be wrong but I thought the purpose of a rice cooker was to save time?  The time rang for cooking just 1 cup of rice is about 35 minutes.  More rice increases the time to almost an hour. My previous  one cooked less than 10 minutes.  This one has a turbo mode but it recommends you presoak your rice before using. And even then it knocks the time down just a few minutes.  And on top of that when I came to check on the cooker the water vent had spewed droplets everywhere!!! So be prepared to lay a piece of paper over it!! I need to clean the outside of it immediately.  I don’t have too much experience with rice cookers so I don’t know if this is the norm.  But if this much vapor spurts with 1 cup of rice I can only imagine with a full pot.  I may go have to find my plain white 30 dollar rice cooker from before.  Not fancy but works way better

author: Spark
title: Great rice, but the CR-0655F controls are a dealbreaker (returning)
body:
I bought the CUCKOO CR-0655F and, on pure cooking performance, it does a very good job. The rice comes out consistently well and the results are what I hoped for.

The problem is the user experience. The touch buttons are difficult and frustrating to use, and the LCD screen is not backlit, so in normal/dim kitchen lighting it’s hard to read what you’re selecting. The labels/buttons also don’t have great visibility against the dark red body, so I found myself squinting and second-guessing settings.

What pushed it over the edge is how the unit behaves when you press the controls. There isn’t enough grip/stability, so it slides along the countertop when you push a button. I often had to use two hands: one to hold the cooker steady and the other to press the buttons. That gets old fast.

Bottom line: the CR-0655F makes good rice, but the controls and visibility make it annoying to use day-to-day. I’m returning it and switching to something with clearer, easier controls.

author: Johnny P
title: Cuckoo 6qt Rice Cooker
body:
I haven't had a need for a rice cooker, mainly cooking my rice on the stove top.
After many long work nights and busy days with kids, and many youtube videos on one pot meals, I bought this rice cooker. Just a simple, no fail cook/warm button. None of those with a million cook options :).
(It's important to know that these rice cooker cups that comes with the rice cooker are NOT your standard 1 cup size, it's more like 3/4 of a regular cup size).

I was pleasantly surprised at how quickly it cooked my rice, especially my sweet glutonous rice where normally you would have to soak for 4-6 hrs to overnight. I was extremely impressed at how quickly and cooked thru it was in such a short amount of time. I have tried making hainanese chicken and it turned out perfectly. My new favorite go to! I've also tried various rice and chicken one pot meals, even steaming sweet potatos and it comes out perfect everytime! I love that the design is not bulky, durable, and also love the color. It's a keeper for me!

author: john a.
title: Translation issue, capacity incorrect
body: Edit: I have received the rice cooker and have been using it for about a month on a weekly basis. It's great! It's Korea's number one brand for a reason, and unlike Zojirushi, Cuckoo actually makes affordable models. You won't regret this purchase, just keep in mind that you will need to learn the ratios. I have included an explaination that I believe will have you cooking perfect rice from your first try. I is not a 6/12 imperial cup capacity cooker. There is an Asian industry standard 180ml (.76 cups) cup which comes with the cooker. By my math, the rice cooker is 4 cups dry, 8 cooked, measuring with US cups. I'm still very satisfied, I just wanted to fight false advertising, which in this case I think is just a translation issue. If you use the provided cup, you'll be fine. If you lose it just remember when the instructions say cup they mean 3/4 cup or 180ml, then fill water to the line inside which corresponds to the number of (180ml) cups you use.

I've had this rice cooker for 1 year and it is extremely easy to use and perfect for people who don't need any of the special features that increase the price significantly of other rice cookers. It makes rice and keeps it warm, that's it.

author: Sandy B.
title: MADE IN CHINA---not Korean quality. Very misleading. YOU WANT KOREAN QUALITY---BELIEVE ME!
body:
Looks to me that Cuckoo is playing the "slight of hand" in both the packaging and 'LACK" of manufacturing info posted on Amazon. Notice in pics I've posted....THIS COOKER IS MADE IN CHINA....which is exactly opposite I was told by Amazon.
The branding and packaging SHOULD be easier to determine "country of manufacture." And both Amazon staffer I ordered through....and a posted question stated this unit "MADE IN KOREA!"
****NOT*****
Made in China.
Cheap little cooker---no "Off switch"....plugged in it is on warm. Couldn't cost but a few cents to include off switch. But typical cost cutting apparent in most Chinese products....and anyone can buy much cheaper cookers with these features on Amazon for $15-$20. I would pay $50 for Korean made cooker...but not Chinese made.

Not happy....

Will be sent back....due to misleading info....the fact it is virtually hidden in amazon post....and the quality of Chinese made Cuckoo's are inferior. I've owned one before. Lasted half year.

Amazon SHOULD make sellers post country of manufacture.
I'll try one time more to buy a KOREAN Cuckoo....then I'll simply quit wasting time and money buying on Amazon....and simply buy local---where "country of manufacture" in easily seen.

C'mon Amazon---treat customers like we actually matter!

Without us----you cease to exist.

author: Loring
title: When is a Cup not a Cup?
body: I??m giving this rice cooker 2 stars because while it works, the product title is incredibly misleading. It claims to be a ??10-cup?? rice cooker, which led me to believe it could handle 10 standard U.S. cups (8 oz each) of uncooked rice. In reality, the included measuring cup is only 6 oz, which is not a standard cup measurement. That means this cooker only holds about 7.5 standard cups of uncooked rice, not 10. I found this out when my rice cooker finished cooking and half of the rice (in the top) was dry and undercooked and rice had expanded into the steam ventNowhere in the title or main description is this difference clarified. You have to dig deep into the manual to find that they??re using ??rice cooker cups,?? not standard kitchen measurements. For anyone planning meals or bulk prepping, this discrepancy makes a big difference.Manufacturers need to be more transparent. If you're buying this thinking it can handle 10 U.S. cups of uncooked rice, it cannot. It??s frustrating and feels like a bait-and-switch.

body: It can cook rice a little better than my instant pot but not the best result. I can cook better quality rice in a casserole on the stove and so much faster. Markings on the pot is useless as it's hard to see. But even if it's marked with contrasting color I would not use it as it resulted to very soft rice. I always use equal ratio for rice, 1 cup water to 1 cup rice and the markings tend to have more water. The Set and preset options are very confusing and the manual doesn't really helps. author: J Chin
title: dead after 8 months
body: This was our first fancy rice cooker. As a family of 5, we eat a lot of rice - 3 times a day. We had our last one for 10 years when it finally died. I decided to splurge on a fancy one, one that can do more than just cook rice. At first, it was great. The rice came out perfectly. We made white rice, brown rice, quinoa, porridge and it all came out perfectly. But just a week ago, it died, in the middle of cooking rice, it died. No more lights and because it's completely automated, there wasn't a way to trouble shoot. We followed the guide to see if it was user error but honestly, we didn't abuse it in any way. I had high hopes for this rice cooker but alas, we have gone back to the brand we had before. Maybe simple is better.

author: Henry
title: Good enough for a starter might doesn't quite have all the features
body:
It's a good basic cooker, despite it naming itself "Smart Rice Cooker". It doesn't even have an internal clock so you can ask it to cook fresh rice by X. It does have delayed cooking so you either have your rice cooked much earlier or get good at timing. The other complaint is as others have mentioned really hard to see markers. This is only a problem if you don't have enough lights so use those flashlights on your phone and that helps a lot.

For the price it's good, and at the end of the day it made perfect rice and didn't require me to fuss about settings.

I did love that I can control the temperature of Keep Warm function. Also the overflow water tray is great. I wish it had more of an incline so that the water would drain even with the least bit of water but it's pretty good.

title: Manual sucks, missing key info, hard to figure out
body: The thing cooks efficiently, but the manual is missing key information in several respects and seems to require the user to know things like ratios. The buttons are not intuitive. While the English in the instructions is clear, the instructions manage to be singularly unhelpful. You'd think they would tell you how much rice and water to use in different modes to get to the desired quantity and style. But no. That would have been a step too far. I just wanted a multipurpose rice cooker - I wasn't trying to practice the scientific method. Once I figure out how to use it the hard way I am sure it will be fine. But it seems they were trying to do too much in one machine and missed key data points (give us a table please showing ratios, people) such that I found myself using Google to operate it. I should have got a simpler cheaper model. Waste of money.

author: MBernstein
title: Solid Product Once Fixed, Terrible Customer Service
body:
The lid of this product was broken from the get go. We didn't think anything of the lid not staying closed without the pot, but after a few uses we noticed the gasket wasn't flush and the little pins were bent. I called customer service and ended up going through the following sequence:

-Call number from Amazon chat, no answer
-Go through insurance plan we happened to purchase, find out its still under warranty and they gave us the correct number
-Call number, it ends up being the West Coast US number and I need to call the East Coast US number
-Wait another day for them to call me back and send them tons of details about my order, zero integration with amazon and very manual
-No response to confirm they received my info, called back and they said they will ship it out next day from NY

It has been over 3 weeks and I still have not received a replacement lid, nor a shipping number, nor an update. When you call the number, you usually get someone who speaks a foreign language. I ended up fixing the pins myself and reattaching the gasket, but for the price, you should go elsewhere.

author: C. Kim
title: Disappointed... Get what you pay for
body:
We've used many Cuckoo rice cookers in the past and were looking forward to this one, esp since the price was so attractive.  Unfortunately, we essentially got what we paid for.  Here are my list of product deficiencies, in no particular order:
1) the cooking (inner) pot is very light.  Maybe made out of aluminum.  But more than that the nonstick coating is very skimpy.  Within a week, already the bottom of the pan's coating has scratches.
2) the menu buttons design on the top of the lid is poor.  When closing the lid, more often than not, one of the buttons gets pressed and resets the menu settings
3) rice & water level markers on the inside of the pot is incredibly illegible, even with flashlights shining on it
4) even with the correctly matched water level (say for 4 cups of rice) rice tends to be dry.  we prefer ours fluffy/sticky and have not yet been able to accomplish that despite several attempts to compensate with more water
5) on the PLUS side, the handles on the cooking pot is convenient as is the removable inner lid & steam spout for cleaning

Very disappointed that the best part of the rice cooker is these 2 features.  Returning this one and after having learned our lesson, we will look for one that costs several times more than this.

author: HL
title: Makes delicious rice
body:
After doing many research about rice cookers, I’ve decided to give Cuckoo a try. However, I can only this product a 3 star. One reason is because the rice cooker came damaged. The clear container in the back that traps water when opening the lid is slightly cracked. Not sure if it’s just manufacture defects or it’s damaged through shipping. Another reason is the water level is so hard to read. The inner pot is in the color black.The words and numbers on the inner pot is black too, which make it hard to read when trying to measure the correct water level. Also, I feel like the buttons are not very responsive, especially the cancel button. Have to press many times for it to work.

Now, let’s talk about the pros of this rice cooker. It has many modes to suit your needs. It also have a delay function of when to start cooking. Unlike other rice cookers, Cuckoo cooks the rice evenly. Also, the look of this rice cooker is very clean and modern.

author: jon
title: Does the Job Very Well
body:
I love to cook. I have restaurant experience from my youth, and I'm usually in the kitchen six nights a week these days. Even when I travel, I rent a house instead of booking a hotel room so I'll have a kitchen. The one thing that's always given me trouble is rice. Maybe a third of the time, it comes out okay, but the other two thirds, it's either crunchy or too wet and soggy. I've tried less heat, more heat, less water, more water, and every trick I could find online to correct the problem. The exact method that worked great last time results in crunchy rice this time.

Enter this rice cooker. I followed the instructions, went about cooking the rest of our dinner, and when it was time to plate the meal, the rice was waiting inside, cooked to perfection. It could not be easier, and it doesn't take very long at all. Cleanup is easier than expected. I thought there'd be more parts inside, but it doesn't really add any more time to washing dishes. Honestly, my only gripe is that I didn't get one of these sooner. Even if you don't have issues cooking rice, just freeing up the rest of the stove is super convenient. I highly recommend this to anyone thinking about getting a rice cooker.

author: Jenn M
title: Good rice cooker
body: This is a good rice cooker & steamer. Normally, I don't like to get single use appliances, meaning appliances that really have only one purpose. Rice cookers being the most common. I prefer having multi-use appliances, so that they don't just sit on a shelf in my kitchen or pantry. However, I really like the large capacity of those rice cooker. I also like the easy operation (measure out the rice, water, push the button, & let it sit). I like how easy everything is to clean as well, as all of the pieces either come out, or they come apart easily, & they can be hand washed or thrown in to the dishwasher. I also like that this can be used as a steamer for things like tamales or pot stickers (though it's not technically recommended, unless you deodorize the cooker before cooking rice in it). It is on the pricier side of most of the rice cookers that I have seen, but I still feel that it is a good value. I also like that the user manual gives you instructions on how to cook the rice so it will come out sticky (chewy) or softer. Overall, this was a good choice for me. Although, it does take up quite a bit of counter space, so this is not something I would recommend for anyone who is looking for something that is going to be a space saver.

author: Michael
title: Missing A Key Feature
body: We??ve been using the Cuckoo CR-1095 10 Cups Basic Electric Rice Cooker and Warmer for a couple of weeks now and as much as we??re impressed with how well it cooks rice, it??s missing a key feature for which I feel compelled to deduct a star from the rating.  The directions explain that when the sensor detects the rice is cooked it will automatically switch to warming mode and to wait 15 minutes before opening the cooker.  Well, there??s no buzzer or alarm to alert the chef that the rice has finished cooking or warming.  So if you aren??t right next to the cooker when it switches to warm mode there is no way to know when the 15 minute countdown began.If the goal of the design was simplicity, they missed the mark by not providing an audible signal for when the rice is ready.  That said, if you pay close attention and notice the cooker has switched from cook to warm, wait the prescribed 15 minutes while it finishes cooking on warm mode this makes perfect rice every time.  We did find that we prefer to add a little extra water to get a more sticky consistency with the jasmine rice we enjoy.

title: Massive Rice Cooker
body:
This rice cooker is HUGE. I didn't realize how much space on my counter it would take, and if I had looked at that in advance, I would not have gotten this. I only make a few servings at a time, so if you are like me, please read the sizing on the listing before purchasing. I kinda regret getting it myself with my very limited kitchen space.

Past that personal oof, I found that making rice in this is so easy and clear. The instructions help a bit and the measurements of rice to water are easy to keep to.

The bowl is anti-stick, so cleaning is a cinch and washing the rice in a separate bowl prior to cooking will likely keep that anti-stick for much longer.

There are only two modes, cook and warm. Basic but really all you need to get started. It automatically switches from cook to warm.

The included basket, paddle, and scoop are lovely.

All in all, if this were half or even a third the size, I'd swear it up and down. This is just so big, it would only make sense for a minority of households.

author: RCH
title: This is a great Rice Cooker for the money
body:
I own two of the Zojirushi Commercial rice cookers but needed more production capability (cooked rice).  I was relooking my options (the Zo is more than $400 for the 20 cup commercial).  I found this Cuckoo model and did a bit of research.  The Cuckoo brand is Korean and is considered to be a top of the line cooker.

Pluses:  Half the cost of the Zo Commercial cooker.  50% more production capacity than the Zo  (30 cup vs 20 cup) per cycle.

I bought one of these and used it for about 10 days (we do a 50 pound bag of rice every morning).  Both Zo's plus the new Cuckoo helped.  After a week, I ordered a second of these Cuckoos.  (both of these together cost less than a third zo).

I really now prefer the Cuckoos to the Zo's.  For us, the capacity of the Cuckoo is perfect (max volume before the lift from the pot becomes too heavy).  The fact that there is a third indicator light (shows cooking, steaming, and warming) rather that the two for the Zo (cook and warm) so you don't have to time your warming light to estimate steaming time.  When the Cuckoo leaves steam and goes to warm, the rice is ready.

I can't speak to longevity yet because the short time I have owned them.  I can say they make perfect jasmine, basmati, and sushi style rice, and do it well.

date: Reviewed in the United States on April 15, 2024
author: Adasterix
title: Straight forward high yield rice cooker
body: From the product description, this rice cooker is intended for making large batches of rice typical for events or scenarios where dozens of people are being served.  It is not quite up to full kitchen duty for a professional restaurant where operation would be needed non-stop during the day, but for daily use at a bed and breakfast or hospitality service or banquet this cooker can really shine.The build quality of this cooker is quite good.  The lid latch is well designed and secures reliably.  The metal casing has a nice brushed steel finish.  The inner cooking pot has a good quality non-stick coating and the pot itself feels sturdy and durable.  The included plastic spoon is durable and does a great job at grabbing cooked rice.  The included silicon ring mat does a great job at preventing rice from overcooking and fusing to the bottom of the pot.  The bottom feet are plastic, and do not have rubber soles, however due to the size of this cooker I did not experience an issue where it slid around on my countertop.Operation of this rice cooker is simple, measure rice and water according to the instructions included with the cooker, then press down the cook latch to start the process which from there is fully automated. No additional steps are needed. The cooker has measure marks embossed on the pot portion to help make these measurements quickly. They are marked at 10, 20, and 30 cup ratios with matching marks on where to fill water.  A simple ratio that seems to work if being more precise is 1.5 cups water for ever 1 cup rice.  I tried this on a small batch of 2 cups rice to 3 cups water (4 servings) and this cooker did really well.  It will automatically bring the water to boiling temperature then switch to steam mode where excess moisture is let off through a steam vent at the top.  Additional excess moisture is also captured in a small removable clear plastic bin near the hinge of the cooker as needed.  For this small batch, this overflow was not needed.  The resulting rice quality was perfect.  I did have a bit that stuck to the silicone mat, which should be removed as soon as cooking as finished.  This is likely due to not washing the rice quite as much as was needed, as starches can "glue" the rice down if not washed thoroughly.  But overall, I am very pleased with the results even in smaller batches and look forward to using this for large events (or cooking several weeks worth of rice for home meals).  This is a great product that is simple to use and clean.  It is a little large for typical home use but can still work if there is space set aside for it and if rice is a staple of the family diet.

author: HouseCat
title: THIS IS THE BEST RICE COOKER! MUST BUY!!
body:
If you are looking for a Cuckoo rice cooker (you already know this brand is great!), this one has one of the most safety measurements, induction heating, pressure cooking, broad cooking functions, can speak Eng/Kor/Chi, and stainless steel coated pot and lid. I did lots of comparisons between models and brands before I decided to get this. 6-cup is good for a family of 3-4. If your family is bigger, consider getting a 10-cup. If you don't need to use that many functions, you can just throw rice and water in and press Pressured Cooked. Done!

ANYONE HAVE A PROBLEM WITH YELLOW OR SOGGY RICE, be sure that you open the lid as soon as the rice is cooked and stir it thoroughly to let the moisture/water out. After that, you can close the lid and let the rice stays until you are ready to eat. You basically have to stir the rice like that with any cookers anyway. I tried the rice once after 5 hours and it was still really great. My family has multiple cookers and sometimes they can keep the rice for days.

I got this rice cooker at a such amazing deal from Amazon Warehouse! Hope it will stay for years.

I still use the porridge button because when my mother cooks congee, sometimes she makes it watery and sometimes she doesn't, so I've had both ways. When you first start the rice cooker, it is in Korean but you can change the setting to English. It has a built in battery for emergencies like a power outage or if you accidentally unplug the machine while it's cooking, it will resume its cooking when it's plugged back in. I usually keep my rice cooker unplugged and each time I plug it back in, the English setting is still there. Make sure to check out where the rice cooker is made from because I've noticed the cheaper Zojirushi/Tiger brand is made from China. I was told by my mother to never buy a rice cooker that is made from China because they break down faster than the original one. Well if I'm going to spend over $100 on my rice cooker, I might want to make sure it last for a long time.

author: Madison Stemm
title: Amazing rice cooker! Cooks sweet, sticky rice super fast!
body:
UPDATE: I've had this for half a year now and I still love it. I've almost always got rice cooking or sitting in Keep Warm in the Cuckoo, and I've still had no issues. I love how fast it is with plain sticky rice, and the GABA setting for brown rice makes brown rice that tastes *awesome*. I haven't tried the dough fermenting setting yet, but I think I'm going to this weekend. It's definitely something I'm interested in.
At any rate, I wholeheartedly recommend this rice cooker! It's one of the biggest workhorses in my kitchen, and I really don't have any big complaints with it after 6 months. If you're willing to spend a big chunk of cash on a rice cooker, you won't be disappointed with this one!

*******
tl;dr: I was torn between this and the Zojirushi induction heating pressure cooker rice cooker, so I bought both. I liked the Cuckoo better! I liked the tactile buttons, low spatial profile, and dimpled scooper with the Zojirushi, but the rice from the Cuckoo cooked faster, came out sweeter and stickier, and the bowl was much higher quality (from my understanding, the Japanese version of the Zojirushi cookers have a similar high-quality bowl, but the American versions use a thinner bowl). The Cuckoo also lets you customise the end-product of your rice a lot more! You can't go wrong with either brand, but the Cuckoo won me over in the end.

I don't write reviews very often, but I love this cooker and I wanted to add my two cents about it!

I've had a low-end micom Zojirushi (the Zojirushi NS-LAC05XA) for something like four years. Before I bought it, I'd only used the cheap Black & Decker and Aroma rice cookers that burn out after a year, and dry out rice after it's been sitting for a few hours. The micom Zojirushi was an absolutely incredible upgrade! Suddenly, my rice came out evenly cooked, soft, fluffy, and lasted for DAYS on "keep warm", which was amazing since I was living alone and it was annoying cooking small portions of rice at a time.

For that record, that Zojirushi is still going strong, and I'm going to be giving it to my parents, who still just use a Black & Decker rice cooker. I still maintain that was probably the best kitchen purchase I ever made as a college student! I just upgraded because I wanted a larger rice cooker, and I was really curious to try out an induction heating and pressure cooker!

Anyway. Once I knew I wanted an induction heating rice cooker, I started agonising about which one to get! I'd never heard of Cuckoo before, but it seemed to have a strong following. From what I could tell, they had been in the pressure cooker business for years, whereas Zojirushi was a relative newcomer to that technology. It looked like an all-around fantastic rice cooker (not to mention looking properly futuristic with that white and steel body!) and had some cool modes (like nurungji cooking mode, so I could make proper sungnyung without using a pot!). The equivalent Zojirushi (NP-NVC10) had a similar set of features, though I couldn't find any information comparing the two. I was torn. I'd developed a bit of brand loyalty to Zojirushi from my experience with their rice cooker and thermoses, but the Cuckoo seemed really interesting. What was I supposed to do?

I bought them both, of course!

So after using the two for a few weeks, here's what I have to say comparing them:

CUCKOO PROS:
* FAST. Regular white rice cooks in under half an hour (and it even has a TURBO MODE that cooks it even faster, more like 15 minutes!!) whereas the Zojirushi takes over an hour. The rice isn't necessarily better with the Zojirushi, either. It comes down to preference, but it's less sticky, more granular, and the flavour is a little more grainy, but I think it's less sweet. Personally, I prefer the Cuckoo's rice flavour.
* STICKY. I like sticky rice, it makes it easier to eat with chopsticks, it's chewier, I just like the texture more. Rice in the cuckoo is a lot stickier and softer.
* ADJUSTABLE. Every cooking mode (glutinous rice, sushi rice, GABA brown rice, nurungji, etc) all have the additional "My Mode" customisation that lets you adjust the heated soaking and steaming times to make rice sweeter or softer! This lets you dial in rice to your preferred texture, and it's fantastic.
* DURABLE. The Cuckoo's pot is a LOT more heavy duty than the Zojirushi pot, which feels paper thin by comparison. I don't know if that results in better rice, but thicker cast-iron metal would definitely result in more even heat distribution, so I'd assume that would reflect in the rice. As a more damning point, the Japanese version of the Zojirushi model evidently has a much thicker pot. It sounds like this American release may have a thinner pot for more cost-effective manufacturing (and most people probably wouldn't know any different anyway.
* INFORMATIVE. The Cuckoo has a really nice touch during the cooking process: it updates when it begins steaming the rice, when it releases the steam, and when rice is complete. The Zojirushi just tells you when the rice is done!
* CONSIDERATE. The Cuckoo goes into "Night mode" after 9pm, when the brightness on the screen reduces, and the volume of the voice lowers. That's really nice!! The cable also winds up underneath the body so you don't have excess cable floating around your counter, something the Zojirushi doesn't have. ALSO, the pot has plastic handles, whereas you'd be better off waiting for the Zojirushi pot to cool down before you try and pick it up to clean. Trust me, I've burnt myself.
* CLEAN. The Cuckoo has a fantastic option to auto-clean and sterilise itself. I used this when I first got it, and I'll probably be using it once a month to make sure everything is all clean. On top of that, there's a little spill-over reservoir in the back for collecting condensed water that drips down when you open the lid. That's nice!
* VERSATILE. Besides being able to happily cook oats (something the Zojirushi's warranty official advises against), it even has an option to act as a regular pressure cooker! Considering an electric pressure cooker is usually at least one or two hundred dollar, this is fantastic.

ZOJIRUSHI PROS:
* TACTILE. Physical buttons! That's a gimme. Definitely not a dealbreaker, but it makes me happy.
* CLEANER. The included rice scoop is SO MUCH BETTER. It has little bumps on the spoon so rice doesn't stick to it. It's way better at non-stick than the Cuckoo's scoop.
* EFFICIENT. Extended Keep Warm mode. After 12 hours, the temperature drops so the rice doesn't dry out.  You can manually adjust the keep warm temperature on the Cuckoo, and I believe it reduces the temperature overnight, but the manual isn't entirely clear on that. Actually, the Cuckoo's manual isn't that great in general, which leads me to my next point:
* LOCALISED. Much proper English manual. The Cuckoo's manual is kinda sloppy Engrish (with some funny things, like one point where it informs you that you can adjust the voice to be "woman, English, or Chinese"), and the recipes in the back are all in Korean =( The Zojirushi's manual is a proper localisation, with English (!) recipes! The recipes seem more westernised though.
* STRAIGHTFORWARD. Simpler cleaning. The steam lid has a push-release button, whereas the Cuckoo's lid has to be unscrewed.
* ADORABLE. Cuter notifications. When the cooking begins and ends, it plays 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star'. The Cuckoo just informs you that rice cooking will now begin, and plays drums when steam release starts, and then plays some Cuckoo theme song when the rice is ready. It's kinda weird, but cute too.
* MODE-IER. Adjustments to make rice harder/softer/normal (I think this uses variable pressure settings). I wish the Cuckoo had this! Other modes include rinse-free rice, steam-reduce rice, and umami mode -- but in my comparisons, bumping up the soak time to level 3 in My Mode seems to be the same as Umami Mode!
* SMALLER. Lower profile body, easier for storage

Overall, the Cuckoo definitely suits my needs more, by far. When you get right down to it, I like the way the rice tastes more, I like all the possible adjustments, I like the higher-level visibility of cooking progress, and I LOVE how much faster it is. The Zojirushi has lots of nice little touches, that make it a better operational experience, but the Cuckoo definitely seems like the superiour rice cooker. Hands-down, between the two I'd recommend Cuckoo every time!

...I'm going to miss hearing Twinkle Twinkle Little Star, though =(

author: Susan
title: Makes amazing rice. Taste and texture highly improved. Def upgrade from basic rice cooker!
body: This is an amazing rice cooker. Quickly learned not all are built or work the same. Yes, there is a small learning curve. IE you don't just measure the rice, wash the rice, and flip a switch. However, the taste, texture is substantially different. Who knew! I do now lol. Additionally, the manual is extensive, it walks you through everything and then some. I love the turbo cook which cuts down the time (if you are in a hurry?) to about half regular. I started small and just cooked plain white (short grain) sticky rice. Paid attention to the USE THE CUP it came with, as cup measurement is different from USA. Washed the rice, added the water, it didn't look enough? Took a leap of faith, closed the lid, locked it ( pressure), pressed the right button and off it went. The fun thing was a voice telling you when it's beginning to cook, that steam will be released and then it's all done "stir the rice." I can see where in the future maybe I won't want her help any more, but for now it makes me smile. Really and delightfully heavy pot, very easy to clean. OH, there is also a sterilize/clean function. Which did have to google? Found out it's two cups of water, and yep, press the button. Cooked brown rice too, without soaking, which can be definite challenge. It was soft, but with body and texture and delicious. Going to try buying the Korean or Japanese addition of 12 plus grains (1/4 cup to 1 cup white rice). To learn more about adding protein (beans) and fiber. Will also say that I waited after deciding this was the one I wanted, and purchased it through Amazon warehouse (like new) for substantially less than manufacturer price and even less than refurbished. I feel now I've raised my standard of living! grin.

author: Frank & Celia Zou
title: Awesome Cuckoo Rice Cooker!!!!
body: My wife, who is Korean, had long talked about wanting to get a new rice cooker.  Many of her friends had a Cuckoo brand and loved them, so with Christmas coming up I figured this would be a great chance to get her one.  Although this had no ratings yet, and was a new model, I took a chance on it and got this one for her.  I tend to have a history of buying her things that she wonders what I was thinking about when I got it for her, but with this I hit a grand slam!  We installed Cuckoo's app on her phone and set the thing up that way, which took only a few short minutes to do.  Now I will say that when you plug this thing in it will speak to you in Korean, so for the non-Korean speakers don't be surprised.  You can set it to English if need be, so don't let that put you off.  The front panel is in English as well, so you won't get lost in trying to figure out the controls.  She finally cooked her first batch of rice today and couldn't get enough of it.  She is fairly picky about the quality of her rice, but this thing blew her away with how good it came out.  Although this thing is pretty expensive for what many would claim is just a rice cooker, my reply would be that not all rice cookers are created equal.  This machine is made to get the most out of the rice you cook, and on that point it is top notch.  Unlike our old cookers that cook from the bottom, this thing does it differently, so the rice comes out much better.  For those that eat rice regularly, like my wife does, you will love this cooker, or most any of the Cuckoo brand cookers.  For the person who only eats it every so often, this would most likely be an overkill and not worth the money.  My wife's previous cooker was 10 years old, so I expect her to keep this for just as long as that one, so for me the money was very well spent.  Given the different types of rice my wife makes, this thing just can't be beat.  Her old one did a satisfactory job on them, but this one takes rice cooking to a whole new level.  My wife and I couldn't be happier with this!!

author: ccpff
title: Hi-tech, high price, but super high quality rice cooker
body:
Our old rice cooker was on its last legs after 16 years, so we saved up to get one of these new hi-tech rice cookers. We were wrestling between a Cuchen and a Cuckoo - and from what we were told, they are very comparable. We did read some reviews that stated the latch on the Cuchen that holds the inner lid piece did have a tendency to break, so we opted for the Cuckoo, which holds the inner lid with a circular metal latch.

The instruction manual is horrible and a pain to decipher. Takes some focus and effort - but eventually one figures out how to use this thing. Be aware - it comes out of the box speaking Korean - so you will want to navigate to English. Most of the useful rice cooking functions are easily accessed and most others we won't even bother looking at.

The rice does cook very fast and well. The induction heating along with the pressure cooking works wonders compared to our old machine. The same rice we have been cooking for years came out more flavorful and with much better texture. Definitely made a believer out of me.

author: Hermit
title: Mind-blowing rice from a brilliantly designed machine!
body:
If you enjoy rice and perfectly prepared rice (I mean PERFECTLY), this amazing machine is the one. I have never tasted such incredible rice in my life, and I have had a couple of higher end Japanese fuzzy logic machines over the years.

The machine is well built and looks like a beautiful, curvy space ship complete with a blue LED control panel. It's extremely well-made, with solid, hefty stainless components. The inside pot is also substantail. I am truly blown away. I would love to see more of these in the US market -- they are remarkable and far exceed their competition.

It even speaks! The voice helps you navigate, as the machine is rather complex. The default language is Korean, so I recommend changing the language as your first step if you are an English speaker (it's not intuitive to do this, so reference the manual).

PROS: Life-changing rice goodness! It's well made and cooks brown, mixed, white, sushi, glutinous and gaba rice. It also rises and bakes bread and cooks soup and porridge. A count-down indicator lets you know when your rice will be done cooking. The voice provides helpful information and has day and night volume controls. Settings are highly customizable, from cooking speed to rice softness. The operation is quiet except when steam is vented near cooking completion (you hear a short burst as steam releases). And, it has a cleaning cycle. It's also easy to clean manually. It's a machine you can grow into as you learn its various functions.

CONS: This is not for someone who enjoys an on/off cooker experience. I think reading the manual is critical to understand this sophisticted machine -- and the manual is not always understandable as there are translation errors or sentences that are not entirely clear. So there will be learning and fiddling (though I think that's half the fun). There aren't a lot of supplemental resources online either, so you need to be the adventurous type if you want to make more than simple white rice. It's also an expensiv machine. While I think it's well worth the investment, if you honestly cannot distinguish between well-prepared and regular old cooked rice, this machine would not be worth your time or money.

title: Rolls Royce of Rice Cookers
body: I have always had the basic Zojirushi rice cookers.  I decided to upgrade since my old rice cooker was just not up to par anymore.  I just made my first batch of rice in this today and it is the best rice I have ever tasted!  I made a mix of white rice and brown rice.  Not all rice cookers are created equal as the prior reviewer states and he is right!  The heating element is not only on the bottom but around the sides as well.  The cleanup is super easy since the inside is all in one piece with no crevices to clean under.  The under-lid comes apart for easy cleaning.  The inside pot is sturdy and thick.  This rice cooker is quite large and oval shaped.  This is definitely pricey but well worth it for making rice and other dishes since this is also a pressure cooker. The controls are easy to navigate and this makes the most perfect rice ever!  Looking forward to many years of deliciousness.

Surface has is a bit of grove so I think it won't scratch while cleaning. Inside pan is a bit heavier than last one.
In addition, it has NFC which you can use your Android phone - download app - and set few things initially.
However, I found this NFC is least used feature.

Except those changes, basic functionality was pretty much same.

However, I have noticed it keeps rice wormer much longer and keep it fresh.

for sure, it does produce a quality rice cooked ( Sticky rice ) and my Korean mother-in-law loves it.

author: Charles NYC
title: IN THIS ESSENTIAL WAY, IT BEATS ZOJIRUSHI
body:
In America, Zojirushi has been the well-deserving gold standard in rice cookers for a long time, and I had used their highest end pressure cooking model for quite a few years with excellent results. But I had one serious regret after buying it, all because I didn't check the specs before purchase: Zoji's very expensive pressure rice cookers are essentially no faster than the much cheaper non-pressure models. White Japanese rice is still close to an hour, brown rice almost 90 minutes and GABA rice clocks in at about 3.5 hours. I ended up making rice--especially brown and GABA--much less often that I wanted because the cooking time would delay dinner too long, especially during the work week.

When I first looked at the specs for this Cuckoo Pressure Rice Cooker, two things blew me away: first, the price! Wow--it makes Zoji look like a bargain! But second, the SPEED: white rice in under a half-hour (with an even faster "Turbo speed" available) and brown rice in about 50 minutes. (GABA, however, is not that much faster at 3 hours.) For that kind of speed--which meant I would use my rice cooker a lot more often--I decided to sell my Zoji and take the price plunge on the Cuckoo. And it was SO worth it!

The first thing I noticed was build quality--the Zoji was perfectly fine, but this Cuckoo is built like a tank and it's big. The smaller 6 cup size, which I have, is as big or bigger than the Zoji 10-cup. As for speed, it was sometimes even faster than the specified times.

But speed would mean nothing if either taste and texture were compromised here, and that's not the case here. In fact, the GABA brown rice is the best rice I've ever tasted at home, period. As for white and brown rice, I'd call it a draw with the Zoji. Some may have a preference for one or the other, but that will be a matter of personal taste rather than a true qualitative difference between the two machines.

So why four stars and not five? There's one area where Zoji trounces the Cuckoo. Because Zoji has been serving the American market for so long, it's easy to find tried and true instructions for cooking virtually any kind of rice you want to prepare. Cuckoo, by comparison, is a relative newcomer to the U.S. market, so that kind of information is non-existent for their cookers. I've been using Zoji instructions for wild rice and other non-Asian varieties, but results are hit and miss because they are very different machines. Another sign of this newness to the American market is the English language instruction manual, where the clarity of directions leaves a lot to be desired. I'm pretty technically minded and still found the learning curve steep. Once you get the English language navigation on the rice cooker turned on, it gets a lot easier--but just changing the language requires googling for instructions on how to do that.

So there you have it: the mostly excellent summary of what you get with this Cuckoo rice cooker, along with its few flaws. Whether it and its price tag are for you is only something that you can decide. I hope you find my review helpful in making a buying decision.

author: Rick
title: Excuse me stewardess... I speak Korean
body: This one requires a translator.  Seriously!  Just to restate, this is a rice cooker.  I found the operation and controls not at all intuitive.  The instruction manual reads as though they simply copied the Korean instructions and pasted into Google translator.  Much of the instruction doesn't make sense because of the bad translation.  No kidding, it will take you at least 5-10 minutes just to figure out how to get the cooker to stop yelling at you in Korean.  As far as the rice goes, it was good but didn't find it to be any better as far as texture and quality compared to my 10 year old Panasonic.  I primarily purchased this for white rice and to cook steel cut oats in the morning.  THIS WILL NOT COOK STEEL CUT OATS (SCO) via the porridge setting!  Regardless of the ratios of oats to water I could not keep the contents from overflowing.  Each attempt resulted in a huge mess all over the cooker and my countertop.  Apparently, PRESSURE rice cookers cannot handle steel cut oats on the porridge setting.  This is confirmed on Zojirushi's website.  If you're looking for a rice cooker that can handle SCO, check out Tiger's JKT.  It's half the cost, has a dedicated SCO option (reviews indicate it makes great oats) and it makes excellent rice... among other things.  It also looks to be a lot more intuitive/easier to operate and you don't have to deal with a computer yelling at you in Korean.
