body: yes
style: I think this rice cooker is just okay. There's a lot of inconsistencies in the rice results...and if you eat a lot of Jasmin rice, I don't think it is the best cooker for that. It does very well for brown and GABA rice, and short grain. It doesn't do well for that special crunchy bottom rice, which is more chewy than crunchy, and I think not good for my teeth enamel. The pressure unit doesn't seem to work properly. It originally would be silent when cooking, until the pressure release, but now it just cooks with the release valve pretty much open on its own. The inside steel plate that's removable for cleaning has a super short silicone that makes it difficult remove without using a dry cloth for gripping. This same plate also falls into the rice while cooking pretty regularly, so I think that silicone gasket that secures it isn't right during cooking. I hate opening up my rice cooker to see this plate sitting directly on top of my rice. There's many little annoying features that just don't work. I also hate it when my rice turns out grey. It only does it sometimes, so I am not sure why. Maybe I don't wash the rice enough. But I have never had grey rice with any other cooker in my entire life of rice cooking. So I get worried about the chemicals that might be in my grey rice.I have had this cooker for over a month now, and compared to my old fuzzy logic Zojirushi rice cooker, I find the rice better with my old cooker. The good thing about the newer Cuckoo is the speed , and it cooks a good brown and GABA rice much better because of the high pressure. But we don't eat brown that often.I am contemplating on replacing this with a Zojirushi again, and saving this for when I need to make brown rice. Pretty disappointing overall. The Cuckoo does the two things better that my old cooker lacked, but I don't know if it was enough to sacrifice for quality, white (not grey) rice.

author: Eldon
title: Don’t go for it if you expected a high quality Japanese rice cooker, they are just not the same.
body:
Well, this is my first time to write any product review from my Amazon purchase.  The product earned 2 out of 5 stars across various categories, are pretty much to it failed to meet with my expectations.  I grow up in a traditional Asian family where rice cooker is one of the most important cooking tools in the kitchen.  I have to admit that my family and I are pretty “serious” on the type of rice we eat, as well as how the rice cooker could perform.  With a so-called “smart-rice cooker” at this price point, all I could say is that IT COULD NOT COOK THE RICE THAT I EXPECTED. No matter which programme I choose, or the amount of water I added, the rice was never soft enough. Compared to my TIGER brand $99 from Costco, this $360 Made in Korea rice cooker just can’t even make a decent porridge.  All I presume is the programme and the high pressure technology could have two advantages. One, quick that I could have my rice done in about 20 minutes. Two, the steam and high pressure is good with the grain rice.
Unfortunately, this pricy rice cooker (probably because it was invented and branded from Korean) didn’t have the receipt for the rice to sit enough time to absorb enough water.  In the due course, the rice is for those who like “harder”.
Last but least, when look into details, many plastic parts including the attached accessories are flimsy.  All I could say “don’t go for it if you expected to have a high quality Japanese rice cooker”, they are just not the same.

Additionally, I have tried cooking with different types of rice, such as jasmine rice, Basmati, and sweet rice. All the rice I have tested has turned out great with this rice cooker. One thing I’d like to mention is that I learned from another reviewer that the English manual did not provide clear instructions on how to set up the clock. I follow the Korean instructions instead, using Google Translate.

body: This is a high quality rice cooker. The material of each part is very sturdy. The actual item looks lighter than the picture. There is a learning curve on how to use it though. I couldn’t find from the instruction on how to change the time and how to do slow cook. I did some research online and talked to the product support team on Amazon and got my answer. So yes the volume, yes or no voice, texture, keep warm temperature, slow cooking/soup coking functions can all be set, but you need to go through quite a few steps to get there. Once you figured these out, it is a pleasant device to use. Plus, it was indeed very quiet and the non pressure coming mode dud not generate any steam out so it did not make my kitchen look like a sauna room. I also wish the device by default has a stainless steel inner pot instead of a separately sold one that I have to purchase from another website.

author: b
title: Excellent rice cooker with some short comings
body:
I use my rice cooker pretty much every day.  I eat a lot of rice, probably on average about 2 times a day so I'm always making fresh rice every 2 to 3 days.  I'm replacing a Cuckoo eco pressure rice cooker (CRP-P1009S) which has served me well for a few years but it was a 10 cup model and, for me, it was too big for one person so I was looking for something with a smaller capacity.

I knew I wanted another Cuckoo but this time with their induction heating technology.  I was going to get their other twin pressure IH cooker but I saw they had a newer model with their quiet pressure cooking technology so I decided to splurge and buy it since I use my rice cooker so often.

Well, I received the rice cooker and I call it the Robocop.  It's quite nice looking but I have some minor complains.  But before we get to the complaints, I have to say the quiet pressure cooking technology really works!  My old cuckoo was quite loud especially during the steam release.  The new one is very, very quiet.  You can still hear the steam release but it's night and day compared to the old model.

Also, it makes fantastic rice!  I make my own mix of rice which consists of brown rice, brown sweet rice, barley, and sweet black rice.  Compared to the old rice cooker, this new one makes the rice very soft, yet chewy, and sticky.  I use the high pressure multi-grain setting and the rice comes out perfect!  It's definitely better than the old cuckoo using the same rice mix.

The reason for the 4 star review is as follows:

1. Terrible manual.  No where does it tell you how to set the clock.  I finally figured it out but it would have been nice if that was mentioned.

2. The buttons are all touch sensitive and don't push in when you hit it so it's hard to tell if you're actually pushing the button since you're just hitting a hard surface with no give.  I liked the soft touch buttons of the old cooker where it would actually push in.

3. No more rice paddle holder on the side of the cooker.  I don't know why they got rid of that.  You spend this much money on a rice cooker and there's no place to store the paddle?

But, overall, at the end of the day it's all about the rice cooking ability and this cooker shines in that department.

10 cup cooker is bigger than I would like but quality for this price, hard to beat!!!

Lid doesn't fly up with force as the other units do when opened. Better visibility of controls and it comes with a rice paddle holder.
Now if they could include retractable cord and a lid that doesn't jump out at you ! Japanese models are better optioned in that regard.
I think it would elevate their user friendly critics. Japanese rice cookers seem more detailed in user functionality and ease of use!
For me it'sa 10 +++

Very happy with this item!!!!!!!
Highly recommend

author: R. Lin
title: Likely our First and last Cuckoo
body:
My wife and I was really excited about the new pressure rice cooker from Cuckoo and we've always used Zojirushi  or Tiger brand from Japan in the past because we are serious about our rice cookers.  But the price of Zojirushi are out of control so we gave Cuckoo a try. Cuckoo is supposed to a premium Korean brand but we were disappointed.

After receiving and opening the rice cooker, I was already disappointed by the lack of quality that you can just feel.  It feels lower quality than our 10 year old Instant Pot.  Then we started cooking, the top lid is not removable and it's simply not a good design because food sticks to it and makes it extremely difficult to clean.  And it took more than 2 hours to cook porridge, what's the point of a pressure cooker if cooking time is not reduced?  and the last straw is that the porridge is nothing special and didn't come out like what we would expect the pressure cooker to do.

This is going back for sure even though we don't like to abuse the return policy.

author: RCH
title: This is a great Rice Cooker for the money
body: I own two of the Zojirushi Commercial rice cookers but needed more production capability (cooked rice).  I was relooking my options (the Zo is more than $400 for the 20 cup commercial).  I found this Cuckoo model and did a bit of research.  The Cuckoo brand is Korean and is considered to be a top of the line cooker.Pluses:  Half the cost of the Zo Commercial cooker.  50% more production capacity than the Zo  (30 cup vs 20 cup) per cycle.I bought one of these and used it for about 10 days (we do a 50 pound bag of rice every morning).  Both Zo's plus the new Cuckoo helped.  After a week, I ordered a second of these Cuckoos.  (both of these together cost less than a third zo).I really now prefer the Cuckoos to the Zo's.  For us, the capacity of the Cuckoo is perfect (max volume before the lift from the pot becomes too heavy).  The fact that there is a third indicator light (shows cooking, steaming, and warming) rather that the two for the Zo (cook and warm) so you don't have to time your warming light to estimate steaming time.  When the Cuckoo leaves steam and goes to warm, the rice is ready.I can't speak to longevity yet because the short time I have owned them.  I can say they make perfect jasmine, basmati, and sushi style rice, and do it well.v/r rh

author: Kevin
title: Game-Changer for Rice Lovers!
body:
The CUCKOO CRP-RT0609FW has completely changed how I cook rice and meals. The twin-pressure feature gave me the ability to pick high or soft pressure depending on what I was making. It doesn't matter if it's fluffy white rice or hearty brown rice, it always comes out nice.

The 14 menu options are so convenient; I've made GABA rice, porridge and steamed vegetables. The nonstick inner pot is a huge help when it comes to clean-up, and the Auto Clean is an awesome feature that makes it easy to keep clean without extra effort.

I liked the Safe Steam Release safety feature, and the 3-language voice guide in English, Korean, and Chinese is pretty nifty and surprisingly helpful.

Overall, this rice cooker is sleek, smart, and affordable. It looks great on your counter and cooks like some high quality, restaurant-quality, worth-every-penny kind-of-machine each time. I would definitely recommend this to anybody that wants dependable, high-tech cooking that is easy and enjoyable!

title: [CRP-RT0609FW] Great cooker. This is how to change to English
body:
TL;DR: For CRP-RT0609FW only: Step 1: Press [TIME SETTING] for 3 seconds. Step 2: Press [ > ] once. Step 3: Press [HIGH P COOK]. I uploaded an image for clarity.

I seen other instructions saying you need to press [Auto Clean] for 3 seconds – that didn't work for me.
What did work was to press [Time cook] for 3 seconds, then I got a "0:0" on the screen and pressed [ > ] until hearing "This is English" and then press [High Pressure cooking] to confirm. I give this rice cooker 4 stars only because it's so complicated and they seem not care much about the language.

Therefore pressure cooking is not activated for use.  I have to bang on the machine several times then the machine would engage pressure mode and orange light turns on.  The pressure plate and temperature sensors are both clean and free of blockage its definately a mechincal issue. It works great if the orange light actually turn on so can use pressure mode. title: Cuckoo Convert
body: For years, I used my Instant Pot to cook rice - it did an OK job but cleaning the stainless insert was usually a bummer, especially when the rice stuck to the pot. I finally decided to try out a proper rice cooker and researched Cuckoo before buying this model. I am so happy with my purchase! I have been using it for about a month now and have zero complaints. It is easy to use, clean, and makes consistently delicious rice.My go-to is brown short grain (sushi) rice or Nishiki's Premium 7 Grains Mix - sometimes, I mix them together. I use the glutinous rice setting for the brown and mixed rice for multi-grain rice/multi-grain + brown combo.The water to rice ratios are pretty much fool-proof: However many Cuckoo-sized cups of rice, then fill to the comparable number water line on the insert (I don't make less than two cups at a time).I tried to give a better idea of size and scale compared to my standard toaster-oven in my pics. When not in use, I store it in a large cupboard over my fridge.The auto clean function is a nice feature - I use it after every preparation.This may be my favorite purchase of 2021 and I have only scratched the surface of what this powerhouse machine can do.

author: Jonathan
title: Just a basic reliable Korean rice cooker.
body:
First, these cook rice to the satisfaction of the Korean consumers, who prefer really plump, hard rice, unlike people who eat long grain rice or the Japanese consumers who prefer softer fluffy rice. Furthermore, Korean pressure rice cookers cook at a higher pressure and higher temperature than other pressure cookers such as Instant Pot. That's the reason most Korean households primarily use pressure rice cookers. On the other hand, pressure rice cookers are non-existent in Japan. So, if you prefer your medium grain or short grain rice cooked in Japanese style, this is not for you.

I bought this to replace one that is about 15 years old. The voice thingy has become very talkative. It used to only say what's necessary, but now it just keeps on talking. It's good that one can turn it off. The font/words for the buttons are very light, which makes them very difficult to see. Compared to 15 years ago, the options to tweak the cooking parameters is much easier, such as keep warm temperature, degree of browning on the bottom, change language and the volume and some other functions. I don't really see anyone would need to deviate from the default program, but if you want, there they are. Also, because of voice instructions, it's easy to personalize the rice cooker. Other than that, it's a Cuckoo rice cooker. Some complain that it's too big. Yes, it is little bigger than the Japanese brands. But one needs to remember that this is a pressure cooker, which means it gets hotter, so there should be more insulation material between the outer wall and the cooking pot. Also, the primary target market is Korea, where the rice cooker sits on the kitchen counter and is never put away. So, storage convenience was not really on their mind when the designed them. If you want a Korean rice cooker, Cuckoo is the one to get. Not only is it the best-selling brand in Korea, but consumable parts such as the pressure seal rings are easier to find.

author: Lee
title: Do not buy from GlobalEcom or Amazon warehouse. It is refurbished and not new!!!
body:
I bought this product because it was new, and no where in the description said that it was refurbished. NOWHERE. It was false description. It broke after two months, and Amazon refused to issue a refund and told me to contact Cuckoo directly. I found out from that from that specific agent who refused to issue me a refund that the product that I purchased was a refurbished one. He told me that I should have known that it was a refurbished product since it was being shipped from Amazon's warehouse and blamed it on me.

I called in again, and this time, the agent issued me a refund right away, and apologized.

Do not buy Cuckoo products from GlobalEcom or Amazon warehouse; they are used and refurbished. If you look at other Cuckoo rice cookers from GlobalEcom and Amazon warehouse, you'll see that customers are having the same problem as I did.

author: R. Becker
title: This Rice Cooker Makes Me Happy!
body: I bought the Cuckoo CRP-RT0609FB - 6 Cups, Twin Pressure Rice Cooker & Warmer specifically for brown rice.  The Cuckoo arrived, I used the instructions in the manual to quickly change the vocal prompts to English, put it through the self-clean cycle, loaded two cups of mixed brown and red rice, added water to the line marked two under GABA Rice, closed the lid, turned the knob to PRESSURE, the Cuckoo prompted me to choose a pre-set, so I chose GABA/PRESSURE.  40 minutes later, the Cuckoo announced the rice was finished cooking.  I opened the Cuckoo to find perfectly cooked brown/red rice.  The Cuckoo automatically went into KEEP WARM mode.  The first batch was just a test.  Over the next 48 hours, my wife and I sampled a little here and there until we'd eaten it all.  After 48 hours, if anything, the rice seemed even better than when first cooked.  Took the pot out of the Cuckoo and worried for a moment about how difficult it might be to clean after keeping rice warm for 48 hours.  I needn't have worried.  A splash of water and a quick sponge and the pot was perfectly clean.  The non-stick coating works really well.  I don't know how long one can hold rice in the KEEP WARM mode, but 48 hours was certainly not a problem.  Perfect brown/red rice in 40 minutes, 48 hours in KEEP WARM and it still tasted great and the pot was a breeze to clean.  I am extremely happy with my purchase!  I know this multi-cooker can do a whole bunch of other things and I'm looking forward to exploring, but to me, everything else is just a bonus.

author: Joyce G
title: high-quality
body:
The CUCKOO CRP-ST0609F is a high-quality rice cooker that combines the power of pressure cooking with the convenience of a warmer. With a 6-cup (uncooked) capacity, this rice cooker is perfect for smaller families or for those who want to cook rice quickly and easily.

One of the key features its twin pressure system. This system allows the rice cooker to cook rice quickly and efficiently, which is perfect for busy families who want to prepare meals quickly. Additionally, the cooker has a warming function that helps to keep the rice warm and fresh until it's time to serve.

The rice cooker also features a non-stick coating, which makes cleaning up a breeze. This is especially useful for busy families who don't have a lot of time to spend on cleaning up after meals.

Another great feature of the  CRP-ST0609F is its user-friendly interface. The digital display is easy to read and navigate, and the buttons are clearly labeled and easy to use. Additionally, the cooker comes with a variety of pre-set programs, making it easy to cook a variety of different types of rice, including white rice, brown rice, and more.

Overall, this rice cooker is a great choice for anyone who wants a high-quality rice cooker that is easy to use, efficient, and reliable. With its twin pressure system, non-stick coating, and user-friendly interface, this rice cooker is sure to be a hit with busy families who want to enjoy delicious, perfectly cooked rice with minimal effort.

author: Kris R.
title: Perfect Rice, Every Time
body:
This sleek white rice cooker has become a kitchen staple. The dual pressure cooking technology delivers consistently perfect rice every time, and the 6-cup capacity is ideal for families.
Performance: The pressure cooking function works beautifully—rice comes out fluffy and evenly cooked with minimal effort. I've tried multiple rice varieties (white, brown, jasmine, arborio) and it handles them all with impressive results. The cooking time is noticeably faster than traditional cookers, which is great on busy weeknights.
Design and style: The clean white finish looks modern and fits seamlessly into any kitchen décor. It's compact enough to sit on the counter without dominating space, yet the 6-cup capacity means I rarely need to cook twice for our family.
Features: Beyond rice, the dual pressure function gives you flexibility in cooking settings. The controls are intuitive, the keep-warm function is reliable, and cleanup is straightforward with the non-stick inner pot.
Durability: Build quality feels solid. It's been a dependable workhorse without any issues so far, and the stainless steel accents add to its longevity.
Worth considering: At this price point, you're investing in efficiency and consistency. If you cook rice regularly, the time and quality savings pay off quickly.
Bottom line: A reliable, attractive rice cooker that delivers professional results. Highly recommended for anyone serious about their rice game

author: Cozystrich
title: Tastes Just Like Home — Amazing Korean Rice Cooker Value
body:
This rice cooker is from one of the most trusted brands in Korea, and the performance lives up to its reputation. For this price, the value is outstanding — the rice comes out exactly like the bowls I used to enjoy back home: chewy, glossy, and perfectly cooked every time.

It’s a great fit for a 2–3 person household, and the compact design looks sleek on the counter. There are plenty of cooking modes available, but if you mainly plan to use it as a rice cooker, I recommend sticking to the rice modes. If you want to explore other functions, make sure to use the cleaning mode regularly — it helps a lot.

If you’re new to Korean-style rice cookers, take a moment to read the manual. It explains everything clearly, and you’ll avoid mistakes early on. Just remember: use a soft sponge for cleaning the inner pot, and never use a metal rice scoop.

For the best results, use the correct water level and mode for the type of rice.
For reference, I usually cook 2 cups of white rice and 1 cup of brown rice, fill the water up to the “Mixed Rice 3” line, and use the high-pressure “Mixed Rice (Normal)” mode. It never sticks and comes out great every time. (See photos and videos for reference.)

And one more tip: regularly taking apart the removable parts and giving the cooker a thorough cleaning also makes a noticeable difference in the taste of the rice.

Overall, I’m extremely satisfied. As expected — Cuckoo never disappoints.

title: Powerful Suction! Blew My Mind!
body: First off I just want to say that this vacuum is astoundingly quiet. I have never owned a vacuum this quiet. You could have a regular volume conversation or watch TV while this vacuum is running and have no issues. It is lightweight too. Like obviously it‚Äôs not as light as a feather and my arm did get tired holding it after a while, but it wasn‚Äôt excessive and just switching hands back and forth made it not an issue. I consider myself to be pretty weak in the arms and I didn‚Äôt have much trouble. If you are EXTREMELY weak, elderly, disabled, or a literal child, you may have some issues. The average adult should not find this vacuum too heavy, though.Now for the part that blew my mind! After ordering this vacuum but before it arrived, I did a very thorough vacuum of my whole house with my old vacuum. I brushed stuff out from the walls, I got in all the crevices, under everything, made multiple passes. I considered it one last hurrah for my old vacuum, to really get some work in so that the new vacuum wouldn‚Äôt start it‚Äôs first day getting beat up with a deep clean. Well, when I got this new Cuckoo vacuum out, put it together, and started vacuuming, I immediately heard the distinctive clinking of stuff getting sucked up. ‚ÄúOh man‚Äù I thought, ‚ÄúThis vacuum is great. I just spent the weekend vacuuming the crap out of these carpets and this new vacuum is managing to pull more out.‚Äù I just quickly ran through the hallway and two bedrooms to see what it could do. I didn‚Äôt even get in all the corners, just ran it through the heavy traffic open areas. Literally about five minutes of vacuuming and this thing pulled out a wad of hair the size of a baseball and about 3/4 cup of pure dirt. My jaw absolutely dropped. ‚ÄúI just cleaned these carpets a few days ago!‚Äù I thought. ‚ÄúNo, you just cleaned them NOW. They were obviously still filthy before‚Äù I replied to myself.Needless to say I am thoroughly impressed, satisfied, obsessed, and living for this vacuum. It was so simple to put together, to use, and the instructions are straightforward enough that I believe it will be simple to maintain as well. Everything feels extremely high quality, snaps together with confidence, and works amazing. Also the lights on the front are so freaking bright you will be blinding all the dust bunnies under your couch. My ONE COMPLAINT is that you have to plug the vacuum into the dock to charge. You cannot charge just the battery (well, you can technically, by plugging the battery into the base of the dock‚Ä¶)Anyways I highly recommend this vacuum, I firmly believe it is worth the price for the quality and versatility. WAY better than my old vacuum and also way better than the corded push vacuum my mom bought just last year for about $80 less. Once again I am obsessed.

body:

It has a place to put a spare battery that will also charge automatically, but I don't see anywhere to buy one (not even on their website). I'm hoping those are coming later.

author: Shelley.1709
title: Powerful and lightweight!
body:
This vacuum is the best of both worlds: powerful enough to get a lot of dirt up, and lightweight enough that its easy to operate.  Rounding out the positives of this vacuum are the fact that it's versatile with the included attachments, it's quiet and not loud enough to scare my dogs, and I can quickly and easily go from carpet to hardwood.

I admit I had my doubts on how well this would work just based on it's size, weight, and my previous experience with "dust buster" rechargeable hand vacs, but this far exceeded my expectations!  I don't have to drag out a heavy vacuum, only to wrestle with the cord while using and change the settings by stopping and having to bend down to switch the setting on the base.  This one is literally one touch on, off, and to change the settings.

The auto sense thing is pretty amazing too!  I have a combination of hard wood, throw rugs, and regular carpeting in my house.  I can easily and quickly go from one surface to another.  It has not scratched my wood floors, which I was nervous about, and it helps me sweep up anything that gets tracked in.

The base is easily fitting in a corner of my kitchen and the ability to pop it off the base for sweeping and pop it back on the base for charging makes things so much easier.  No more dragging the big vacuum out of the closet.

The attachments fit easily and work well for different messes.  I have two dogs and two grandchildren and this is working well for quick clean ups.

title: not good
body:
I didn’t expect that in 2025 this electric water boiler would still be inferior to Zojirushi. I bought it because its minimum keep-warm temperature can go as low as 104°F, whereas Zojirushi’s lowest setting is 160°F.

Drawbacks:
• The boiling process is extremely noisy, and even after the water reaches a boil, it continues heating and makes strange noises.
• When the water temperature drops, there is no flashing indicator to show that the temperature is still above the preset level.
• Each time you have to manually switch the boiler mode after refilling.

Also it doesn't have any memorization and I have to reset temperature everytime I unpluged and replugged it (I do need to refuel the tank from time to time, right)? After used it for 2 weeks, I switched to installed insinkerator hot &cold dispenser instead, which is so so much better.

author: phil
title: Simplicity king
body:
Our 10 years old Zojirushi water boiler went bad, and we found that the price went almost twice as much as what we paid before with no upgrade. So we decided to give CUCKOO a try. And this hot water dispenser from CUCKOO meets almost all aspects of our daily needs.

This thing is huge, which can boil up to 4 liter water at a time.

It has sight glass that you can see the level easy, and the whole interior of the water boiler is one piece with stainless steel material.

And to start the boiling process, you will need to press "On/Off" -> "Boil". It cannot automatically keep warm after boiling. To keep the water at certain warm level, you will need to set it separately on top of boiling, which is a little bit annoying since we often tend to forget.

Also to dispense water, you need to press "On/OFF" -> "Unlock" -> "Dispense", which is a little tedious.

One major difference comparing to Zojirushi is the way you attach the cord. Zojirushi has this magnetic attaching cord, while CUCKOO is the traditional three prone plug requiring a little bit force to push in. This could be a little hazardous since you have a whole tank of water in the pot.

But overall, for the price, and the simple functionality, this is a good value.

author: Random Reviewer
title: Nice hot water dispenser with a few design flaws.
body:
There are several features I like about this hot water dispenser and several features I wish were different.

Things I like:

1. I found the device easy to use and set up and use directly out of the box and only referred to the manual to review the set-up requirements and how to clean the device.
2. Lock/Unlock feature.
3. Dispenser feature.
4. Keep warm setting.
5. Auto turn off after boiling if a keep warm option has not been chosen.
6. Touch button panel.

Things I wish were different:

1. The lid is not removable and the hinge feels flimsy allowing the lid to shift slightly left to right. I worry that it will fail with continued use.
2. I don't like the location of the lid release handle. It's directly over the reservoir so if you need to open the lid while the water is hot there is no way to avoid the steam so you need to wear an oven mitt.
3. I don't like the location of the plug. This is a pretty large appliance and it's going to take up a substantial amount of counter space. Putting the plug in the back center causes this dispenser to sit several inches forward from the wall or to be placed in a corner to compensate for this.
4. Length of time to boil even smaller quantities. I didn't notice much of a difference in time between bringing a full reservoir vs a half reservoir to a boil.
5. See through the reservoir panel. I wish it was larger because I find it to be dark and hard to read. I have to put my phone flashlight on to see it.

I'm not sure if this hot water dispenser is as good or exceeds other brands but I do think it performs well enough to be considered when shopping for one. There are some flaws but they do not impact this dispenser's performance.

author: green_earth
title: Large reservoir, lots of possibilities
body:
My summary: this product is beautifully put together and a very attractive addition to any kitchen, produces hot water in abundance, seems to be super easy to clean or keep clean, and as you consider your individual needs this may be a great value for your kitchen or serving area.

We have been using this now for several weeks. It gets used for hot drinks, instant breakfast cereals and so forth.

Learning to use it as a bin a little bit of a challenge and the process of dispensing and understanding what's happening is a little problematic only in that it's not as straightforward as you might expect. My youngest child is 12 years old, and everybody has gotten used to how it works without complaint - but it did take a fair bit of learning to get everybody up to speed on what to expect. To clarify that point, as it sits it will lock and it's not the type of thing you simply walk up and push the dispense button and expect it to work. You have to push and hold the unlock button first then push dispense and there's usually about a one to two second delay before water comes. This delay ended up in hot water being spilled on our floor, countertop, and table multiple times as people thought something was wrong. Everybody's accustomed to it now and knows what to do - but just a comment to assist those who first begin to use it. Also, if you said it to keep the hot water at a certain temperature it will assume you are in charge of how long it will maintain that temperature. It will stay on for as many days or hours as you leave it on. There is no timer function that I can find. In fact, that's the one thing I wish they would have included is a maximum time for keeping the water warm because it's easy to forget.

author: Stephanie
title: Need better directions
body:
I like this water dispenser, and yet I didn’t start out liking it.

First off, it just says open the lid. It didn’t say how to open the lid. I didn’t know if it opened from the back or from the front. After messing with it for about five minutes, and even had my husband take a look, I figured out that you have to press the vent cover and then lift up and the lid will open. I got very frustrated with this. Just post a picture or write how to open it.

Next, I was wondering if the lid is detachable for cleaning. I guess it’s not. No instructions about that either.

When I boiled the water, I had to keep hitting the unlock button and it was very finicky and didn’t want to disperse the water. I figured it out.

Glad it stays locked. That’s a plus.

It takes about 20 minutes for the water to heat up. Might be quicker to just use my teapot. However, I like the fact that the water after bringing to a boil will remain hot, so no more boiling water on the stove.

It holds a good amount of water, so that’s one more plus for this unit.

This is a very large appliance so be sure you have enough room on your counter if you want to use it daily.

After all of the hassle, I’m enjoying my new hot water dispenser.

Not sure if I would recommend this particular model. I wish the lid was detachable so it would be easier to clean.

author: Christie M.
title: Not as convenient as I hoped.
body: I use a lot of hot water throughout the day, mainly for tea but I also occasionally drink instant coffee and make broth for recipes. I was looking forward to having hot water at my fingertips throughout the day with this dispenser, but it hasn't been the convenience that I've hoped for. The dispenser holds five liters which is a lot and it takes a very, very long time to come to a boil. Even when I fill it less than half way the boiling time is much longer than any electric kettle I've ever owned. The keep warm feature is nice, but I like my water boiling so I still have to re-boil it when I come back. The machine also doesn't empty all of the water when dispensing, no matter how much I run it I still have to flip the machine over to get all of the water out of the bottom. I'm sure this is useful for some people, but I personally wouldn't buy it again.

The ability to set various temperatures is a bonus, catering to different beverage needs. I'm genuinely thrilled with its performance and versatility.

author: Brittany R.
title: Great Safety Features
body:
Overall, I'm really happy with this hot water dispenser. The instructions recommend that you fill it with 5 liters of water, boil it twice, and then dump it before using it the first time. This isn't necessarily a fast boiler. It took about 20 min to boil 5 liters. I like the steam vent on the top that's set near the back of the lid (less risk for a small child reaching up and getting burned by the steam. It's also much quieter than my electric kettle. Once the water is ready, you have to push the unlock button (it lights up when it's unlocked) before you can dispense the water. I really appreciate this safety feature since the water is so hot and could burn an unsuspecting child that is just pushing random buttons.  You have to hold the dispense button down the entire time you want it to dispense. Again, a great safety feature. If you are not wanting boiling water, the machine has several temperature options. If you press the keep warm/setting button, it allows you to select what temperature you would like it to warm to and then hold. It can hold a temperature for up to 48 hours.
Overall, it's an amazing product and I'd highly recommend it.

author: MM
title: Love this even more than I thought I would
body:
I drink a LOT of tea, and hot water means I have to boil a lot of it. I have a fabulous kettle that has been doing very well, but however silly, the sound of the water heating and reheating really bothers me while I'm on my zoom calls. So, I was curious how this unit would be, with the ease of having hot water at any moment, without having to wait for the kettle to boil.

The unit comes in its own box and is well packaged with foam. It is a bit over a foot high, so it's a decent size, and holds 5 liters of water. It's suggested in the accompanying leaflet (yes I actually read those!) to fill the unit up with water (to the fill line) and let it boil twice, and then discard that water, I assume to boil off any manufacturing residue. I did this, but found I needed to do another big fill / boil off, to get the water to taste clean.

But once that is done, it works amazingly well! I was a bit concerned that the water would not be hot enough for my tea, but it's great! And I love the ease of just walking to the dispenser, push the "unlock" button and then the "dispense" one, and get HOT water instantly. (be aware that the water is indeed hot. Initially I had my cup a bit too low, which means that some drops spilled on my hand and that was a bit painful. Simply raising my cup to closer below the spout stopped this from happening)

If I have to find one fault, it's that the lid, when opened, can be wiggled a little from side to side on the hinge. It does seem sturdy enough for normal, regular use.

I am happy with this dispenser!

author: MacGuffin
title: Great Little Cooker
body:
I'm a fan of Cuckoo products and own a multi cooker and 10-cup rice cooker that's the "papa bear" equivalent of this "baby bear." This twin pressure induction cooker is Cuckoo's top-of-the-line three-cup model and it's a gem.

Like my other Cuckoo products, this is a high-quality appliance. The inner pot is very heavy and has a premium, and very attractive non-stick surface. What's nice is that the various types of rice can either be cooked under pressure or steamed, depending on how you like your rice. You can also cook it super-fast with the turbo setting, in addition to other settings for things like baby food and stored (i.e. frozen) rice.

GABA is the setting for plain, pre-germinated, or cooker-germinated brown rice. It's necessary, if the latter is your choice, to choose the 3-hour setting; the other two settings are pretty much press-and-play. The cycle takes quite a while from start to finish--just shy of four hours. However, it's a much less fussy way of germinating rice than worrying about pre-soaking, and the nutritional values are pretty much the same either way. If you come home for lunch, you can start your GABA rice before you return to work and it'll be ready for dinner. Even if you opt not to use the four-hour cycle, your rice will stay warm until you return, courtesy of the "stay warm" setting that kicks in automatically when cooking is completed.

I wish this unit had a "scorched" setting and, unfortunately, the cooked cereal settings are gone as well. It's tiny and, I suppose, can only accommodate so many functions but cooked cereals would've been great for a single person. I also wish its steam plate was like that of its "papa's," i.e. with a push button instead of having to pull it off (like my multi cooker's). It's also something of a pain to place its "packing," i.e. sealing ring, after you've cleaned it. I discovered that the best way is to place it completely as best you can before attempting to secure it. Make sure to align its tabs with the cover's holes.

The instruction booklet is rather opaque--you can tell that whoever translated it from Korean wasn't completely comfortable with English. Supplemental literature that explains the various functions, along with some recipe suggestions, wouldn't have come amiss, especially at this cooker's price point. We can only hope that someone at Cuckoo actually reads these reviews.

All in all, I'm extremely pleased with this little guy. I have a large house but a very small kitchen and this saves me from having to pull out the multi cooker if I'm just preparing rice (the 10-cup is only for guests or unless I'm really jonesing for scorched rice). I picked it up on sale, plus there was a $10 coupon. If you need a rice cooker that's less capacious than six cups, this is the one to get.

author: Simon
title: Defective pressure cooking function
body:
This product is defective.  For a price tag of $656, it only works for cooking rice.  The reason we bought this is also for its pressure-cooking function.  When it worked (only a couple of times since we bought it), food come out pretty good, of course not as good as the true pressure cooker on the market.  However, after using the pressure-cooking function for about a couple times, it started to leak steams the top part.  We didn't know that it was actually leaking as we thought it's just normal pressure release.  But most of the meat recipe that we cooked with pressure cooking function, all of them turned out uncooked for the meat.  For whole grain, they come out to be under cooked, extremely dry, and sometime burnt due to leaking steam.

Apparently, this is a very common problem for this cooker.  There are quite a bit of complaints about such problem and there are many Youtube clips showing how to fix them.  But it requires taking the cooker apart.  With a new cooker, if we were to take it apart would void the warrantee.  However, we have reached out to Cuckoo for support.  They only response once asking about where it was purchased.  After presenting the order information from Amazon, they went dead silent, and it's been months now.

To the potential buyers, beware, when you make this expensive decision to purchase this product.  It's defective and support is virtually nonexistent.  Hope you have better luck if you decide to purchase one.

To Cuckoo, I hope you are reading this.  Please make better product as your price point is very high.  Have some decency to support your customers as you are leaving them a bad product and experience.

author: Pamela
title: Good while it worked
body:
I purchased 2 of these rice cookers, 1 for my mother and 1 for my family. The device worked well while it worked. We only ever used it for rice and it did a good job at cooking rice. It is much heavier and bigger than our previous rice cookers. Unfortunately, both our devices lasted almost 2 years before they started failed.

For my mother's, the inner pot where you cook the rice started to peel. The peeling got so bad it was unusable. This started happening after the warranty, 1 year. The solution - to buy a new inner pot for $89.99 on the Cuckoo site.

For my device, the 'ECO' message appeared and the device stopped working. This happened earlier this week after the warranty period. I contacted Cuckoo and they advised that I could send it to their California location to be fixed but I am responsible for shipping and repair costs. I looked up how much it would cost me to ship the device and the cheapest was UPS Ground for about $65. They gave me an estimate that it would be $30 shipping + $40 repair. The total would be $135.00.

For such an expensive device, it should have lasted longer. I'm not sure if I will repair it or buy another from this brand. In the past my family had Zojirushi rice cookers and they lasted longer than 2 years. In fact, I pulled out my old one to use when the Cuckoo stopped working.

This is a nice device and it worked well when it worked. If you don't mind buying a new one every few years and the price is not an issue then consider this rice cooker. If you'd like something that lasts longer, is priced less, and don't want to have a purchase a new one every few years, then it would be better to consider another rice cooker.

author: MH
title: Bad Build Quality: Fit and Finish Raise Questions about Durability
body:
This Cuckoo rice cooker does not feel like a $500 rice cooker. There's something about all of the mechanical parts that just feels like it's going to break at any moment. From the front panel, to the lid release button, to the way the lid swings open and clangs the bowl -- it's all very cheap feeling. Even my Instant Pot feels better quality. The Cuckoo looks nice, but once you touch it, it's plasticy and unrefined, and just doesn't match what I expected from this price range. In my Asian American household, where rice is made almost every day, there is no way I could trust this to be my kitchen workhorse and stand up to years of use. Sorry Cuckoo -- I was hoping your cool designs would be paired with higher build quality.

It's back to the Japanese brands for us. I've used a Zojirushi IH for 10+ years that still works great, even if it's getting a little dinged up. My mom's Zojirushi is probably pushing 20 years. Everything about Zojirushi rice cookers feels much higher quality than this Cuckoo. The Zoji's aesthetics are not great, but at least I can trust it will do its job for years to come.

author: Jing W.
title: Not Crazy for Cuckoo
body:
The menu is ATROCIOUS.  absolutely ridiculous.  Spent 30 min just trying to figure out what the hell they are trying to communicate.  The pot: they inexplicably cram all this info into one spot.  It looks straightforward enough but they inexplicably have arrows pointing down on either side of the column like these numbers relate to one another?  They had all the space in the world to make a clear,  coherent, intuitive guide but they wanted to make a puzzle.  At this point my kids driving my crazy bike it took so long and so i decide i'm just going to run it and find out.  But then I get to the front interface.  No tactile buttons,  I'm cycling thru the same 5 options, none of which I want (and there's no 'white rice' button either (it's called non p cook).  Its talking to me but it's all in Korean etc.  I'm sure this stuff is in the instructions but using a rice cooker to make white rice - it should be very intuitive and simple. If you don't get that right,  what are you even doing?  I used to push a button down and that was it.

This rice was fine.  Nothing special.  I did no-pressure white (Nishiki brand).  But I'll keep trying and seeing if the price is justified.

BTW, the picture is a head on shot that hides it's size.  It's massive - way too big for anyone's counter - i don't care how big your kitchen is.

Ah, and the auto cleaning feature is fine but be aware,  it does not save you any time.  You still have to clean it manually.  The auto feature just steams the parts you can't reach.  Technically it's *more* work.

body: I wasn't sure what to expect from a rice cooker that cost this much, but whatever my expectations were they have been exceeded. This is a really great kitchen appliance. It feels very well built and premium and the included manual is very well done. The rice it produces is clearly superior to my (perfectly fine) previous cooker, I would have 0 issues distinguishing them in a blind taste test. For mixed wild rice the results were delicious - every grain cooked to perfection. I probably will only ever use a small fraction of the features of this machine but as long as it keeps working I will be happy with it.

title: AVOID THIS ONE
body: DO NOT BUY THIS ONE. I'm a lifelong Cuckoo user and this one is by far the worst. All the features are there and it's works well for the most part. However, if you fail to clean it regularly and it forms bacteria in parts of the machine you cannot clean with the auto-clean function or by hand (without taking it apart), you are SOL. It makes no sense that this rice cooker has crevices or parts that is unreachable/inaccessible by hand. None of the other Cuckoo rice cookers I've used in the past 30 years have had this issue. No matter how many cycles of vinegar or baking soda water to clean the machine completely kills the bacteria and the odor it creates is absolutely disgusting. Please look for other models or Cuchen rice cookers without this issue.

author: BuTeK
title: Arrived broken. Nice cooker, but for this price i expect it to work.
body:
Unfortunately, mine arrived malfunctioning in a subtle way. When cooking under pressure, it simply fails to pressurize, so I have to give it 1 star.

It seems like the little electrical solenoid that controls the pressure valve is miscalibrated relative to the valve’s weight. When I added a small weight to the top of the bucket, it finally pressurized as expected.

In the video, you can see my unit attempt to pressure-cook, this abdurdity continues for about 10 minutes, and the rice came out uncooked. Tried a few other settings with similar results.

Otherwise, I actually love the results. The bowl is heavy-duty and comfortable to use, and induction heating is extremely fast. I can steam buns in about 10 minutes, straight from the fridge to the plate.

Without the malfunction, this would probably be a 4-star review, with a few nitpicks based on my current Japanese fuzzy-logic cooker:

1. The control buttons aren’t great, especially the “stupid” ring in the center. It gives the impression of being a knob, but it’s really just three sluggish buttons. Switching to the right cooking preset takes more effort than it should.

2. It’s missing several conveniences that Zojirushi includes by default: no handle, no easy detachable cable, and no place to store the spatula.

title: Meh
body:
I got this because I didn’t want to spend more on a Zojirushi and this one has a 14 min turbo rice cooking function, since it is induction and pressure cooking. I knew that cycle wouldn’t be the best but jeez, the rice was hard as a rock.  I then just ran a  regular cycle and the rice came out a lot better but I still found it to be on the stickier side. Which I don’t mind, but then I did multigrain rice. Waited an hour and it was the same thing. Still very dense and within minutes of eating it was hard.

I like different rices. Sometimes basmati sometimes multigrain sometimes jasmine, and sometimes rice a roni preseasoned rice packets. I don’t think this devices aim is to do that. It seems like it only is aimed at sticky or short grain.

The pressure function seemed like I would cut cooking times in half with the same quality,  but sadly it didn’t.

The unit is pretty big,  no handle makes it hard to move around. And the controls are complicated- some buttons are touch, but not the most popular ones I would think. Personally  I don’t find it worth the price tag. I’d rather spend a little more and get the zojurishi

author: Beth A
title: Perfect rice, but read this before you buy this rice cooker
body:
REVIEW OF 6-CUP MODEL
I'm very glad that I decided to replace the malfunctioning 3-cup with this model instead of another of the same size and capabilities.  We primarily eat brown rice, and with this we have many choices in how we want it cooked (in contrast to the top of the line Zojirushi this replaces, which had a single brown rice setting, and a GABA setting).  Cuckoo categorizes brown rice with other non-white rices together under Multi Grain settings, and I can choose GABA, Multi Grain Rice, Savory Multi Grain Rice, Turbo Multi Grain Rice, and can choose to "scorch" (toast) the bottom of any of those preparations; plus there are Sticky Multi Grain Rice, and High Heat Sticky Multi Grain Rice modes; giving me ten options for my brown rice instead of two.  So far, our experience has been that each of those options which we've tried has cooked rice which is superior in taste and texture to any other brown rice we have eaten.

Another thing I prefer about this rice cooker to the Zojirushi is that rice has always been ready to eat by the completion time which has been set, whereas we learned that we had to set the Zoj to an earlier time, or we could be waiting as much as ¾ hour for our rice to be ready.  Yes, I learned how to compensate for this peculiarity of our really good rice cooker, but why should you have to remember how much earlier to set it for this or that function.

That said, I have found this rice cooker has a definite learning curve.  Some of the terminology in the manual and the button labelling, and the sequences of setting this machine are not obvious to the Western mind.  Just as an example, the term "Preset" is used instead of "Timer" and rather than saying that the timer has been set to whatever time was chosen, it tells you "Preset has been reserved."  If, despite its ability to give you that degree of control over how your rice is cooked, you're not willing to put up with a certain amount of frustration initially, as you set this rice cooker with the manual in hand, it's probably not the right one for you.  I tend to be somewhat impatient, but don't admit defeat easily, and persisted.

REVIEW OF 3-CUP MODEL
It's a tribute to how incredibly well this cooked rice on the settings which worked for me that even though I have sent it back because I could not access the setting I primarily want to use (GABA) that I'm giving this four stars, and asked to have it replaced.  As an example, I have never had brown rice which had this depth of flavour nuance – it's absolutely outstanding.

1.  Before you buy this, know that the control panel is difficult to navigate, particularly so because the English section of the product manual appears to have been literally translated from Korean by someone without a good working knowledge of English.  It's possible to figure out what is meant if you ask yourself what other words that word which is incomprehensible in context could be a synonym for, but it's a bit frustrating when you're just trying to get your rice on so you can get on with your day or with getting a meal on the table.

2.  Beware that if you're buying a 3-cup, it is listed as having one less setting than the 6- and 10-cup models, but nowhere do they tell you what it is which it doesn't have.  I *think* I've figured out that it's scorched brown or GABA rice, but it could be its not being ready for easy dumpling cooking by having a steam plate, or it could be cakes, or perhaps an easily identified way to cook our oatmeal…  I don't really know.  I do know, however, that I came to my senses before the 3-cup replacement arrived, and decided to get the full featured 6-cup model, despite its much larger outside dimensions.

I should say that this is not a problem which is peculiar to Cuckoo.  I have encountered it before when I got a 3qt Instant Pot Ultra, which also didn't have the feature I most wanted, although the product description did not indicate it was missing.  I don't know why they don't tell the consumer which settings are or are not available on smaller models, or even they feel the need to do this, considering chips and circuitboards have gotten so small, but I've now gotten the message that it's an issue and am swearing off getting smaller models of home appliances.

If you wish to avoid either or both of these problems, I strongly suggest that you go to the Cuckoo site <cuckooamerica.com>, download the manual(s), and ask yourself just how well you'll cope with the technology, and how important it is to have stellar rice.

As for myself, I didn't give up on Cuckoo.  We eat rice almost every day, and like to use different varieties and preparations.  So I've ordered the 6-cup, and accepting my bread machine needs to be moved to create enough space (this is bigger than the 6-cup top of the line Zojirushi).  As great as the Zojirushi is, the rice cooked in this top of the line Cuckoo is incomparable, so it's worth it to me to figure it all out.

Thank you for reading my review.  I hope you found it helpful.

body: This is the best rice cooker that I have ever owned and I have owned many over my lifetime.  I actually ended up purchasing one that showed that it was open box to save a few bucks, but when I received it, it was basically a brand new product.  The capacity of the pot is great and we almost never need to make a full pot of rice unless we're entertaining, but it's nice to know that we have the capacity if we need it.  We haven't really had the opportunity to use all the different functions that are available on this machine, but as far as its ability to make a lovely pot of regular steamed rice is superb.  It's easy to maintain and clean the different components after a use and as long as it lasts the test of time, this will end up being a fantastic purchase.
